For anyone who has played DS1 but not DS2 yet, here's my take on the major differences between them.
Positives (improvements in DS2):
+The mechanics have been improved since DS1. Hollowing has a more significant impact in DS2 - temporarily losing a percentage of your max HP until you use an item to reverse the hollowing (not the humanity stat - which has been removed); dual-wielding has become much more viable in the form of a new system called the power stance; the old curse status has been effectively replaced by the less-severe petrify status, and a new status called curse - which is relatively minor in its effect, but much more common than DS1's curse - has been introduced.
+There are more weapon types in DS2 than in DS1 - including a few new classes of weapons, such as twinblades - and a new branch of spellcasting has been added (hexes - the damage adjustment of which is based on whichever is lower - Intelligence or Faith). Unfortunately, a few of my old PvE favorites (e.g. manserpent greatsword, demon's greataxe) have been removed.
+Pyromancy damage is now dependent (to a moderate degree) on Intelligence and Faith, so it's no longer the near-build-independent ability that it was in DS1.
+Stats have been reworked, and there are no longer any stats that you'll probably never invest in. (Hello, Resistance from DS1.)
+DS2's NPCs' characters, and sometimes backstories, are more "filled out" than those in DS1. The voice acting is also a bit better. (There are a few characters to whom you actually develop some attachment.)
+Fast travel is available between all bonfires that you've visisted starting at the beginning of the game. I'm a bit conflicted about this. Walking everywhere before I had the Lordvessel let me take in the environments in DS1, but eventually I hated having to walk back and forth between distant areas more than a few times. DS2's world is a bit bigger than DS1's, so the fast travel becomes a bit more important; as a result, I'll call this a positive.
+Matching with other players (for assistance or PvP) in NG has changed and is now based on total souls used; this is to prevent low-level but heavily-equipped players from destroying people who are equipped with level-appropriate gear. In NG+, this system gets deactivated.
Negatives (of DS2 relative to DS1):
-DS2 is somewhat less difficult than DS1. For those who dropped DS1 because it was too difficult, this will be a good thing; for those who relished the more difficult sections of DS1 and the sense of victory after completing them, don't expect that feeling to be quite as strong or to manifest itself quite as often. I consider this a net negative since most people familiar enough with DS1 to use it as a frame of reference probably mostly fall into the latter category.
-DS1 bosses are, overall, more interesting. Many of the DS2 bosses are large humanoids - though only a few are as simple as fighting a more-difficult regular enemy. There are few bosses on the creative level of, say, the Gaping Dragon, the Centipede Demon, or Smough & Ornstein.
-Pure Dexterity builds are not particularly viable in DS2. Quality builds (mixed Str/Dex) are still viable - now also because they tend to be effective builds for focusing on power stancing.
-Enemies will only respawn (after killing them, then resting at a bonfire) ~10-15 times. After that, if you want to farm those same enemies, you have to use an item which will effectively put the region associated with that bonfire into NG+ difficulty. (When you go into actual NG+, any regions where you have used that item will be increased again in enemy difficulty, e.g. to NG++.) This can be repeated multiple times at each bonfire during the same playthrough. If you're farming rare-drop items, this can get particularly annoying. (On the upside, many treasures respawn by going through this process, so it becomes pretty easy to farm rare matierals this way.)
-DS2's environment is prettier than DS1's, but it's also less bleak and dreary. Part of why it feels this way is probably because the human population of Drangleic (DS2's kingdom) is higher - and less likely to go hollow mid-game - than the population of Lordran. Regardless of the reason, you never get quite the same feeling of dread in DS2 as when you enter Blighttown for the first time or when you enter Sen's Fortress for the umpteenth time.
Overall, I recommend DS2 to Souls series veterans as well as new players. For the experienced, there's plenty of fun to be had in DS2, even if there aren't as many moments of temporarily overwhelming difficulty followed by an extreme sense of accomplishment as there were in DS1. For new players who aren't quite as enamored of the difficulty level that the Souls series seems to embrace, DS2 may be the best entry point for the series.

Definition of a golden oldie - Homeworld Remastered.

Speaking as someone who has never seen any of the movies or played other games in the alien franchise, this game was really good. This game is a very well done survival horror game that has a good art design and game mechanics that feel very fitting and real. From what I understand this isn't some regular movie licenced game being that its not something that is there because of the movies. This game stand on its own and is a very good survival horror game even to me who has never had any prior experience to the aliens franchise.

Pros
-------
+ Dark and terrifying atmosphere
+ Really good alien animations and detail
+ Sneaking around and hiding is intense
+ Smart alien AI
+ The sound design is up to par
+ Long campaign mode
+ Good amount of useful gear and items to craft
+ Survivor game mode can offer good amounts of replay value (if you have the DLC)
+ Wonderful visuals
Cons
-------
- Droid AI can be easily outsmarted and outmaneuvered
- Choppy cut scenes
- Some bad glitches and bugs, nothing gamebreaking so far though
- The Survivor game mode only comes with one map without the DLC
Overall impressions so far have been very good, a terrifying experience that I recommend to any true fan of the  horror/survival genre and the alien series, I believe Sega have truly revived themselves with this one and thier past mistakes can be easliy forgiven thanks to this.

Even 1,5 years after it's release this game remains one of the more impressive survival horror of late. It doesn't pick up its pace for a couple of hours into the story, but it never slacks on creating an atmosphere and immersing you into its world. It is an incredible journey, sometimes challenging, but always rewarding in the end.
The game is not perfect, I remember having a few gripes with the way the game handled its first enemy encounters, being unable to pick up enemy weapons, or me blaming an Alien AI for being too smart and all-seeing, but later I could see the reasoning behind these decisions. And those problems went away pretty fast.
The game runs great and looks like original motion picture. I didn't encounter any bugs or crashes.
Looking back I'm not thinking about the jumpscares, or those tense moments of fleeing away or hiding from the Alien. It is this cozy, comfortable feeling, that you earned during all those hours in the game. Lurking in the shadows, outsmarting your enemies. Skills that you didn't unlcok with xp grinding, but those that you learned yourself. And I just wish I could visit the Sevastopol Station for the first time, again. And that is a sign of a great game.

(Warning, minor spoilers at the end of the review)
This game was awesome to play. Controller or Keyboard, they both play really well. This game will make you paranoid and lockers will become your new home. Get used to it buddy, its either that Alien is gonna shove that tail up your ♥♥♥♥♥♥ or you spend the night in a cramped locker, your choice.
So, this game isn't all about locker hopping. If you're brave enough, you'll try your best to sneak past what maybe the best AI design for an horror enemy ever. The Alien will move around in the vents and can hear your tracking device beep. You can also travel around in the vents as well. The Alien is known to crawl through the vents with you and kill you in there but I never had that happen to me but it still can happen to you.
Speaking of sound, the sound design is masterful and immersive. When you're walking down a hallway you can hear the Alien moving around in the vents, his growl is subtle but terrifyingly believable. Voice acting is amazing. The actors are engaged and show emotion in their voices. Especially the lead role, Amanda, daughter of Ellen Ripley, who was in the original films, her voice actor couldn't of done better.
The facial animations and 3D models were so realistic. The Enemy design and the art in general represents the movie down to the cracks in the wall, its so good. Its like they were in the set for the movies to design this game. Its so bazaar being in the ship you saw get over taken by Aliens. Even in the DLC you can experience that for yourself as you can play as one of the original crew members from the first film in a short but sweet experience.
Then there's the game play. You don't get to see the Alien right away. You actually have to deal with other humans that are as scared as you so they form pacts with others and you have to deal with the groups of them that will kill you on sight. Stealth in this game is a main priority through-out the game. You maybe able to fight some enemies off but there's no way of killing that Alien. A matter of fact, you get caught by that Alien, you might as well stick an apple in your mouth and prepare to be that Alien's main meal for the week. Unless you scare him off with a badass flamethrower you eventually get in the later portion of the game. The other enemies that you will have to deal with as well, is the working Joes. They are robots that aren't as dangerous as the Alien but they can, and will ♥♥♥♥ your day up if you aren't careful fighting them. Admittedly, the AI for Humans and Working Joes are much, much weaker in comparison to the Alien. Not bad, just weaker.
I guess this game overall took me roughly 10-15 hours on my first playthrough to complete which is fairly long for a horror game in all honesty. People complain about the backtracking but I liked it a lot. They already added in a lot to the game in terms of the ship you explore and so the game at one point will become more open as you explore the ship trying to find your way around it.
End of review if you don't want to hear minor spoilers.

An awful lot of games claim to provide an “immersive” experience, very few succeed to the extent that Alien: Isolation does. As other reviewers have already noted, this game really feels like you’re playing through a AAA movie - the voice acting, environments, action and music are all terrific. Isolation also stands apart from most games you’ll play today by being a true gamer’s game - totally focused on a kickass single-player campaign experience. You’ll crawl and hide your way through this game and enjoy (almost) every second of it.
Of course, no game is perfect, and Isolation is no exception. There is a bug in the first mission that requires a restart or a door won’t open and when you open up the controls on a PC game it really shouldn’t pull up the mapping for a controller. The very end of the game also feels a little bit on the tedious side. But those are ultimately minor complaints. This game is definitely worth picking up - whether you’re a fan of survival horror genre, or not.

I was a bit late to the party in playing this, but was pleasantly surprised when I did.
An operator in a border control office doesn't sound like the most exciting premise, but it is confusingly fun.  The entry policy changes daily and you are paid/penalised on how many people you process each day; do you risk shortcutting a guy in the hope they're legit, go for a body scan only to find he is actually a she, or detain them and earn a sneaky commission from the supporting guard unit. (Note these are only a handful of the possible options as the game unfolds)
At the end of the each day you must then mange your home finances; who from the family gets the food and medicine and who will go without and risk death.
Certainly worth a look, it’s the bureaucracy you always dreamed of!

Factorio is like the ultimate management sim, you start off with nothing and start by builing a small factory, all while holding off the attacks of the local biters (unless you are playing in sandbox or peaceful mode), and by the end of the game you will have this massive factory that will build everything for you if you so choose. factorio while in Alpha hardly seems that way, it has many things to do and the devs are constantly pushing out updates and bug fixes, and if they arent enough this game already has a fairly sizable modding community, and the best part, if in doubt you can download a demo of the game and try it for youself!

I bought this game years ago from their website, and didn't once regret it. From the first time I saw the video, I've only gotten ever happier and more satisfied by Factorio. I've played 350+ hours so far (over 100 in one world) and can easily see myself tripling that.
Mind you, all of this is BEFORE you take into account the steady stream of satisfying updates. These updates aren't your piddling "50 more vanity items!" we've grown so accustomed to. No, these are incredible additions, things like "this huge single-player game is now fully multiplayer and coop", and "in late-game you now get to go to SPACE". Also worthy of note is that the game's balance has been constantly improving, as have the graphics.
And if all that wasn't enough, the game has extensive mod support, which is always my favorite feature as a developer. Mods can keep a game fresh and fun for over a decade. That being said, my 300 hours have been sans mods - the base content is just that good.
I can't express how much I recommend and endorse this game! If you only get one game this year, I urge you to try Factorio's demo. Instead of yet another tepid, linear AAA game, Factorio will please you for years. It already has for me. I look forward to making some great mods for this... Assuming I ever get bored with the default game.
EDIT (3/20/2016): As of the latest update, Factorio loads over 400% faster on my old Thinkpad. What sorcery is this?! Keep up the great work, Wube Software, it's much appreciated! :D
(Also, Night Vision is less eye-straining and more useful than it was the last time I tried it.)

This game has an unexpected new story but also has some big faults that just completely ruin the experience. I've played the entirety of it with a keyboard, and I
can't get used to the controls for Classic Sonic and the Avatar. Another big problem is how automatized the game is, specially at the start, and how from one level to another you're required to act on things that normally happened automatically.
The graphics are awesome and much more realistic, and easily surpass Lost World's simplistic aesthetic. Although I need to ask... why do the cutscenes look so compressed? They're clearly happening in real-time on the engine, since our Avatar is present.
The music is
a point in favor of the Sonic franchise, and this game definitely reminded us of that, with some
pieces like Infinite's theme.
Note:
My final statement is that this game was a good take on the Sonic series, definitely better than Boom, but it was risky and even though the Modern and Classic Sonic formula was perfect on Generations, they still managed to mess up some things. Also, I couldn't see any reason to repeat any stage at all, even though they tried to add some replayability with the "SOS" mechanic.
Oh... the "Customize your Avatar and people can use it in their games" thing? I'm sorry to say that it's an extremely lackluster addition, and could have been expanded in so many ways, but they did just enough to grab the attention of...
. (you know who I'm talking about)

as much as it hurts me, i can not recommend this game. in fact it's more a movie than a game. maybe sonic team forgot what they were working on.
starting with the good sides:
it's graphics and sound are amazing.
and many well done cut scenes, as i mentioned, it's more like a movie.
but that's about it..
the bad things:
basicly everything else. the main part that makes a game: the physics.
they simply do not work right.
classic sonic never felt so bad to play, especially now after sonic mania, this is just a rock which only gets through the level from the springs and boost pads or the drop/spindash and the platforming sections are so incredibly hard/frustrating to control, that you can only hop through it, very slowly and carefully. maybe you can become good at it, but it's the worst controls/physics to learn i've ever experienced in a classic setup.
oh and ofc it has cheap deaths. in fact almost everything feels like a cheap death.
not a sonic-style deaths in which you just drop into a pit you havn't seen, or ran into enemies. but deaths that happen just because they wanted to kill you at certain points, maybe to ♥♥♥♥ up the scores, so you have to play it more often or to leangthen the gametime. i dunno. the avatar: he has no way of quickly gaining boost, no spin/dropdash, no boost. nothing. he instead has this weapon thingy that sometimes is fast, sometimes is a bit of fun, but ultimately gets boring real quickly, since it's either working on it's own, or not fun to use after multiple times. overall he could have a place, if he had a way to boost up to full speed more quickly too.
but quick movement also means the game plays itself, since the phsyics are so bad, you have automated sections in every corner. you as a player only really jump and use your weapon. even the running often happens on it's own. just like in modern sonic stages.

STALKER is an example of a game that has numerous flaws, and yet manages to be amazing.  In fact, despite its bugs, unfinished and missing content, janky world etc. has managed to find a spot in my top 10 most beloved games of all time.  Not only that, it is the one game that has sold me on the concept of a survival game.  The Zone is a trecherous, scary place that is caked in so much atmopshere that it's hard not to feel as though every step you take is one step closer to your own untimely demise, and nothing is as satisfying as making it out of a rough encounter without bleeding to death or barely escaping an irradiated area after you realized you didn't pack enough anti-rads.  You are NEVER safe in this game.  Ever.  Admittedly Shadow of Chernobyl is the most linear of the three STALKER games, but honestly each one is cheap enough that you should just get all 3.  If you want a more open world, then play Clear Sky or even better Call of Pripyat.  But Shadow fo Chernobyl is still a gripping experience and a great starting point for this wonderful, creepy world - and there are lots of mods out there worth checking out, as well as the excellent standalone game STALKER: Lost Alpha which seeks to recreate STALKER based on its original design document and the many features that were cut during its lengthy 6 year development time.  Definitely check this one out.

This is a great game.   It's basically sailing anywhere in the world with real weather.
There's not a lot of races at the moment and the interface could be improved, but it is alpha.

A unique game that isn't quite there yet, but has lots of promise for fans of sailing.  The game is pretty and while some crucial aspects are very crudely implemented, every line is there and they for the most part do what you expect. You have access to multiple genoas and they each have their own characteristics. You can adjust your main sail in detail and the game acounts for sail twist and offers advice on the options you have to improve your current setup. The devs are very active and organize races every weekend. They seem passionate and determined (both about sailing and the game) and that is the most important part.
While I have only gotten a few hours into the game, some gaping flaws really need to be addressed. You can pull up the biggest genoa you have even in close haul and somehow you go faster. This is despite the fact that the lower part of the genoa is now underwater. The waterline seems to be mostly cosmetic at this point in time and that really breaks immersion. Ports are not in the game so you can't really go anywhere. That feeling when you see the port lights in the distance in the late evening after a full day out is such a huge part of the experience and is sorely missing. You cant really see the coastline until you are right on top of it and that is also a shame.
I will probably not be sinking a lot of time in this game until the simulation is a bit more fleshed out, but I would recommend it to anyone who has been waiting for a game like this for years like I have.

Has potential but needs a heap or work.  Game is suited to shortish based match racing and isn't a "sail around the world" simulator although you could do this if you wish.  Lots of bugs (not game killers just annoying).
I basically log in once or twice per day to check wind, lines and course then log back out.  Will monitor and update accordingly.  Postive because I want this to succeed.....I hope I don't regret it.

Let me preface this with the fact that this game is a pre release and is still in the works, which they do disclose when you purchase. Therefore there are glitches, and frequent changes.
That being said, when the game works properly, it is a very enjoyable replacement to actual sailing for those who live in arewas where sailing is only a spring-fall past time. The graphics are very nice, the sound is soothing, and learning some tips and tricks in sail maagement is pretty beneficial. The ability to choose difficulty levels from everything from soley navigation to controlling every line and sail is a huge plus, and the choice between multiple different types of sailboats and keep them moving in different locations throughout the world keeps things very interesting.
Again, it's in pre release and there are definitely some things that could be improved upon, the biggest to me being that no matter how you trim your sails, the heel is excessive. The maps screen takes up a lot of space in your view which can be changed in video settings, however they revert back to original every time you log out and log back in. You can choose to change your keyboard shortcuts, however every once in a while it glitches and one button activiates three different processes.
Overall, this is a very fun simulator and once they take care of the glitches it will be pretty dang perfect! Definitely recommend to those looking to escape when actual sailing isn't an option.

Speaking as someone who has never seen any of the movies or played other games in the alien franchise, this game was really good. This game is a very well done survival horror game that has a good art design and game mechanics that feel very fitting and real. From what I understand this isn't some regular movie licenced game being that its not something that is there because of the movies. This game stand on its own and is a very good survival horror game even to me who has never had any prior experience to the aliens franchise.

Pros
-------
+ Dark and terrifying atmosphere
+ Really good alien animations and detail
+ Sneaking around and hiding is intense
+ Smart alien AI
+ The sound design is up to par
+ Long campaign mode
+ Good amount of useful gear and items to craft
+ Survivor game mode can offer good amounts of replay value (if you have the DLC)
+ Wonderful visuals
Cons
-------
- Droid AI can be easily outsmarted and outmaneuvered
- Choppy cut scenes
- Some bad glitches and bugs, nothing gamebreaking so far though
- The Survivor game mode only comes with one map without the DLC
Overall impressions so far have been very good, a terrifying experience that I recommend to any true fan of the  horror/survival genre and the alien series, I believe Sega have truly revived themselves with this one and thier past mistakes can be easliy forgiven thanks to this.

Even 1,5 years after it's release this game remains one of the more impressive survival horror of late. It doesn't pick up its pace for a couple of hours into the story, but it never slacks on creating an atmosphere and immersing you into its world. It is an incredible journey, sometimes challenging, but always rewarding in the end.
The game is not perfect, I remember having a few gripes with the way the game handled its first enemy encounters, being unable to pick up enemy weapons, or me blaming an Alien AI for being too smart and all-seeing, but later I could see the reasoning behind these decisions. And those problems went away pretty fast.
The game runs great and looks like original motion picture. I didn't encounter any bugs or crashes.
Looking back I'm not thinking about the jumpscares, or those tense moments of fleeing away or hiding from the Alien. It is this cozy, comfortable feeling, that you earned during all those hours in the game. Lurking in the shadows, outsmarting your enemies. Skills that you didn't unlcok with xp grinding, but those that you learned yourself. And I just wish I could visit the Sevastopol Station for the first time, again. And that is a sign of a great game.

(Warning, minor spoilers at the end of the review)
This game was awesome to play. Controller or Keyboard, they both play really well. This game will make you paranoid and lockers will become your new home. Get used to it buddy, its either that Alien is gonna shove that tail up your ♥♥♥♥♥♥ or you spend the night in a cramped locker, your choice.
So, this game isn't all about locker hopping. If you're brave enough, you'll try your best to sneak past what maybe the best AI design for an horror enemy ever. The Alien will move around in the vents and can hear your tracking device beep. You can also travel around in the vents as well. The Alien is known to crawl through the vents with you and kill you in there but I never had that happen to me but it still can happen to you.
Speaking of sound, the sound design is masterful and immersive. When you're walking down a hallway you can hear the Alien moving around in the vents, his growl is subtle but terrifyingly believable. Voice acting is amazing. The actors are engaged and show emotion in their voices. Especially the lead role, Amanda, daughter of Ellen Ripley, who was in the original films, her voice actor couldn't of done better.
The facial animations and 3D models were so realistic. The Enemy design and the art in general represents the movie down to the cracks in the wall, its so good. Its like they were in the set for the movies to design this game. Its so bazaar being in the ship you saw get over taken by Aliens. Even in the DLC you can experience that for yourself as you can play as one of the original crew members from the first film in a short but sweet experience.
Then there's the game play. You don't get to see the Alien right away. You actually have to deal with other humans that are as scared as you so they form pacts with others and you have to deal with the groups of them that will kill you on sight. Stealth in this game is a main priority through-out the game. You maybe able to fight some enemies off but there's no way of killing that Alien. A matter of fact, you get caught by that Alien, you might as well stick an apple in your mouth and prepare to be that Alien's main meal for the week. Unless you scare him off with a badass flamethrower you eventually get in the later portion of the game. The other enemies that you will have to deal with as well, is the working Joes. They are robots that aren't as dangerous as the Alien but they can, and will ♥♥♥♥ your day up if you aren't careful fighting them. Admittedly, the AI for Humans and Working Joes are much, much weaker in comparison to the Alien. Not bad, just weaker.
I guess this game overall took me roughly 10-15 hours on my first playthrough to complete which is fairly long for a horror game in all honesty. People complain about the backtracking but I liked it a lot. They already added in a lot to the game in terms of the ship you explore and so the game at one point will become more open as you explore the ship trying to find your way around it.
End of review if you don't want to hear minor spoilers.
(Spoilers area)
One gripe I have with this game however is the fact that the ending was so ♥♥♥♥ing unsatisfying. I won't give away what happens but basically, instead of a big boss fight, you get a stupid ♥♥♥♥ing QTE that has no business being in this game whatsoever. I don't get why companies make these amazing overall games and then ruin the ending because they need to be lazy as hell. Its lazy!!! So lazy! QTEs shouldn't exist in games like this and in the form that they are presented in. Not cool! At all! This would of ruined the game if the game was a meh experience. Luckily, the game was amazing and is still worth getting.
(Moar Spoiled Dinner)
This game also did one thing right at the same time that was minor but was very noticeable. At one point, this game will make you feel truly alone. The Isolation name is very real in this game. You will feel alone, helpless, like you're unable to conquer the challenge the game presents Amanda with. You will feel alone and that is immersion at its best for me. I felt scared and alone. You have nobody but you. Its amazing in a game like this. That alone sold the experience.

An awful lot of games claim to provide an “immersive” experience, very few succeed to the extent that Alien: Isolation does. As other reviewers have already noted, this game really feels like you’re playing through a AAA movie - the voice acting, environments, action and music are all terrific. Isolation also stands apart from most games you’ll play today by being a true gamer’s game - totally focused on a kickass single-player campaign experience. You’ll crawl and hide your way through this game and enjoy (almost) every second of it.
Of course, no game is perfect, and Isolation is no exception. There is a bug in the first mission that requires a restart or a door won’t open and when you open up the controls on a PC game it really shouldn’t pull up the mapping for a controller. The very end of the game also feels a little bit on the tedious side. But those are ultimately minor complaints. This game is definitely worth picking up - whether you’re a fan of survival horror genre, or not.

Have been playing this game all the way back since mid 2013, played through the many eras of open beta and such. Have played through a total of 3 server regions which is insane, NA (250ping) > OCE (110ping) > SEA (15ping)
This game has become my absolute favourite game throughout the years. I remember watching youtubers play this game like AllShamNoWow and Shibby2142 which influenced me to play it. The game has grown throughout the many years of development since beta, which has seen many changes. Not many features that were in the beta look the same as today.
Gameplay wise it is very expansive, with the current total god count at a total of 80 at this point of time, which is considerably alot and they are releasing a new one roughly every 2 patches each. The game has a sense of achievement, which makes me want to play the game, as well as a form of progression, which is in the form of masteries and unlocking new gods. I remember the times where I was a F2P player, which I had to spend the in game currency to purchase or rent gods, but the ultimate god pack is where it is at, a value for money purchase. The game is really not at all P2W, as everything can be unlocked with in game currency, without spending a cent. The only real thing is the time to grind it out, and the fact that some gods can be more stronger than the others. But cmon, its a team game, if one guy is wrecking, just work together then. The game features a very unique 3rd person MOBA style, compared to its relatives DOTA2 and LoL, which is to me much more intriguing as it makes you feel as if you ARE the god. Combat is very flexible, with many ways to fight or disengage, and one single move can turn an entire fight over. The matchmaking system can also be very screwed, with the possibility of low levels being matched with an entire party of veterans.
Aesthetics wise, this game has come a long way, looking like an unpolished turd long time ago, and now graphics are top notch fancy. The game has gone under many graphical reworks, including maps, UI and gods. The maps went through many revisions, for example Conquest, which has seen many different faces and layouts since. Arena constantly goes through revamps to fit an event, like the recent Olympic-themed one which had a running track around, which actually gave a speed boost, and provided some additional gameplay and fun into it. Many gods have went through changes, becoming really detailed characters. I can really say the graphic designers have put in a lot of work, even with the new gods which are also very detailed and well designed. Skins are also a nearly mandatory part of a MOBA game, as nearly every MOBA has it. SMITE has done it well with the vast platter of skins, even with its own tier ranking from 1 to 5. I can say I have spent enough money on this game to not give up on it. This game is also quite well optimized for lower end PCs, with mine for example being a i7-3770 , 8GB RAM paired with a really crappy nVidia GT630, and I am able to run everything at maximum with the exception of world detail, which is set at low to give me the best FPS of around 60, at 1080p.
I cannot forget the many experiences the game has given me, and I also have met many awesome people, including the people of my clan, which are also my fellow countrymen, which I frequently play with.
I definitely would recommend this to people who would like to try out a new game, I promise you a fun and enjoyable experience.

Rome 2, ahhhhh Rome 2.....
So much hype, so many expectations, so many promises.... Here is the thing: Overall, now is a solid game, on single player only( at least for me and my buddy).
Almost 2 years after release how does the game fare? Well, the thing is, this game fails because of what sorrounded and still surrounds it,  from a design and gameplay perspective.
Allow me to elaborate, if you will: this game was HYPED to no end. Several live action videos and developer diaries, ALL of it to deliver an inevitably weak game.  From a  design perspective, many strange decisions: unit cards, UI, retainers, generals, agents, faction bonuses, turns per year are just some features that seem like a downgrade from previous Total War games, namely the previous title, Shogun 2. Gameplay wise,  the battles suffer a lot, and is in this aspect that  most critics arise from. Unit collision is still an issue, cavalry still has absolute no way to it,  kill moves are quite franckly a poor way to make units interact with each other ( even tough recently they appropriated the animation of projectile hit to kill other soldiers without using the kill move mechanic, which is just lazy).
Faction wise, there is almost no variety between them, (amazing that even though Shogun 2 has the exact same unit models and soldiers for every clan they still manage to give more variety and personallity than Rome 2's many factions).  Seriously, aside from character skins and faction banners, there is no difference in gameplay between Rome and Carthage.
That is not to say that the game is a disaster, it is not. It has some good ideas, like province happiness, and graphics wise it is impressive, it is wonderful to see the ancient world more vivid than ever.
What ultimately makes this game a thumbs down for me is the preposterous practices on the part of the publisher and the developer. Sorry, no ammount of justification will ever make up for a broken game at launch ( don't believe me? watch a certain " angry"youtuber review of this game); day one DLC  also is unnaceptable under any circunstance, for it means it is content that was created along with the main game and cut and sold later to boost their profits ( I'm looking at you greek states DLC ( bought it later for 1 buck during sale) );
Also currently, at the time of this review, we are at PATCH 17! This is absolutely outrageous, I ask you fellow gamer, how can a game need 17 PATCHES to be in a working state? Simple, an uttlerly broken game. Even if the state has improved (  sfter almost 2 years.... yay....), the point is THIS SHOULD NEVER BE ACCEPTABLE. The thing is, the moment they released this game is when they decided it was good enough for sale, and this clearly wasn't the case, so, a Shameful display.
In the end, it is painfull, because this could easily have  been the greatest Total War game ever made, a comeback to the glory days of Rome 1, now it is a reminder on how not to launch a total war game.
P.S. The most amazing thing, recently I played with my friend ( fellow Total War fanatic), a Fall of the Samurai coop campaign, over 60 hours  of campaign and not a SINGLE issue, NO desyncs and smooth framerate. We tried to play a Rome 2 grand Campaign recently, and it crashed on turn 2...
A big let down for an otherwise amazing series...

Sonic Forces Is probably the best Modern Sonic game I played so far.
Besides the first few moments of bug that caused the game to crash and giving a roadblock, it was one of those games that I could sit down and without throwing my controller at the ground could finish it in a okay pace.
Gameplay:
The gameplay is solid in my book.
There's no lives. Instead of that you get scores and the scores are calculated based on your time you beat the stage, the retries you took to beat the stage, the rings you collected. + robots and collection bonuses they get calculated into your rank score and additionally they add to a medal system ranking you up.
The game consist of 30 stage + secret stages and 3 additional free Shadow stage which are unique.
Addititonally you have side content like doing SOS mission with certain characters and adaily challange for another bonus.
Classic Sonic:
physics feel slightly off gave me an interesting moment when I tried to jump on a trampoline and with the little momentum I got I landed on the other side of the trampoline.
Additionally they added the drop dash from Mania which can be useful but I don't think I used it much besides the first few levels where I felt more comfortable with it.
They have him only one type of shield. Which is the bubble shield however this time it functions like the blue shield instead of the bubble. It does not have bounce ability, does not protect you from drowning.
Modern Sonic:
They re-balanced the boost. Boost does not being full by default when you enter a level. You need to destroy robots or free some wisps to gain boost. Rings won't do.
In the other hand constantly boosting is also not necessarily viable. there are certain parts of the maps where you have to make sure you either hit a booster to avoid falling off the map or turn low or high speed.
There is air boost this time around.
If you don't have a target with homing attack sonic double jumps. I personally feel it a welcoming change.
no light speed dash
Avatar:
You use weapons costumize different weapons has different bonuses and different uses.
I did not get around myself to try and use all of them but what I tried is
-the burst (which is default) makes a constant flame attack if powered up does multiple jumps.
-Lightning it's an eletric whip practically. if powered up "light speed dash" (follows rings AND enemies this time)
-Meteor targets multiple targets and gives you temporary invincibility powered up
-Greengun I tried this but I don't think there's a wisp for it? it pushes enemies into eachother destroying them instantly but extremely useless against bosses
-Cube  / didn't try
-Drill    / didn't try
-Nega  / didn't try
You have a sort of "homing" attack with it.
Each weapon has different abilities do different things.
Modern Sonic & Avatar:
This is a stage variant. Where you play both of them in the same time. Sonic's speed and your avatar's weapon combined. It's my personal favourite not because you use your character you made up, but because it's probably the most fun stages.
They also added or well re-added a few quick time event to both of them respectively to they gameplay. Which honestly makes sense.
Bosses:
interestingly enough these bosses are less generic sonic bosses. they not the type of "hit me till I die" they were slightly more challenging than usual. Challenging in a way that is still fun to beat. And it's not a "7 times hit and dead" they have a health bar and different spots to attack some giving more or less damage. Like the avatar's weapon can be a consistent low damage but obviously the homing attack is almost always the strongest.
Stages:
the levels are short 1-3 minutes. But they actually are fun to play They feel well designed for what they are.
But as good they are one should mention that they are sort of a "call back" levels. Most of these stage designs (but not layouts) has been seen before in other sonic games.
But it's also not too huge of an issue in my book.
The game can be completed in 3ish hours.
Story:

Eggman discovers the Phantom Ruby and it's powers and attempts to use it agaisnt everyone mostly to make sure Sonic is defeated and stays down. The Resistance's job is to restore the peace, stop and take back they territories from Eggman.
Infinite not explained in the game but he is actually just a Jackal an ex-squad leader trying to raid Eggman's base but ended up joining him.
Soundtrack:
... It's a Sonic game. there's really, REALLY a few Sonic game with bad ost.
I'm not going to score it like 855/1245 what I going to say is. I had fun with it. It's a Sonic game that I feel like I could replay a few times. Some stages even more times. It has it's issues, fortunately did not became a problem on my end. It run smooth on my mid-range PC:
I5 core (4 core)
6 GB memory
750 Geforce Nvidia - TI
Windows 10 os
I recommend it.

Borderlands 2 is an awesome game. It has an interesting story, great characters (especially the main villain Handsome Jack and your companion CL4P-TP aka Claptrap the mini robot) and some of the best gameplay I've ever experienced.
In a nutshell, you are a vault hunter and you are enlisted by a hyperactive CL4P-TP robot who calls himself Claptrap and refers to you as his minion. He wants you to help him bring down the villain Handsome Jack who is apparently responsible for shutting down the CL4P-TP production line.
You can play it single player, but at the same time open your game for up to three others so it becomes a co-op game, and it is at co-op that the game absolutely excels. The creatures on Pandora (where the game takes place) become stronger or weaker depending on how many players there are in a game.
As you progress through the story, you level up. Every mission you play, whether main or side mission has a certain preset level that would be nice for you to have making it clear in advance which missions are easier and harder. Expect more higher level missions as you progress. I think this system works very well indeed for this game. I had a ton of fun playing it, the dialogue is fantastic, the voice acting excellent, the diversity of characters and creatures is astoundingly large.
If you like FPS, humor, great story, great characters and excellently finetuned gameplay, this game is for you. If you liked Borderlands, you're gonna love Borderlands 2.

I have always wondered what it would be like to live in a Class-8 Dwelling in a country that has just emerged from war and reopened its borders and I have been drawn out of a metaphorical hat to be in charge of its wellbeing. Oh? What's that! Papers,Please!
This game was a very, very interesing addition to my everygrowing list of games I should shake the hands of the developers of (Needs a catchier title)
It is a game where you play as an Immigration officer who is the only one in charge of the ENTIRE border control. Which means you have a workload, You have simply a Rule book, The news and a transcript and must make the important decision to accept or deny entry in to Arstotzka, You must carefully assess each bit of their passport, Entry tickets, Work permits, the rules change daily and to keep on top of them all is a difficult task indeed! For example on Day 1 You simply look for the passport and if all the details on that are up to scratch they are allowed in! If you get it wrong 3 times money begins to be deducted from your pay.
That last sentence influenced a lot in me, you have a family to care for who only living in a Class 8 dwelling will not survive long , you must get through enough people in a day to pay rent, Food and heat and sometimes your idiot Son goes and gets ill and you have to buy Medicine... That idiot! It toys with your emotions, you want to let this person in to see their Husband after they were separated after the war, but if you do you will directly be at blame and lose pay and possibly a Family member... See why I like this game alot!
Also the tension is insane! You have so much to think about in such little time it is hard not to become overhelmed and hide behind a convenient pringles can!
I highly recommend this game, the Tension it creates in currently unmatched and the fun you get out of it is addicting, It is also fairly cheap for what you get out of it! With exellence in its Music, Design and plot it is a massive contender for Game of 2013! Enjoy a Class 8 Dwelling folks!

You check papers at border control. All is dull until the first terrorist attack happens, cuts your day short and you realise you are falling short in providing for your family. Then the bribes start. The rebels approach you. Your country oppresses you. A handful of dilemmas and 20 different endings make this game worthwhile.  Even if what you mainly do is check papers. Do try it.

It's a coming of age story told in a very interesting and 'close to home' way a lot of folks of my generation will recognize.

I had originally purchased this game for the simulation aspect of the game and thought to myself wow looks great! I can learn to sail properly... YEAH NO!  DO NOT BE FOOLED BY THIS!  this game is nothing more then a line trimming simulator.
The Pros
Good water graphics
nice boat models and weather as well as waves.
yeah thats bout it....
THE CONS
* It lacks any kind of visual appeal on the land... not even any trees just a big green and brown height map.
* It completly lacks any ports of any kind to sail to ..not even a generic port randomly planted aorund the map until such
time something good could be developed.  (Would take to much work i guess)
* There is no damage mechanics, meaning the mast will never snap, you can run aground with knowledge you will never sink. No damage even in terrible weather.
* You can't capsize your boat... no sir... not even in a giant hurricane...you can rest easily knowing you will reach your destination no matter what the gods throw at you for you are LORD OF THE SEA and nothing shall stand in your path.
* Can't enter the cabins... ur just basically standing there... trimming your lines every so often.
* Only updates that ever come seem to be always for races and nothing actually towards the mechanics of the game/sim. We are then told that this requires the least amount of the devs time to put into the game which is fine and all but what else is he working on because it surely isnt the missing ports, propper terrain or any other propper mechanics.
* Dev does not interact with the community aside from that one time he decided to write a letter about what the sim will not be which pretty much ruled out everything that could make it even a sim or remotely enjoyable. Instead he has some dude who interacts for him and makes nothing but excuses for why they can't do something.
* Certain things take to much time and effort to put into the game so therefore the lone programmer will not be doing it...  instead of making a propper learning simulation.. we have the standing still line simulator.
I normally do not write reviews and this is the first i've done. I dont normally slam games as developing takes alot of time and commitment... which this dev is unable to provide. Week after week is nothing but racing updates, the game does not teach you the propper mechanics of sailing because according to this... you raise sails and  |NOTHING can go wrong or stand in your way.
I feel like i have wasted my money on this title and because i feel like i have been let down in some pretty big ways i felt i should write this for anyone who wants an accurate simulation..because this aint it and probably wont be it for along time if at all.

The first thing to recognize is that this is a simulator and it's in early access. So if you're looking for a quick thrill, this probably isn't the game for you. This game is unique because of its finer simulation of the sails, and in expert mode you're responsible for handling all of the lines. To my knowledge, I don't know of another game that attempts that level of detail.
As an early access simulator you shouldn't expect any fancy visuals or gameplay elements. But if the developers let the community provide content I think this game could provide an impressive environment for anyone interested in sailing based games. The developer has mentioned that the game will focus on sailing first, which I think is important! But if the community was allowed to contribute to the scenery it could be more appealing to the casual gamer.
There has been an effort to import chart features into the game as of this review. Thus there are buoys, wrecks, and structures where they are located on maps. The buoys themselves appear a little crude right now (I'm not sure channel markers are separately rendered either), but I think it points to a bright future for capabilities for near-shore scenery.
Weather data is also impressive. The game processes data from NOAA (GFS data I assume?) on a regular basis to provide fairly accurate weather. Thus, you should be able to use any surface analysis from the web to help you on your voyage. Wave dynamics still need some work, and it would be neat to see ice included in the game. (Is sea current data included?)
So if you like sailing, or  want to do some multiplayer races, I recommend this game. If you'd rather see more features then I'd say keep following it to see if community added content becomes supported. If development keeps steaming ahead with this game then I won't be suprised if it becomes a 'classic' in the sim genre.
EDIT-
Lastly, if you do buy this I recommend turning off the camera focus feature that makes everything out of focus in the background. It makes seeing the lines a pain if you're in expert mode!

This game is something else. Some backstory: I am a sailor in real life, having started out on small boats, some under power and others not. When I was 18 I was offerend a position as a helmsman on a 66' foot sailboat on Lake Michigan. We would do charters from june to november and sometimes would encounter rough seas. Sometimes storms would sweep up onto the lake and we'd have to turn tail and get into the bay as quick as possible.
I learned a lot about sailing during those four years on the lakes, and I aplied that knowledge when I bought this game. This game is the most accurate sailing simulator I have played so far, especially on the bigger boats like the Carribean Rose and the new performance cruiser.
It's not perfect yet, there are a lot of things missing, but for something that is essentially a one man project, I can see great things coming from this game. It's very beautiful, very fun, very educational when it comes to sailing. It's got a lot of potential and gets a lot of things right. I look forward to see how it turns out.

Pros
- Pretty much every line in a sailboat is modeled and can be manipulated.
- You can sail anywhere in the world.
- Real-life weather data.
- Pretty graphics.
- Nice racing experience.
Cons
- Sailing dynamics is not simulated (don't be fooled by the game's name). Center of buoyancy, center of effort, center of lateral resistance, center of gravity are not modeled. Try sailing with just the genoa up. Spoiler: you can't.
- Upper telltales just replicate the lower ones. In other words, sail twist is not modeled.
- Heeling behavior is unrealistic and apparently scripted (poorly).
- When you adjust trim or pull on a line, it takes time for it to take effect, as in, you trim in the main sheet, wait for a second, and the boom moves. Same with any lines.
- How waves affect the hull is not modeled.
- Unlike other sims which can be a training tool (like MS FSX), this is not a simulator of sailing. It could qualify as a simulator of sailboat racing perhaps, or a simulator of pulling lines on a sailboat, that's about it.
- It cannot be played offline, meaning if you have no internet, than you cannot play the game.
I look forward to seeing this game develop into a sailing simulator, which it is not at this time.

Even 1,5 years after it's release this game remains one of the more impressive survival horror of late. It doesn't pick up its pace for a couple of hours into the story, but it never slacks on creating an atmosphere and immersing you into its world. It is an incredible journey, sometimes challenging, but always rewarding in the end.
The game is not perfect, I remember having a few gripes with the way the game handled its first enemy encounters, being unable to pick up enemy weapons, or me blaming an Alien AI for being too smart and all-seeing, but later I could see the reasoning behind these decisions. And those problems went away pretty fast.
The game runs great and looks like original motion picture. I didn't encounter any bugs or crashes.
Looking back I'm not thinking about the jumpscares, or those tense moments of fleeing away or hiding from the Alien. It is this cozy, comfortable feeling, that you earned during all those hours in the game. Lurking in the shadows, outsmarting your enemies. Skills that you didn't unlcok with xp grinding, but those that you learned yourself. And I just wish I could visit the Sevastopol Station for the first time, again. And that is a sign of a great game.

(Warning, minor spoilers at the end of the review)
This game was awesome to play. Controller or Keyboard, they both play really well. This game will make you paranoid and lockers will become your new home. Get used to it buddy, its either that Alien is gonna shove that tail up your ♥♥♥♥♥♥ or you spend the night in a cramped locker, your choice.
So, this game isn't all about locker hopping. If you're brave enough, you'll try your best to sneak past what maybe the best AI design for an horror enemy ever. The Alien will move around in the vents and can hear your tracking device beep. You can also travel around in the vents as well. The Alien is known to crawl through the vents with you and kill you in there but I never had that happen to me but it still can happen to you.
Speaking of sound, the sound design is masterful and immersive. When you're walking down a hallway you can hear the Alien moving around in the vents, his growl is subtle but terrifyingly believable. Voice acting is amazing. The actors are engaged and show emotion in their voices. Especially the lead role, Amanda, daughter of Ellen Ripley, who was in the original films, her voice actor couldn't of done better.
The facial animations and 3D models were so realistic. The Enemy design and the art in general represents the movie down to the cracks in the wall, its so good. Its like they were in the set for the movies to design this game. Its so bazaar being in the ship you saw get over taken by Aliens. Even in the DLC you can experience that for yourself as you can play as one of the original crew members from the first film in a short but sweet experience.
Then there's the game play. You don't get to see the Alien right away. You actually have to deal with other humans that are as scared as you so they form pacts with others and you have to deal with the groups of them that will kill you on sight. Stealth in this game is a main priority through-out the game. You maybe able to fight some enemies off but there's no way of killing that Alien. A matter of fact, you get caught by that Alien, you might as well stick an apple in your mouth and prepare to be that Alien's main meal for the week. Unless you scare him off with a badass flamethrower you eventually get in the later portion of the game. The other enemies that you will have to deal with as well, is the working Joes. They are robots that aren't as dangerous as the Alien but they can, and will ♥♥♥♥ your day up if you aren't careful fighting them. Admittedly, the AI for Humans and Working Joes are much, much weaker in comparison to the Alien. Not bad, just weaker.
I guess this game overall took me roughly 10-15 hours on my first playthrough to complete which is fairly long for a horror game in all honesty. People complain about the backtracking but I liked it a lot. They already added in a lot to the game in terms of the ship you explore and so the game at one point will become more open as you explore the ship trying to find your way around it.
End of review if you don't want to hear minor spoilers.

QTEs shouldn't exist in games like this and in the form that they are presented in. Not cool! At all! This would of ruined the game if the game was a meh experience. An awful lot of games claim to provide an “immersive” experience, very few succeed to the extent that Alien: Isolation does. As other reviewers have already noted, this game really feels like you’re playing through a AAA movie - the voice acting, environments, action and music are all terrific. Isolation also stands apart from most games you’ll play today by being a true gamer’s game - totally focused on a kickass single-player campaign experience. You’ll crawl and hide your way through this game and enjoy (almost) every second of it.
Of course, no game is perfect, and Isolation is no exception. There is a bug in the first mission that requires a restart or a door won’t open and when you open up the controls on a PC game it really shouldn’t pull up the mapping for a controller. The very end of the game also feels a little bit on the tedious side. But those are ultimately minor complaints. This game is definitely worth picking up - whether you’re a fan of survival horror genre, or not.

Played this game for awhile... and Man, this is something I'm forcing myself through.
First off, if you are gonna use characters, play them right.
Secondly, Unless you want to be brotherhood, don't use transitions with text.
First off, the very first thing, there is a time lapse, with a text screen. No animatics, no movie, a literal time pass of 6 months. Better yet, no one actually decides to even cover what happened then, otehr than it was 6 months.
Next thing you know, there is the freedom fighters. If you read the comics, you know what I'm talking about. This is my big peeve, the role choice.
Good ol knucklehead, thinks with his fists first, is the great leader. I mean, seriously?
No no no, it doesn't stop there. You have Amy on computers pulling up info and specs. If anyone knows Freedom Fighters, You'd have Sally Acorn where Knuckles is, and probably Nicole on coms.
(Major Spoiler) One big plothole, you battle infinite, and unlike Eggman who looses his bot and runs usually. Infinite beats you in the cut scenes. Yet keeps doing the cliche of letting the hero live. I mean, why? You get your first cut scene, Infinite is supposed to be a culmination of hate, there should be no question to finish the deed. I haven't beaten the game yet, but this literally happened 3 times in one sitting
But then, let's just say, you were someone like me. Big time sonic fan, and you want to really just give the game a chance. For one, you can see the common theme in the reviews, short levels. But, I can see why they did that. With a new SOS system, you replay levels for some value. Shorter levels make this easier.
So it isn't so bad when you go to repeat levels. But it does give me one bad taste, that is the fact when you have moments when you team up with Sonic, the theme song plays and it's awesome. But if you blast through it, you barely have time to even enjoy it,
And the big disappointment of the day is the extra/special levels. they are much too sort. Usually, I think special levels to be a challenge, or at least there, through something like a long level to make up for the shortness. There isn't a need to be short there cause SOS missions don't show there, at least as far as I have been playing
TL;DR Short levels aren't bad, they do make you want more, but it makes sense when you realize the new feature of the game that others didn't have
Now to get to the nitty gritty. Sonic controls are crappy. Speed engine is there, but the homing attack blows, you can't change directions once you got into the air, which means targetting gets more difficult, and you have to keep setting up your jumps before going forward. The jumps also aren't easy to work with as previous games, almost like it was a new person who made jump controls.
You get your own character, you don't get the spins Sonic has, but its fun at least to try something new. Even more, there are team up levels in Sonic too!
Customization options are really out there. (Personnally trying to get The Super Sonic Knight suit). You get access to looks of other Sega choices, and collect them. Makes it rewarding to play, and trying to beat your scores. Daily's help too by making it easier with a boost to your score.
And that's about it so far. Personnally, still on the fence, Sonic is my hero, so I want to give this a go through til the end to see if it is really worthwhile

To every review mentioning the crashes after the first level, it's been fixed. There are still a few bugs in the game though that causes crashing, but they're CPU related and are far and few between.
I'm just gonna go through the good, alright and bad aspects of the game. I like Sonic games, I speedrun Mania and thoroughly enjoy most of the entries in the series, Classic, Modern, Adventure, Boost, even some controversial ones like Heroes. But I'm also not a fanboy who can't see the good and bad points of a game. So I'll be as fair as I can and explain in detail what's what.
The game looks beautiful in game, no frame drops or anything on my 1060. Especially Modern Sonic's levels like the space ship level where he complains about there not being any floors to run on.
Some of the levels are really fun to play, they appear about mid game.
The level of customisation on the avatars is pretty crazy. After each level I was unlocking 6+ items, sometimes even going over 10, and even more sometimes. So if you like character creators in games, you'll love that. The Avatar weapons (wispons) are also decently varied, and will have you switching things up to find different routes through levels you can't normally access with another type.
I think I actually had the most fun on some of the avatar levels, so don't worry, it's not a tacked on extra, they actually did a good job with all the abilities and making them all work.
Loading times are insanely quick, so you're always doing something. 2 seconds max.
The menus function well, you have a choice of scrolling over the entire world, or pressing Y/Triangle to open up a list of levels which you can easily flick through to see all your levels, scores, times, red star coin collection, ranks, etc. It's clean and works great.
Do you like collecting things? Plenty of avatar gear to unlock and there's 5 red star rings in each stage for you to collect.
The story is nothing amazing, but it's not bad either. It serves it's purpose, it moves the game along, and gives a meaning to going to certain levels in certain orders unlike a few previous games. Sonic gets defeated... ANNND they've found him again, didn't even build any tension. Oh and here's Classic Sonic because dimensions and stuff.
Soundtrack is hit and miss. Usually Sonic games will have an amazing OST whether the game is good or bad, even 06 had a good soundtrack to it. This one is different, whether or not it's good though will be dependant on the individual listening to it. It didn't offend me, but I probably wouldn't listen to most of the tracks outside of the game.
The controls are alright. It's basically Sonic Generations but with some (questionable) changes. I've speedrun various Sonic games, so I'm familiar with all the little nuances with the gameplay in every Sonic game, and even I had alot of unfortunate deaths due to either poor level design, the controls being unresponsive, or some of the changes they've made to the game.
Lives are removed. Doesn't make a massive difference in all honesty except for the scoring system, which will cause you to lose points.
The bosses are pretty decent too, some are alot more fun than the others, wasn't really a fan of the run in a straight line and wait ones though (EG: Metal) with the exception of maybe 2. Ones like Zavok and one of the endgame bosses were fun.
There are missions and daily missions for you to do to unlock new avatar gear and gain bonus experience (As your avatar levels up it gains more gear), they add a little something to each level, but aren't manditory and don't ruin your experience if you chose to ignore them. There are bonus stages too.
Each avatar breed has a different ability, making them all feel slightly unique in their own way.
Level design in some levels is poor. The first levels are notable very easy, as they should be so you can learn the game's mechanics, but TOO easy. Straight line, jump once or twice and you're at the goal easy. Later levels? They have some really BS moments which are hard to avoid unless you know they're there. It feels like because you don't have lives anymore, they put in alot of cheap spots to kill you. The levels are also VERY short. A couple of minutes tops in most cases no matter who you're playing as.
So about the controls. Classic Sonic controls like a tank. Modern Sonic has issues too. Avatar only a couple. I loved how Generations and Colours felt, but it feels like a step back.
Classic Sonic's momentum is REALLY weird, and flat out clunky, as you'll see in some of the platforming sections. His spindash starts out insanely strong then fizzles out after a couple of seconds, it feels weird. Rolling down hills doesn't seem to gain much speed at all. There's barely any aerial mobility and feels sluggish. And the drop dash. Oh lord. As mentioned with the level design, there's alot of pitfalls, especially with Classic Sonic. The controls can be a little unresponsive at times, anyone familiar with jump sqaut animations in Smash Brothers will know what I mean when I say it takes a little bit for jumps to come out. Back to the point. Lots of pitfalls and Drop Dash. You drop dash, you see a hole, you press jump annnd nothing comes out. No problem I'll land on a lower section of the level right? Nope. For some reason Sonic will shoot STRAIGHT down if you Drop Dash off a ledge. Like gravity is increased tenfold, leading to more deaths than there should be. Overall, he feels sloppy. I had much more fun with Modern and Avatar if I'm honest. And the Casino level? Oh boy, enjoy THOSE controls.
Modern Sonic also has issues. 3D sections first. The drift mechanic is gone. Why? Don't know. It was super useful in taking sharp, bending turns turns. Now it's like driving an American muscle car. All power, no steering. This is made worse due to the fact Sonic barely reacts to your inputs while boosting. A turn comes up and it's a case of "Well, I guess we're going this way now". This can make some sections in levels very annoying, and forces (No pun intended) you to slow down. Gotta go fast? Apparently not. In particular a certain section on a very white coloured, futuristic city level. 2D sections also suffer from the clunkiness that Classic does.
The only real complaints I have with the Avatar was their momentum. They'll go from walking to sprinting WAY too fast, resulting in some untimely deaths that should have been avoidable. They also have a pretty slow start up on some weapons, causing you to get hit when you shouldn't.
The cutscenes seemed to be in low qaulity and the sound would be pretty quiet for some reason? And it feels like the balance was off too on which speaker they'd play through.
The abilities on each breed of avatar is great, but I really wish I could choose which ability I could use rather than being forced (Again, no pun intended) to have one based on the breed. Double jump is usually the one people will go for as it's a very useful ability, but it's sadly stuck to the bird when I'd much rather choose something else. Bird characters are usually pretty hideous in Sonic games, and also very obnoxious (I'm looking at you Jet).
The last boss. Spoiler explains what it's like, and why it's a dissappointment. The boss leading up to it is more original.
I beat the main game in 2.5 hours while goofing about sometimes. It's short.
The game is alright, it has it's flaws but does the job on the pricetag you're getting it for.

Post crashing it seems to be a very solid game so far. I have not run into any glitches yet besides a slight graphical one in the first boss fight. That being said the gameplay is what you've come to expect if you've played Generations and the custom character does provide an interesting way to play, especially when the first Wispon you acquire is a damn flame thrower which does mad amounts of damage.
Visuals are superb for a Sonic game and a definite step up over Generations and to a lesser extent Lost World.
Music so far hasn't sat well entirely with me, there has been only one or two tracks I've fully enjoyed so far and one of those is Infinite's theme but you know why.
Overall: A solid entry into the series so far, responsive controls, nice visuals, a story(?). I will update this review after I have spent more time with the game, I shall also provide a score as well once that happens
Edit: I haven't been having the performance issues some people have been having, I have everything set to max and my MSI GTX 960 2GB and i5-4460 seem to be keeping up with very little problems

For those that like replaying short stages over and over again there are some collectables to attempt to pad the disapointing gameplay length.

On the postive side the soundtrack and visuals are actually quite good. If only there was more game attached to this vivid rollercoaster.
For those on the fence, wait for a good sale and just play Sonic Mania and Generations instead.

Great game concept and the fun gameplay.  Its got a minecraft open world building style, but with simplified resource gathering that is limited to nodes that repop fairly often, I really enjoyed building castles, and upgrading the crafting stations to build better and better items.   The pvp combat system is pretty cool, but can be difficult with lag.   I enjoyed defending my castle with guild mates, but never quite got to the point of trying to be king.   Im not a great PVPer, so the full loot drop can be annoying, but that is part of the game.  No problem there.
The big problem comes with griefers.  Getting attacked while you are in the game is part of the game, but logging back in after a day away, and fining ALL of you stuff gone kinda ruins it.  Im not sure if there are exploits that allow some people to pick up your stuff, or if they really spent the time to smash every single item, but on our server several people were shocked to find everything that they had built gone.    There is no safe storage, and even when you log out, your body stays in game, and can be killed and looted.   I was on a "NO GRIEFING" server, but it still happens.
Also, there is no way to identify people until they waive at you.  So you cant tell friend from foe unless they happen to be wearing different armor.  So if someone kills you and takes all of your stuff, you dont even know who to to get revenge on.
So at this point I am done with this game.  I will watch for updates, and I will be glad to change my recommendation to Yes if they come up with a way to stop griefers.

Let me start with what is likely a great disservice to the game, but something I think needs to be said early.
This game is okay if you like the basic concept, but it is really only as good as the folks you play it with.
There is a great deal of depth for what is essentially Rust with a much more in-depth crafting system.  The UI shares a lot in common with that other game, and the general resource gathering aspect will feel very familiar to those that have played both.
But that is where the comparison ends.
I was hesitant to jump in on this one as I had played both flavors of that other game, and a few others games like it, and was expecting the same general type of community.  I'm not going to lie, yes, you'll encounter a few of those folks here as well, but the sheer scope of this game and the community at large, to me, more than makes up for any aspects of PVP that may have you not wanting to jump in on this one.
Building crafting is a free formed "cubed" based with multiple material types and a is a tiered progression tied to your crafting equipment (workstations).  As you improve those workstations, you gain access to better stuff to make, very straight forward and simple to get started in.
Early game is about survival, mid-to-later game play is fortifying, and all of it builds up to trying to take (or defend) the crown for the kingdom.
While yes, you'll run into those folks who simply want to watch the world burn, you'll also encounter those who want to achieve something more, and this game allows both to reside mostly side-by-side, while allowing you the convenience to play (mostly) how you like.
Just keep in mind, at its heart, this is a PVP game that is really focused on the group vs. group mechanics, and there is no solo player mode without hosting your own private server.  So you can play solo if you really want, but you're honestly missing out on more than 50% of the game doing so.

This game is great. Its the first and still the best of all space RTS games. For an RTS, I know only few games that have a better campaign. Homeworld set the bar for space RTS. The music and sound effects are beautifully atmospheric, the storyline to the campaign is subtly laid out and you find yourself fully invested by the end. The way it makes use of three-dimensional space, as well as the aesthetic design is simply superb. The Remastered collection updates the classic to make the most of modern hardware, and is visually spectacular. There are some foibles and let downs - such as scaling the HUD to look right on a 1440p Ultrawide monitor just isn't happening. But overall I'd still recommend this edition whether you know the original and want to revisit it, or just enjoy RTS games more generally.

As a hardcore Alien fan i was excited to play a game like Isolation, which is loosely based on the original Alien (1979), and i was not disappointed. Isolation offers a great survival experience, as you step into a Nostromo-like vessel against different kinds of enemies. Unlike previous Alien (or AVP) titles, the developers did their best and delivered us a well designed game. Personally, i think it's the best entry of the entire Alien franchise.
The flight recorder of the Nostromo was discovered, 15 years after the disappearance of the vessel. It is located on a ship called Anesidora, on the Sevastopol remote space station. Amanda Ripley, daughter of Ellen Ripley, hoping to gain knowledge about her mother's fate, follows 2 Weyland - Yutani members in the station, which is not inhabited only by humans.
Took me about 18 hours to finish the Campaign. The time someone needs to complete Survival Mode missions can't be calculated
An atmospheric stealth - suvrival horror game that gives you the Alien experience better than any Alien game / movie. The atmospheric and realistic gameplay make you feel like a crew member. The first horror title of the entire Alien franchise leaves a very positive opinion, despite the existence of some not-so-minor drawbacks.
+ Graphics are as good as they get, and the game's requirements are not high at all.
+ The sound effects are the crown jewel. A masterpiece. Sound is essential in a horror game's design, and Isolation designers nailed it. Not only the main sounds are great, but also the random vents / steps are so realistic that can give you a heart attack. The voice acting was not equally great, though.
+ The environment of the Sevastopol was also good. Well designed interiors that remind us of the Nostromo, detailed enough to assist the other parts of the game give it a totally realistic look. Everything in the game are inspired by the original movie, and this is obvious with a closer look at the items in the game like the save devices, the computers, the motion sensor. Isolation even has the dusty look of the movie.
+ The gameplay was satisfying. Mostly hide & seek with some action parts, but generally, you can choose your approach and the enemies will repsond accordingly. There are also some minigames you complete via hacking PDA / cutting tools.
+ A variety of weapons and stuff to use, but with barely enough ammo to make you feel safe, and they are to be used with caution.
+ The AI is good(ish). There are many ways off a difficult situation, most of them via your inventory, and the enemies will respond accordingly.
+ Survival Mode. Kinda compensates the absent multiplayer. You start of with some equipment / weapons, with a time limit and some objectives. It is fast paced.

- The story is poor. A side story which as nothing to the franchise. Also, the plot is totally predictable, with some exceptions. This does not make the game less scary, but some horror games have more interesting plots
- The AI is not functioning correctly at some points. Sometimes enemies can spot you even if you hide in the darkest corner of the room and at the same time cant hear your steps 1 meter behind them. At some other points, the Alien will walk around your exact location even if it doesnt know you are there, won't give a damn about the flare you threw as a distraction while at other points will spot a flare 3 rooms away with a huge delay. This AI mulfunction can provoke the following.
- Boring gameplay from time to time. The AI problems might make you end up hiding in a closet or under a desk for several minutes, only to die by the time the enemy finally spots you. Also, the ammount of deaths you will experience is too damn high. Possibly the major problem of the game. Barely 20 hours of gameplay cant normally make you feel bored. That's the only reason the vast majority of people didnt even complete the game (The achievement you get for completing the story is owned only by 5% of the owners of the game).
- The price, especially for DLCs. Absent multiplayer, with only one survival mission, 50 euros (and another 50 for the DLCs which double the game time) are probably a lot. But it's still worth it.
Concluding, this game is worth buying, if you can afford it. If you cant, grab it on sale
