I have an interest in sailing and bought this game as a way to familiarize myself with sailing and its basic concepts. I am 5 hours in and while I understand that is not a lot of time, I have scratched the surface and would like to give a perspective of a beginner. The tutorials aren't the best that I've experienced as they tend to throw a lot of information at you all at once, however they do give you the most basic concepts of sailing and allow you to start sailing on your own, once you start sailing you will receive tips on how to adjust the sails all the way up to advanced mode. There is an "auto-sail" option that gives you only the power to steer the ship. The game is online 100% of the time, once you start the game you are launched straight to your sailboat which keeps sailing whether you are online or offline (unless you anchor). There are auto-navigation options which keep your boat on the proper path to continue your voyage. You will receive e-mails with information on your ships heading, speed, etc.
Overall I have enjoyed this game so far, keep in mind that it is EA and there are minor bugs and glitches.
My only major complaint is the fact that the speech filter is EXTREMELY restrictive. It is like the gestapo on steroids, words like "hell" and "stupid" will get you banned. The developers say that they want the chat to remain "safe" and "friendly" but I see the speech restriction as over the top and unnecessary.

I will still recommend this game to others, but I find it a bit to difficult

This game is a great resource management/base building/upgrading game. Starting out gathering resources by hand, you quickly move onto ridiculous levels of automation as you delve deeper and deeper into the tech tree. This game has already brought me hours of entertainment before it was released on Steam, and I imagine it will continue to do so for years to come.

You notice that your laser turret production is a bit slow so you decide to hunt down the problem.  You note that the limiting resource is steel, so you go to find that some of your steel smelters are low on coal because one of your mines is depleted.  Next thing you know everything is rigged to petroleum, it's 7 in the morning and you have class in 30 minutes.  This is one of those games.

I cannot even describe how itchy this game makes me to keep playing. No matter how much you play, there's always at least a few unresolved loose ends that you're trying to resolve. Finally resolve one production issue and two more present themselves, not to mention the fact that one of your primary resources starts to dry up, giving you yet another problem to solve. You'll finally get a particular, very satisfying production line set up, only to discover that the throughput on something it depends on is way too low, so then you go to fix that up and get it upgraded and improved, only to realise you're having issues in another area, and perhaps you have everything you need to solve it right away, except you've crowded yourself into a tight space, forcing you to reconsider your approach and rework parts of your layout... but now your iron is running out and that means you're not producing steel, which means your ammo isn't getting produced, which means those turrets aren't keeping the base safe from aliens, so now you need to go and attack the enemy to get to that iron patch they're infesting.... but it's too far away, so you'll need to get a train running to and from it... and so on. Once the game grabs you, it doesn't let go. Do not play if you have work you need to be doing!

4 years in development, and it's only average at best, mediocre at worst.
I'll start with the good things about this game. For a Sonic game, it looks very clean and very nice. The soundtrack is nice with some standout hits (Fist Bump), and it has an interesting premise for the plot. Also, the character creator is simple, yet a neat addition, giving just enough options to create a good looking character (or an abomination with a spring for a head) to be used as a major part of the story. However, that's all the good I can say about this game.
Sonic Forces, as a game, is mediocre. Most of the stages see you going through a straight line with some slight variations here and there, and while it does deliver the sense of speed, this game offers no challenge at all. Modern Sonic's stages consist of constantly using the boost to run through everything and reach the end of the stage, Classic Sonic's stages are very bland, offering very few branching pathways and challenging obstacles (and even an autoscroller in one level), and the Avatar stages basically play like the Modern Sonic stages, just without the boost, and instead the multiple wisps, but you can only use one wisp at a time depending on what weapon you equip. To top that off, the control and physics in this game seem less precise and responsive compared to that of Colors and Generations, arbitrarily making the game harder to play. Still, the worst part of the gameplay (or really just the level design) has to be the abruptly short length of the stages. On average, it will only take you 2 minutes tops to finish one stage, and there's only 30 including the bosses.
The gameplay isn't the only thing that suffers here. While the plot has an interesting premise, reversing the roles as Eggman starts off on the winning side, the plot itself and everything that happens in the game is just a mess. There's also optional collectibles and missions you can complete. The collectibles see you finding the red star rings again, as well as the returning number rings from Sonic Lost World that you must collect in order, and the new silver moon rings that you must collect in time before they dissapear. The missions, on the other hand, see you performing different tasks, from remedial stuff such as equipping specific gear or performing certain moves in certain stages, to even some timed challenges.
The collectibles are mostly pointless, besides getting the achievements for the 100%. While the red star rings unlock extra, slightly more challenging stages to play, the number rings and moon rings unlock nothing but achievements. As for the missions, your reward for completing the missions is more parts to customize your avatar with, so they at least have some purpose, despite some of the challenges requiring near perfect play to complete. There's also the free DLC Episode Shadow, but this DLC only emphasizes the problems mentioned above.
Overall, this game was pretty dissapointing. Nothing about it is completely awful, but it mainly ranges from bad to just OK. If you really want to try this game for yourself, wait until the price drops, or for the game to go on sale because this game isn't worth $40. You're better off buying 2 copies of Sonic Mania on 2 different consoles to show SEGA where the money's at. However, if you're looking for a good Sonic game that features the boost gameplay, you'll want to play Sonic Colors or Sonic Generations instead, by the off chance you haven't already.

To preface: My opinion on most 3D Sonics post-Dreamcast are of middling-to-apathetic in nature. While they have never properly hit it home, there is at least a base level of mediocry I can expect and enjoy from the titles (with Colors/Generations being the very enjoyable outliers.)
While, once again, there are tiny things here and there to be enjoyed for the title, such as the much different pace of the Avatar gameplay - very stop and go, but not as bad as preview media made it seem - and a sample selection of great songs as usual, Sonic Forces is disappointing in not being bad, but in being specifically bad in its own series' defined terms.
Dreadful level design, a story that becomes very wrote and uninteresting the more details you get and an ultimately disappointing customization system for the Avatar character lead to a game that, some how, leaves me wanting to play Sonic Lost World - comparatively just as uninteresting and bland, but it at least does mediocrity with a wildly new system in play. This only takes what some have come to expect and fall even further than that.
At most a sale in the far flung future, but you can honestly get just as much playing through Generations a second time instead of this.

This is my first time writing a review so...don't kill me :V
The game is short. Really short. With the free DLC included, I clocked in around 5 hours for the main story (with doing a bit extra on the side). For a 40 dollar game to have such a short playtime, it is really going to turn many away especially considering that Colors (and even Generations) offered so much more for what they were worth. The devs designed the game so that you continually replayed the same levels for hidden items such as red rings or to get a higher score in order to get more unlockables for your custom character.
Thing is, the level design is...questionable. Some stages are really fun but others are just boring especially when you're playing as Modern Sonic. Boost gameplay has led to some divisive opinions on the fanbase and while I do enjoy it, they really went overboard with the boost in this game. A majority of stages can be played just by holding down the button and letting the automated sections do the work. Actual interaction with the game is minimal and they try to hide it through QTEs and the graphics (which admitedly look absolutely beautiful). With that said, the game felt like it TRIED to be another Sonic Colors but failed in that department and created a game with three different playstyles with none of them being fully fleshed out due to how short and pathetically easy the stages are. With that said, I don't mind replaying stages, but I just want the stages to be fun.
I won't be spoiling the story but it was decent for what it was. There were a bunch of cheesy moments throughout but there were plenty of moments where it was fun to watch. A big problem was pacing since they had a habit of throwing everything at you in such a short amount of time. Many aspects about the story could have been fleshed out more (ESPECIALLY Infinite's character) and would have made the game much longer overall. To me, the story felt like a Saturday morning cartoon but I did not hate it by any means.
If I had to give it a score, I would probably give it a 5/10 at its absolute worst and a 7.5 at it's best. Is it worth the 40 dollars? I don't think so, but it wasn't an awful game by any means and there are parts that I enjoyed immensly. I do recommend the game if you're that curious about it, but it'd be best if you waited for it to go on sale.

Papers, Please, Lucas Pope's masterpiece, is my favourite game of all time. Because that's a rather grand statement, I'm going to analyse it from several directions, to fully convey my reasoning.
-MUSIC-
The opening theme of Papers, Please is clever. Very clever. It's use of heavily synthesised instruments harmonises with the early PC-game aesthetic, creating a very comforting, almost nostalgic feeling. It's memorable, instantly recognisable, and effective. Furthermore, the citation sound effect (yes I'm including that in music) has given me recurring nightmares. It is the sound that makes me sit up straight, that makes the hairs stand up on the back of my neck. The only sound to do that beforehand, is the noise that is made when Snake gets spotted and an exclamation mark appears above your head.
-GAMEPLAY-
It's challenging to make something simple seem complex. It is to my great pleasure, therefore, for me to say this game is complex. Not only is this game complex, but it's hard. My god this is difficult. I'd say for a £6.99 game, this is one of the games which I have been most satisfied with the playtime. For those unaware of the game's key focus, you are challenged to match up different pieces of information on peoples passports, identity cards and tickets in a border control booth. If you spot any discrepancies, you don't let the person through. It's really that simple. When it comes to the later levels, you realise that it really isn't that simple. Juggling up to 10 documents is honestly a nightmare, whilst simultaneously being aware of storyline characters to look out for.
-STORY-
Papers, Please is a choice-based story-driven game. Based on who you allow through the border and what you do with the money you earn, you can unlock 1 of multiple endings. Some of these include the destruction of the border, being imprisoned, and becoming the member of a secret order and escaping with members of your family. Because of the authenticity of this iron-curtain-esque atmosphere, you will be affected by this game as if it's a real environment. This higher power of dictators and leaders is constantly looming over you, along with the anticipation of war. One of the many beauties of this game is that it strongly limits the amount of information given about the reasons for immigration to Arstotzka, leaving it both up to your imagination, and your ability to pick up on subtle hints to decide why. It's an incredibly delicate story about an incredibly brutal topic.
-CONCLUSION-
In my opinion, Papers, Please is one of the greatest games ever made. This will always be criticised as an opinion, largely due to the fact that it's a relatively short indie game with very humble-looking graphics and simple coding. It's not a feat of technological greatness, but it is an prime example of what gaming should be. It's a work of art, and my favourite game of all time. If you can manage to buy it, then do so. It's a game to be savoured and appreciated over a length of time, and by as many people as possible.
Papers, Please - 10/10

So, it's been quite some time since the release of Rome II total war, and this is begging the question. IS the game worth it? let's take a look
Rome II total war (emperor edition) is one of the latest installments in the franchise (only behind total war warhammer, I WILL NEVER ACCEPT ATTILA) in which the base game still retains it's core roots, but has since had many changes to "streamline" the game. It seems more like a rome I total war with better graphics but it has it's own unique changes. some are♥♥♥♥♥♥poor, some are pretty ok. so lets take a look at the list:
Pros:
after years of patching i can finally play this game without crashing
multiplayer is fun, multiplayer campaign is one of the best experiences (when you dont desync)
Map is vibrant and entertaining, It also retains the beautiful strategy setup
you finally have a garrison defending your cities for free, no more -2000 income every turn
province system is balanced enough (no longer must you suffer waiting 3 turns to get all your siege equipment)
edicts are a good balancer for your food money or upkeep, though you have to ask why this was needed
i like the idea of slums developing when you leave a plot in a province capital/town empty, it keeps you active in all your settlements meaning your empire and you are efficient
UI is beautifully done, you finally know your♥♥♥♥♥♥br>
the cinematic camera is perfect for youtubers or if you want that epic shot
mods (especially radious) make this game a blast! everything you want is there
scenario/historic battles are better now (the AI tries it's best to follow what the actual leaders  did in that battle)
i can finally employ diplomatic relations without the ♥♥♥♥ing diplomat agent (makes diplomacy less tedious, encouraging you to establish relations and treatis)
Cons:
it took years of patching to play this game without crashing
If you don't have good internet connection you're ♥♥♥♥ed in multiplayer
DLC (although adiquate) is overpriced, STOP DOING THIS SEGA
AI is worse than a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ baby trying to eat a fork (you can steamroll over everyone in the game)
AI doesn't bother to make alliances when they see they're getting♥♥♥♥♥♥♥br>
AI will not be logical in diplomatic relations (even if they have -1000 gold per turn they will not begin trading)
Battles are easy as hell, on legendary only the stats increase, not the intelligence
You need to use edicts just to balance the game (really?)
Agents literally have no use except in either decimating the enemy army, something only the spy can do or improve your troops, something only the champion can do
Your generals aren't memorable, "oh look my rank 8 general died? oh no! wait, what was his name?" It makes your battles less epic as you can't make your own scenario without mixing up the generals
There is no senate system at all (completely removed!) this was one thing i felt was awesome about rome I and now it's not here, It's instead replaced by Imperium and your popularity (imperium is somewhat mediocre but the popularity system sucks)
Final Verdict:
6.4/10 Good game, but in desperate need of AI improvement and the return of some features.
PS:
i decided to leave it at 6.4 instead of 7.0 becuase of the insane prices of DLC, which while i'm not at all opposed to, should not be so expensive so that i spent twice as much on DLC than on the base game.

I've been sailing 22-53 foot sail boats since I was a kid. I've looked at different boat/ship simulators for years, but never particularly bothered with any of them. I've sort of given up on simulating boats, let alone sailing. Then this indie release comes along! I've just finished my first hour of sailing, and I'm mighty impressed!
You get that wonderful gratification when the sound (instantly recognizable) of the water and sails let you know that you've filled the sails properly. Constant fine tuning of the sheets, getting that cozy feeling when the tell tales point straight back - it feels authentic!
The tutorials are great, and even though I've sailed short handed for 15 years, this simulator instantly convinced me I can practise my skills at home and actually have it improve my sailing in real life.
Can't wait to see the progress of this title! Looking forward to having more people out on the water so that I can go amateur racing, or simply pair up for some recreational sailing. :)
Easily worth the money, even though I can understand why non-sailors may think there's lacking detail when you get close to the shore. I'm sure that will improve. But if you respect the difficulties involved in making sailing simulation feel authentic, you will agree that the developer has focused on the most important core aspects of sailing, and you will certainly enjoy the game even at this early stage.
Awesome sailing game!

If you like sailing then this is a must buy. I have always wanted a sailing game that you can literally sail around the world. However you can teleport to where you want to start your voyage or join other friends online on a sailing trip or race. This is EA so there is still some polishing to be done but works well out of the box so to speak.
If you think sailing on open water will get boring, try racing or challenges. Sailing on auto-mode where all you have to do is steer does get boring, but the fun is learning how to get the best out of your sails and steer the boat into the best angle against the wind. And racing, especially long races can be like a chess game where you have to plot your course and choose when to tack and using other web-apps to get forecast weather/wind to help make decisions. The game does use online weather data. Another feature i like is the ambient sound effects is nice, it doesnt sound like looped sfx which would get grating, but varies on waves and wind, it can be quite relaxing if you are plodding a long due to low wind and hearing the water lap against the boat.
The tips you get in the game can be contradictory at times which are real time when changes need to be made, i think sometimes the conditions are on the borderline where two conditions could be true and thats why you get two tips that seem to be polar opposites- but you still learn from them. But eventually you relie on the Trim tab on the navigation panel where you can see the shape of your sails and suggestions as to how to improve them and use that as your guide once you get the hang of things.
Besides multiplayer and being able to chat to other players ingame i like the option to go offline and have the Ai sail you boat which is a must for long races where you need to log off to sleep or do RL stuff in between sailing, however the Ai wont sail the boat as well as player who does so manually and knows what they are doing. Which in a way balances out nicely for long races. This game only currently has three boats, but more will come and improved visuals for land and water. You cannot currently go inside the cabin but has a possibility to be added in the future.

TL;DR: If you don't have money problems and love hunting games, then this is the one to get! If that isn't the case, then look for something else.
The Hunter is amazing, but not very noob friendly. Basically as a free player you can only hunt 2 types of animals (and you don't have the correct weapon/ammo to hunt one of those types). When I began playing the game didn't tell me this or let me know where I should hunt and what I could hunt for that matter. After some frustrating hours of running around I figured it out and started hunting Mule Deer. I did this for a few days until I got tired of hunting the same animal over and over again. I really enjoyed the game though, so I saved up money to buy the 12 month subscription and more importantly get a bow to hunt with. I've had a lot of fun with the game since then and I look forward to playing even more in the future.
There is one problem though, and it's a big one. The pricing is ridiculous. Every single weapon in the game costs money and the same goes for items, equipment and clothes. The subscription packages sets you up with some decent starting equipment, but it's really too bad that you have to pay more money to try out other hunting possibilities. Personally I think it would work better if you were able to earn currency to buy all these things for for every animal you harvest, because the current missions are way too slow for this. A system similar to that seen in Mass Effect 3's multiplayer where you can buy crates with random goodies would also be a great way to introduce players to the game. But again this is only if players were able to gain ingame currency faster than what the current solution offers.
This is all just my opinion though. I will enjoy my subscription while it lasts, but I will not be re-subscribing when it runs out. I don't feel that I get enough for my money.

This review will have spoilers so be warned
So let's start off with the story, It isnt good. It's trying to be way too serious for a sonic game, the pacing is way too fast and it feels unfinished. We find out sonic is kidnapped and presumed dead, literally just a few seconds later we get "SONIC IS ALIVE." It feels so random. Infinite is cool but disappointing, And it feels like he just kinda disappears, so i do hope we see him in another game later. The characters don't question what happens to him, then when they beat eggman, eggman is nowhere to be seen and they do not talk about it. This is what i meant when i said it feels unfinished, there is still stuff left unanswered. Like, how did eggman even get this far? He had already basically taken over the world before they met Infinite, what was sonics team doing then?
Alright, moving onto gameplay now.
Its pretty great, Modern sonic and the avatar respond really well, they feel good and have pretty nice levels, while the maps are somewhat short and linear they are a lot of fun to play on and they look great.
Then theres classic sonic that feels shoehorned into the game, you could remove him and nothing would change, but he is here and you have to deal with it, He feels really bad, he feels slow and clunky and is by far the worst part about the gameplay.
Any other things i want to talk about
Music is great, so many good original and remixed songs, definitely one of the best things about the game
The character creator doesnt feel great, theres a lot of different items to make your character look original and all but they look really out of place compared to the other characters.
Plenty of side missions to do, which is cool but most of them are just doing a level all over again
The wispons were a cool idea and work well, but theyre pretty useless, they all tear through enemies so easily, the only one worth using is the first one you get (The fire gun) because it doesnt slow you down when you use it and it kills enemies instantly
TLDR pros and cons
Pros:
Fun gameplay
Looks great and feels great
All of the music
Other characters are heavily involved in the story and that is awesome
Boss fights are really fun
Cons:
Classic sonic
Wispons are pretty useless
Levels are really short
Story feels too edgy,fast, and incomplete
Tails sucks (what the hell happened to him?)
Classic sonic again
So why am i recommending a game with this many faults?
It's fun, though the game has its issues it was still a fun game to play and i absolutely do not regret my purchase. Though maybe if you buy it you should wait for it to go on sale, Either way, i hope you enjoy it whether you are reading this before or after playing.

As a long time Sonic fan who's played all the games, I was actually pleased with this game. There's areas that really bug me though. For example the game could've been so much more than what we got. Levels should've been a lot longer and the game in general should've had more levels. Another thing that hindered this game was that they tried crossing its story with Mania's and it had Classic Sonic. Classic Sonic sticks out really oddly in the game. Most of his stages aren't greatly designed and are just eh. He feels like he shouldn't belong story and gameplay wise. Classic Sonic also controls worse than he did in Generations which is really odd. You think the controls would be better considering its Sonic Team's second attempt at this style of Classic Sonic. While we're on the controls I think I should mention Modern Sonic is more akin to Colors which didn't feel as great as Generations. He's fine In terms of Control Custom Character is the most fun to play as. He's slippery but I've never really had that be a problem for me. Honestly looking back on it, Custom Character is the best part in the game. His stages are a lot of fun, have the best music, and its really fun to customize him.  Modern Sonic is pretty fun as well and has some great stages. I also love how you can play as Shadow in Sonic levels. Tag Team stages were a blast especially the one near the end. I would say while this game isn't a stand out amazing game like Generations or Mania, I had fun with it still. I would recommend this to any Sonic fan who likes the boost formula games and wants a short fun little experience. I would say if you're on the fence about it, wait for a price drop. The game would probably be better at a $20 or $30 price to be honest.

I'm in disbelief that this game was developed by the Colors and Generations team. Level design is featureless, controls handle like an inarticulate robot, game mechanics provide scarcely a choice when it comes to freedom and how to approach a situation. I would not give Sega my money for this. After Mania, I guess two good Sonic games in a row was too much to ask for...?

I'm a long-time, die-hard Sonic fan and will tell you right now: don't buy this game.
It's an utter disappointment in nearly every way save for graphical fidelity and Eggman's character as a legitimate villain once again as opposed to the bumbling oaf he somehow morphed into after 06.
I only have 2.5 hours on record because that's how long it took to beat it. The level design is utterly mindless and you'll either win without knowing what you did or blast off of some ledge into a pit you couldn't see coming. If you thought boost gameplay from Generations and Unleashed was mindless and dull, I promise you this is far worse. The boss fights were laughably easy, and there's not even a final fight with super forms! Hell, the Chaos Emeralds aren't mentioned at all! Shame, Sonic Team.
My Switch and Odyssey are right next to me, and I have all the desire to play and 100% it, as opposed to zero desire to even fire this sack of crap back up again. It doesn't seem like Sonic will ever stand up to Mario like the days of old at this rate.
Worse yet the game is tied to Sonic Mania (a great game not developed by Sonic Team) and the plot is all over the place, filled with holes and head-scratcher moments. The tie-in was unnecessary and puts Mania in a bad light. Further, the powers of these Phantom Ruby things is entirely different between both games: in one it manipulates time and space like the Chaos Emeralds, and in the other it just project illusions. Why the inconsistency? There are so many bad choices here!
Wanna fight Chaos? Too bad, he's only in a cutscene as an illusion. How did Silver get there? 06 never happened, right? Who is Infinite? Why does he just disappear at the end? How can this game be so bad in almost every way?
Classic and Modern Sonic really shouldn't be separate entities with different plots, but that's going to be the new thing now because of Generations it seems. There's a hint of the two Sonics coming together again in the future, but let's hope they don't do this ever again.
As a final note, the Sonic series has always been known for having a fantastic soundtrack and this game failed incredibly hard at having anything memorable in the music department. It's sad because so much effort was put into composing and writing lyrics for a number of the stages, but they're all annoying, butt-rocky, distracting, and unnecessary. Yes, the sun is falling from the sky. No, I don't want to hear you telling me about it in song. Nothing from this game is going in my playlists. Where was Crush 40 and other composers like Tomoya Ohtani? Out to lunch because they saw how bad this game was going to suck?
At the end of the day you could argue that 06 would have been better than this game had it actually been finished as it was originally planned to have been. 06 had great ideas that were never brought to full fruition because of a stupid marketing decision that ended up trashing Sonic's reputation by releasing the game far too early. This game on the other hand has bad ideas that were given to time to culminate into an entire game based around them, and no one at SEGA seemed to think that there was anything wrong with whatever the design team came up with, now called Sonic Forces.
Next time actually play your games and see how fun they are before releasing them, Sonic Team. If you thought this was fun, if you thought this was a game that everyone would enjoy, then you need to quit your job and find something else to do for a career, because keeping this up will eventually turn even the oldest of fans like myself against you. Faith shaken.

I haven't sailed now for 17 years, but I used to love racing dinghy's as a teenager. One of my biggest desires in life is in fact to get out n the water again.
This game, it brought back all the memories of sailing for me - even though the boats in this game are very different to those I had experience with, it manages to replicate the motion in the water so well, and the level of detain in the simulation is stunning.
It's still a little rough around the edges, the oceans are a little featureless and the water surface doesn't show the wind, so you can't read it to plot your course, but this early access title is already exceptional value for money, if you value a realistic sailing experience.
I easily and wholeheartedly reccomend this game to any experienced sailors who want to dig into a detailed simulation. For those who maybe want to learn to sail, it could be a useful tool, but only in support of other ways to learn, although the detail in the tutorials suggests the dev does want this to be a tool that teaches new sailors too. Don't expect to have dolphins zipping through the water with you, to see land as much more than a dark strip in the distance, or to stride around your boat while your crew sing shanties. It is right now, an avatarless experience, you won't see anything other than the sea and boats - and even if some of the spectacular stuff does get added, with the attention to the simulation the dev has given this title, expect it to be work to get that experience.

What A Feeling!
This sim captures so much of the special essence of sailing.  There are visceral elements involved, whether racing or cruising:  a tilted deck, pitching and rolling, interaction between wind and waves.
Here's one that sailors will instictively remember:  You're on a broad reach, heeling a bit, creating the usual hull wave, moving at say 7 kts in your 38 foot ocean cruiser.  Then you quickly turn downwind.  The boat...and horizon...level out with a WHOOSH of waterline spray, the wind noise drops down, and the wave you had been pushing along moves off...then the following wave picks you up; after pitching backwards for a couple of moments you gently pitch forward...then back.  A very visceral feeling.  I'm describing the game right now.
If you're a sailor, you'll definitely want to give this one a try.  For non-sailors, there's enough detailed tutorials and hints to start you sailing immediately.  You can't go wrong; the in-game boats are keelboats and cannot capsize.  If the winds get too big, you just heel over until everything is in balance.  (You can also reef the sails of course.)
Before I "took the plunge" and purchased this great (soon to be legendary) sim, I was concerned about the few things it maybe could not do.  Now, I'm more amazed by the things it does well already:
1.  Smooth, largely issue-free gameplay
2.  Persistent world.  Exit game, your boat keeps going on the course you set, or even follows the waypoints you set down
3.  Wind and wave dynamics
4.  Realistic weather, based (I think) on current conditions worldwide.
5. And social interactions!  You can for instance teleport your boat alongside anyone else and have a casual chat, meet fellow sailors from around the world.  You can even chat with sailors on the other side of the world and compare notes on current conditions.
Even though this game is in early access, it does everything I've described seamlessly.  Much kudos to the dev(s)!

I'm a sailor and a gamer and finally these two things have combined well in a sailing simulator. I have many a bad sailing games before and at long last this game has actual potental.
Sailaway is definitely a bit rough around the edges, a little buggy, a slightly awkward UI, fairly primitive racing, and land masses that look straight out of the early 90s, BUT as an early access game its enduring to see that the things that really matter are already rock solid. The boats are gorgeous, wind and water mechanics are realistic, and sail shape is everything.
Oh, and did I mention the real world weather?! Do you know how cool it is to check real world wind reports to find your ideal spot in the game??? You don't now, but you could....
If you had ever been interested in a serious sailing simulator, I wouldn't hesitate to pick this one up.

Firstly, this is an early access game, and it's still in very early alpha. The development team is one (very clever) programmer. I mention this so people know the risks and that development will be slow, and the game sometimes buggy. Kerbal took a decade to get where it is now, after all.
Secondly, this is a realtime and realistic simulation. There is no altering the time of day, there is no sailing at 500 knots (although you can telepot your boat), there are no AI ships to race against, there is no downloading the content. An active internet connect is needed. FPS players might be bored, until they realise how good sailing is.
Thirdly it is first person, and there are no avatars. You can have crew on your ship, and friends who buy the game can join you, and you can talk but you won't see them.
This is not a game for sightseeing, you don't really sail to admire the generic landscape. This is a game for sailing, as close to possible to as real life as can be simulated. Thousands of miles of rolling ocean waves, storms, gusting winds, the spray of water in your face, bad weather, sea sickness and all the other joys of sailing.
Perfect for anyone who already sails, or people who are very keen on sailing. Your ship sails the seven seas and oceans of the world *in realtime*, it could take a year or more to sail around the world if  you are game to try.
The game is linked to the NOAA data feeds so you experience the actual real wave period and depth, windspeed and direction, plus the time of day of your ships position - as if you were really there.
Easy enough for a beginner, the game also offers a good challenge for the advanced sailor. I've also found on most fine days this is also a great game to have next to you all day long as you do other things - just watch it every now and again to make sure your ship is on course and your sails trimmed.
The online community is nice, friendly people with a lot of combined sailing knowledge. They are not the normal grumpy and complaining people seen in other games.
I recommend it, but please be very sure of those points I made before.

It's really hard to convey with words what makes this game interesting. On the surface, this game feels exactly as if you were doing real life work:
- You get a job.
- You are assigned your tasks.
- They feel like a chore.
- You screw up
- You get reprimanded
- Your responsibilities grow, while your salary stays the same
However, throw in the realities of having a 6 member family to provide for, and it starts getting complicated. Fail to bring home enough money and some family members may have to starve, or freeze. If one of them is sick, you may have to choose between medicine, food, or heating. Will you take bribes then to offset these costs? Will you cooperate with terrorists to get a pay cut? Will you try to get through that gate as many people as you can, since you get paid by the person?
At first it's really easy to make these desicions since you have no sense of what's really going on. After the first few hours go by, and you're grinding along day after day, you start to feel more like playing the character. You start to feel compassion for some of the pixelated people that desperately beg for entry. You start to make judgement calls based on how your family is doing. The game begins to develop into an extremely interesting experience where you're constantly being morally tested.
The game has about 20 or 30-something outcomes (can't remember off the top of my head). So far I've managed to see about 9 of them. Every time I finish I'm finding new paths and possibilities to explore in order to see where the story goes. This is one of the 10 best experiences I've had with video games this year, and I wholeheartedly recommend you give this one a chance.

I have played steam games for roughly 1,154 hours. Although this is not nearly close to others, this amount of time has collected vast amounts of memories both hilarious and frustrating (thanks CSGO). In those 1,154 hours, the 30 that I dedicated to this "early access game" are the most unique, interesting, and addicitve hands down.
-Science
Factorio is a sandbox game that proves to constantly introduce new goals to its audience. This is accomplished by its diverse and intuitive research dynamic. By progressing in the game, new items and structures are introduced allowing the player to further expand his/her creation through automation. Not only is this aspect of the game balanced, but it progesses the game at a pace which keeps you glued to the screen needing one more minute. I don't want to go into detaill about how science is made and such since this is only a review, but the main point I want to make is that this base gameplay experience is extremely addictive and makes the game aweome as a whole.
-Combat
Not only is combat relatively rare in these types of games, but if it is implemented, it is not oftenly made well. Let me tell you, Factorio is different. The fighting in this game is extremely balanced with the player not too weak or too strong in comparison to enemies. Instead, Factorio allows the player to research new military technologies to combat evolving natives that threaten their factory. Due to the constant growth rate of enemies and military strength, the game provides the player with a relatively constant need to stay alert and defend their base. By doing this, Factorio seperates from other automation and resource managing games by including two objectives: Automation and killing angry natives.
-Automation
Put simply, Factorio presents automation as one of the most fluid concepts the player has to learn. In Factorio, the player is forced to use their own imaginitive ideas in combination with the game-built designs in order to create an efficient factory. Although this may take a few tries and possibly a quick search on youtube, the feeling of accomplishment after automating a certain process is extremely rewarding unlike any other game I have played.
-Tutorial/Learning curve
An essential part of any game is teaching the audience how to play. Although the built-in tutorial teaches basic aspects of the game, I feel that in order to make a late-game factory, a player is forced to consult other resources for advice. This small, but critical characteristic is immensely important for casual gamers, but will most certainly be addressed during the full release of the game.
-End Goal
Like other reviewers, I feel the need for a greater end goal for Facotrio. I will keep this negative short though since the develpoers are working on this issue for the full release.
-Conclusion
In conclusion, Facotorio is most definitely an immensely polished game that deserves 100% positive reviews. The moddability and interaction with the community simply adds onto the already amazing game making it a masterpiece. Please do yourself a facor and play the free demo so that you can experience this fluid-like gameplay like the rest of us.

Okay, this was originally a thumbs down review, but I rethought that
This is a thumbs up for the Homeworld classic portion of the Homeworld Remastered Collection, which I picked up on sale for about $11. While the original Homeworld (HW) is an actual classic that, almost 20 years on, is still worth picking up, I wouldn't give a thumbs up for the Remastered (HWRM) collection at its full $35 retail price. If you want details on why, feel free to read on. Otherwise, do yourself a favor and pick up the collection on sale if you've never had a chance to play the original.
There are some pros to the Remastered collection. It is absolutely gorgeous, with incredibile ship models, effects and phenomenal new environments and backgrounds. The audio is cleaned up, which lets you appreciate even more the great voice acting (I liked the somewhat scratchy quality of the original, as it contributed to the underdog space navy feel, but to each their own). And the Homeworld 2 engine, which the Remaster is based on, has a generally much better UI than original Homeworld.
Sadly, the switch to the HW2 engine also fundamentally alters the core Homeworld gameplay experience. It's not unplayble or anything, but it isn't nearly as satisfying and I frequently felt like I was fighting my units behavior than having their behavior fight for me.
The first and most obvious change is that formations are broken down into smaller subformations. In Homeworld, if you had, say, 20 Ion Frigates in a wall, the whole 20 ships would form into a 4x5 grid and react as a single, large entity. In HWRM, there appears to be a max unit limit for each type of formation, so that 20 ship wall becomes two 10 unit walls. This may not sound like a big deal, but when coupled with the fact that the HWRM engine treats each of these 10 walls as seperate entities, you start to get real problems. Yes, each subformation will stay as a wall and focus fire on the same target when given the attack command, but in the absence of orders each subformation reacts independently according to whatever base stance you have set. So in the aggressive or neutral stances, it is entirely possible for half of that 20 unit wall formation to wander off to attack an enemy in range and for the other half to never respond at all because the actions of the first subgroup meant the second subgroup never encountered the enemy. This makes fighter groups extremely difficult to control, because you need lots of fighters or bombers to make these units an effective threat, but in the new engine that just ensures there are even more subformations responding independently of each other. In every skirmish match I played eventually my fighter groups would get hopelessly spread out, ensuring that the fighters functioned substantially less effectively than they should.
The second, and far more problematic issue, is that some formation interactions and all the stances no longer work correctly. In particular, the sphere formation is completely broken. In HW, setting a sphere of units to guard or attack a ship meant that the whole formation would spread out until it was a big ball either surrounding and protecting the ship, or pouring fire into it. In HWRM, if you have a sphere of fighters guarding, say, a resource collecter, instead what happens is that the group of fighters just follows the resource collecter - as a little ball. Instead of enveloping a ship to attack it, now that ball will just make multiple firing sweeps against the enemy - as a little ball. This yet further reduces the usefulness of some of the strike craft and support ships.
As for the stances, in HW aggressive stance units would stay in their formation no matter what, in neutral they would juke around a little, and in evasive mode they might break the entire formation to avoid incoming fire. Each had its uses. However, in HWRM, aggressive now means the formation will attack anything in range, until there are no more targets remaining. Neutral is now defensive, meaning units will attack if fired up, pursuing the enemy for a fairly large distance, and then return to position. The evasive stance is now passive, which means the formation will remain in formation and never return fire under any circumstances (there is still an evasive behavior, but it's really not the same thing at all). In particular, changing the HW neutral to the HWRM means certain actions like the guard order are almost useless, as your ship AI will frequently leave the unit it is guarding to comply with the new stances.
Again, this may not sound like a big deal, but in HW some of the best tricks (like cloaking groups of salvage corvettes or attack craft to get past an enemy) only worked with proper positioning, and I really felt like the strike craft and corvettes in HWRM were substantially less useful than in the original. In Homeworld, a handful of fighters, bombers and corvettes were a threat to even the biggest capital ships, if you could catch a destroyer or heavy cruiser unsupported. In every Remastered skirmish match I tried, I eventually just recycled my fighters and corvettes for the resources, because they were too much of a pain to manage.
I hate to sound like I am griping about what may seem like minor changes, but I never felt frustrated with the units in Homeworld like I did with the units in Homeworld Remastered, and eventually gave up on both Remastered campaigns. Thankfully, the original game is included with the collection, warts and all, and I can't recommend the 1999 version enough.

I've played few games that are as much raw fun as Broforce.  The game is extremely simple when you break it down, shoot bad guys, spread freedom, kill Satan, and ride off into the sunset with a wailing guitar. I'm a long-time, die-hard Sonic fan and will tell you right now: don't buy this game.
It's an utter disappointment in nearly every way save for graphical fidelity and Eggman's character as a legitimate villain once again as opposed to the bumbling oaf he somehow morphed into after 06.
I only have 2.5 hours on record because that's how long it took to beat it. The level design is utterly mindless and you'll either win without knowing what you did or blast off of some ledge into a pit you couldn't see coming. If you thought boost gameplay from Generations and Unleashed was mindless and dull, I promise you this is far worse. The boss fights were laughably easy, and there's not even a final fight with super forms! Hell, the Chaos Emeralds aren't mentioned at all! Shame, Sonic Team.
My Switch and Odyssey are right next to me, and I have all the desire to play and 100% it, as opposed to zero desire to even fire this sack of crap back up again. It doesn't seem like Sonic will ever stand up to Mario like the days of old at this rate.
Worse yet the game is tied to Sonic Mania (a great game not developed by Sonic Team) and the plot is all over the place, filled with holes and head-scratcher moments. The tie-in was unnecessary and puts Mania in a bad light. Further, the powers of these Phantom Ruby things is entirely different between both games: in one it manipulates time and space like the Chaos Emeralds, and in the other it just project illusions. Why the inconsistency? There are so many bad choices here!
Wanna fight Chaos? Too bad, he's only in a cutscene as an illusion. How did Silver get there? 06 never happened, right? Who is Infinite? Why does he just disappear at the end? How can this game be so bad in almost every way?
Classic and Modern Sonic really shouldn't be separate entities with different plots, but that's going to be the new thing now because of Generations it seems. There's a hint of the two Sonics coming together again in the future, but let's hope they don't do this ever again.
As a final note, the Sonic series has always been known for having a fantastic soundtrack and this game failed incredibly hard at having anything memorable in the music department. It's sad because so much effort was put into composing and writing lyrics for a number of the stages, but they're all annoying, butt-rocky, distracting, and unnecessary. Yes, the sun is falling from the sky. No, I don't want to hear you telling me about it in song. Nothing from this game is going in my playlists. Where was Crush 40 and other composers like Tomoya Ohtani? Out to lunch because they saw how bad this game was going to suck?
At the end of the day you could argue that 06 would have been better than this game had it actually been finished as it was originally planned to have been. 06 had great ideas that were never brought to full fruition because of a stupid marketing decision that ended up trashing Sonic's reputation by releasing the game far too early. This game on the other hand has bad ideas that were given to time to culminate into an entire game based around them, and no one at SEGA seemed to think that there was anything wrong with whatever the design team came up with, now called Sonic Forces.
Next time actually play your games and see how fun they are before releasing them, Sonic Team. If you thought this was fun, if you thought this was a game that everyone would enjoy, then you need to quit your job and find something else to do for a career, because keeping this up will eventually turn even the oldest of fans like myself against you. Faith shaken.

STEAM BIG PICTURE MODE! I will start off with that. USE IT!  For some reason, the game just doesn't run properly without it. I ran Sonic Forces on a powerful high end computer, and it lagged, slowed downed, stuttered, and would sometimes freeze for a few seconds (making the music go BT-BT-BT-BT-BT-BT). But this was BEFORE I learned that Steam Big Picture mode fixes everything. It's weird for sure, and I don't know why it fixes the game, but if it works then it works. Click that controller icon in the corner of your Steam client to enter Big Picture Mode and get to playing.
That fixes the stuttering issues, but before talking about the rest of the game, I also want to cover another slight issue I've discovered. This game is not friendly with Steam account sharings. I've found that whenever you log off your steam account, and someone else logs in to their Steam account (same computer) and accesses the game via Steam Library sharing, if they start a campaign, the other file will disappear. This may or may not be a big deal for others, but just be aware of it. I lost 5 hours of progress because of it.
The game itself is great. I love the Custom character creator. It's not complex like the Sims (quite frankly I'm glad it isn't, I don't want to spend THAT much time customizing my character). You get plenty costume unlockables after completing missions. While playing I felt like I was unlocking 2 Loot Crates per level!
The gameplay overall is pretty great. Yeah, some areas felt a bit weak, and it lacks a bit of a challenge, but overall I was quite content. If you enjoyed Colors & Generations, you'll enjoy this. The boss battles are fun, and I love Infinite's glitch gimmicks!
The  soundtrack is amazing, of course. The classic Sonic tracks were kinda "meh" in my opinion, but everything else is great. And the vocal tracks are BEAUTIFUL!
Honestly, I think my favorite part of the game (this is kind of a bold statement) is the storyline. As I type this, I don't know how it ends (in reference to the file issue I mentioned above, I lost all progress right before completing the game) but so far I was way into it. I love the war zone feel you get with all of the character dialogues and the chat between your fellow troops and units.
Overall, the game is great. The main point I want to get across is that there are definitely some performance issues with the PC port, but they all seem to go away by running the game in Big Picture Mode. After that, the game is a treat! Just be weary about sharing your game with a sibling!

It’s hard to believe this is Orbcreation’s first game release and what a certain beauty this is going to be.
Sailaway the persistent Sailing Simulator, although still deep into Early Access, has without doubt accurately captured the essence of sailing with this fantastic simulator.
Already there are three accurately modelled boats to utilise, with accurate rigging and sail mechanics.  The weather is real-time driven via highly accurate meteorological data provided by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), the oceans are then affected accordingly increasing or decreasing swells and wind conditions.
If you’re new to sailing then fear not, there are already a plethora of tutorials and challenges geared towards teaching you the foundations and fundamentals of sailing and there are more set to come.
Game controls are easy to master and simple to remember, ensuring you spend more time enjoying the experience than worrying about it.  Multiplayer is also already working, that is to say there will be other boats around but also affords you the opportunity to have multiple crew members on your own boat.  Find yourself a more experienced sailor and pick your ultimate destination!
Sailaway is not just limited to Regatta’s either, the entirety of the world’s oceans is also at your disposal and whilst you do always have GPS and charts available, for now at least (electrical fault spoiler), you can also navigate using the accurately positioned stars at night.  That’s not going to help you much during the day but you appreciate the level of detail included in this title already.
Because this simulator runs in real-time it can take months to cross an ocean, this journey will even continue when you’re not playing the game and will keep you updated via email of your boats GPS position and any incidents which might occur, like running aground.  You can even adjust your boats course and sailtrim from a mobile phone or tablet.
For my maiden voyage I decided to sail the Dover Strait, at night, with a 40degree headwind and I made it.  The English Channel was calm (for the English channel) and the moon was almost full, a simply fantastic experience cheered on and supported by other players online one of which joined me for the final stretch into Calais.  Incidentally, like the stars, the moon is also functional which means that some nights shall be very dark indeed.
If you’re a sailor already or like the idea of becoming one, this is a definite must buy for you.

Such a legendary game deserving more attention than it gets.  You don't see many FPSRPGs floating around out there, but thankfully the few that are are mostly excellent, from System Shock 2, to Deus Ex, to Bioshock, and of course Fallout 3.  Of all the games STALKER is similar to, Fallout would be the closest, in terms of atmosphere.  And boy does this game have atmosphere up the wazoo!  It compliments all the other aspects of the game nicely, especially the setting.  But before we get to the setting, let's look at the story real quick.
Before the game proper, you're treated to an introductory cutscene showing a military truck with a bed full of dead guys.  The vehicle is struck by lightning and careens off the road, flinging its corpse passengers all over the place.  The next morning a man approaches the scene of the crash and finds one lone survivor, the amnesiac player-character.  He awakens with only one objective written on his PDA: Kill Strelok.  As you can imagine, the main objective of the game is to search for clues on this Strelok, and why you even need to kill him in the first place.  Now, I'm not gonna lie, I predicted who Strelok was before I even climbed out of the bunker you wake up in and begin gameplay.  I'm sure most of you can figure out who it is too, but I won't 'spoil' the 'tweest' nonetheless.  Aside from that obvious flaw in the plot, the story is mostly decent, but a little clunky.  Conveyed mostly through banter between NPCs, journal notes on the PDA from the player-character, and cryptic cutscenes triggered when accomplishing a major story-related objective.
What's a bit more interesting than the plot is the setting.  The backstory behind your current surroundings is of course related to the infamous Chernobyl disaster that made a once wonderful landscape turn into a lifeless husk.  But in this alternate reality, a second disaster occured at the site.  A massive explosion that had dire consequences for the surrounding countryside.  Rampant radiation mutated the environment, creating anomalies that break all the laws of physics, and morphing animals and people alike into savage beasts.  The disaster threatened to overtake much more than Chernobyl and the city of Pripyat, and thus the military was deployed to quarantine the area, aka The Exclusion Zone.  As the years passed, people outside the military and science communitites began to take an interest when it was revealed that the strange anomolies created incredible object called Artifacts.  They possessed strange properties, making them extremely valuable.  People began breaching the military barriers surrounding The Zone, treasure hunters bent on finding these artifiacts to attain riches.  They were dubbed Stalkers, and in only the course of a few years, their numbers not only grew, but grew large enough to form non-military factions within The Zone, each with their own goals and views on The Zone.  I can go into much more detail, but that would just use up more characters than the review box allows.  Needless to say, the lore behind the STALKER series is very immersive and interesting.
But the most important aspect of every game is the gameplay, and this game delivers on excellent gameplay.  While its RPG elements are pretty simple: limited backpack size with a maximum weight-carry of up to fifty kilograms, sidequests provided by interactive NPCs, artifacts that add to varius stats, at the cost of adding radiation poisoning to the player-character until the artifacts are either unqiue in that they have little to no drawbacks, or are just taken off completely.  Alternatively, you can sell the artifacts for rubles which you can use to buy items, weapons, and armor.  The weapons and armor also have their own lifespans (and can't be repaired unless you have certain mods installed, which is really annnoying, I have to admit), so it's best to have some backup weapons and armors either in your backpack, or stored away if you can't spare any extra weight.
The gameplay proper, that is to say the combat, is excellent, however.  This isn't like your typical FPS, where you can just run around out in the open, shoot a couple guys, then duck behind a wooden table that can completely block high-velocity rounds and regain your health automagically.  This is a survival game, in addition to a FPSRPG.  Lots of things can go wrong while you're in combat.  The few times you have other NPCs backing you up can get their asses killed (let's face it, friendly combat AI is severely lacking in even the most advanced and well-funded games of any type, much less a game from an obscure Ukranian developer).  If you're wounded, you can bleed out, which means you need bandages that close up the wounds, but don't actually regain much health.  If you want a major health boost, you need to use medkits you've collected somewhere along the line.  That and the enemy AI is surprisingly smart, even on lower difficulties.  They don't just run at you while you're spraying the entire battlefield with a heavy machinegun.  You so much as graze them with an SMG, they jump behind cover and try to flank you.  This is especially dangerous when they have lots of buddies.  Many a game was quickloaded because I neglected to check if someone was trying to surprise buttsecks me with a shotgun.  On a related note, it's always funny to turn around just at the right time, see a guy that was trying to sneak up on you, and blow him to hell before he can even react.
And when you're done trudging your way through an army of enemy soldiers trying to get the better of you, you'll lament: "I'd rather fight mutants than these guys!"  That's usually the part where the game requires you to head underground and creep through a very frightening dungeon of Soviet-era radioactivity.  Like I said earlier, this is an incredibly atmospheric game, and it doesn't skimp on the minor horror aspects.  The unease and fear of turning a corner in these old bunkers and labs is superb, and the one or two jumpscares you'll encounter are pretty good, due to the fact that they're used sparingly and not spammed every two minutes.  Battles with mutants are much more frantic and fast-paced than the careful crawl of human firefights.  By the time you're almost done with a bunker you'll be wishing for irate Ukranians screaming at you while shooting guns... only to wish again you were fighting mutants, ONLY to have your wish granted.  Thus the cycle continues.
Unfortunately, the game isn't without its bugs, some of them not QUITE game breaking, but close, if you're smart with your saves.  NPCs suffer from the classic doorway blocking, in which they utterly block you from entering or exiting somewhere you need to be.  Sometimes certain NPCs will just stand around while being attacked.  For example, there's a mission where a squad leader asks you to take out a sniper that's halted their advance on enemy territory.  When I triggered the quest the sniper promptly opened fire.  So I turned around to snipe him back.  I get a nice headshot (with a neat mini-sniper rifle that utitlizes the drop-effect; so satisfying) and turn back to get my reward, only to find the leader dead, and the quest pretty much kaput, even though it's still active and my minimap has an icon indicating his rotting corpse.  Ah well, so I decide to turn coats and inform their enemy that there's still a squad waiting to attack them.  So I go ahead with a squad and take out my former employers... only I can't 'kill all' the enemies... because the leader is already dead.  Awesome.  An entire faction questline is cut short because of this.  Like I said, if you're smart with your saves, you can circumvent these issues.  It's still annoying, though.
Overall, this is an excellent game, and I highly reccomend it with a 8/10.  I also recommend its sequel, 'Call Of Pripyat,' as well.

Homeworld 2 is where it goes downhill. Completely unbalanced campaign, unfairly difficult. When it comes to Homeworld, it's a fleet game. You build fleets, you attack with fleets. Homeworld 2 punishes you for playing it that way. Mission 3, expects you to be in 3 places at once with your small fleet. Guard 2 places while you battle a fleet twice the size of yours. Mission 4 is where I gave up, You're finally allowed a few minutes to breath and rebuild. Unfortunately, as soon as you go to the objective you're beaten down by a fleet 3x your size. Apparently you need to use bombers on a fly by then return to base for the insta dock and heal. Basically exploiting something in the game just to win. Weak game design. It gets better. I looked up the next 3 or 4 missions. They are all the same. Expecting you to sell your ships to build nothing but one ship type to make a mission more fair. I'll be generous with my rating though. 1/10. Would have gotten 0 but they did add a few nice features to the game like researching upgrades.
Oh and Player vs AI is trash too. Don't bother setting the difficulty to Easy and AI enemy to Defensive. They'll come at you with a massive fleet after 15 minutes.
Forgot to mention, HW1 does the campaign perfect in the sense of build up. Starts slow. Mission one is learning how to do the basics. Mission 2 throws in a few enemies with more learning. Game gets harder from there, like it should. More ships, larger fleets, larger enemy fleets and ships. With a new unlocked ship as a big help to beating the level. HW2? Nah, they just jump right into it. Fight a small fleet mission 1. Mission 2 being expected to guard multiple ships carrying personnel. Splitting up your already small fleet to fight at multiple locations. If you do lose any of those ships you need to protect, you might as well restart because you'll need what they give.

THE quintessential survival crafting factory game.
Factorio will push your spatial management skills to their absolute limits as you start to formulate very complicated automated processes and how they string in with being able to incorporate additional inputs of resources and a continually progressing technology tree.
There are some people who play Factorio for 10 hours straight, and there are some who are mentally exhausted after 3-4 hours and can no longer push themselves further. This is an indicator of a game with plenty of depth to offer.
As for the early access part of it - Factorio is mostly feature complete, the only bugs that really hinder gameplay are all present in the multiplayer netcode and currently being worked on. The development philosophy of the creators has been spot on for the past few years.
Unless you aren't seeking a game that will deeply mentally stimulate you, I highly recommend Factorio, even at full price.

Tropico 3 Review – Raymond KT
Summary: As in the original Tropico, the player again is able to play the role of "El Presidente" taking over the control of a tropical island. You decide whether you want to use your army to secure your power base in the best traditions of corrupt, unscrupulous tyrants everywhere, or alternatively to lead your people to prosperity in your role as generous elder statesman. Danger lurks on every corner. There are militant rebels planning a Coup d'Etat for a communistic Junta, while in the background there are two lurking superpowers, the USA and the Soviet Union, who would perhaps prefer a more pliable president in the strategically important island of Tropico! [Kalypso] Collapse
The game itself plays out as a series of scenarios. Each scenario has a primary goal to accomplish and several pitfalls to avoid. For example, a scenario might require you to lure 500 tourists to the island over a span of 20 years while simultaneously avoiding bankruptcy and assassination. Each scenario is scored on several factors and you can submit scores to a central server. This leads to a sort of “high score” competition along the lines of more arcade-style games. Before you actually run the island you get to choose your characteristics. Male or female? Intellectual or moron? Army leader or pacifist? Each choice can provide benefits or handicaps based on the scenario. A playable set of historical leaders is provided for your amusement. Then you can begin ruling your country. Tropico 3 has a nice set of overlays to help you determine the strengths and weaknesses of your island. Taking a few minutes to determine the mineral deposits (e.g. iron, gold or bauxite) and the climate (for growing crops like sugar, bananas or corn) can start you on your way to a basic economy. Of course it is not that simple. Your citizens also want services. Things like health clinics and high schools cost money. And these are not the sort of people to take being unhappy lying down. Every citizen has political opinions. They each belong to one or major factions (e.g. militarists, industrialists, ecologists, religious and so on) and the things you do can make them like you or hate you. This is one the best parts. Tropico 3 is one of the best games in terms of simulating the way domestic politics actually works. Running a nation is not like playing Civilization, where everybody just does what you say. These factions have identifiable interests and can take (some) action to make you see things their way. Of course they may (and often do) oppose each other, and you can't make everybody happy all the time, but that is part of the game. To some extent the graphics make up for this. They are clear and informative, often providing a visual representation of important game information. It's not enough. You will get tired of the music, too. Another problem lies in the difficulty setting. It cannot be adjusted. Some players will find it too easy, some too hard, but there is no way to change it. This was a strange omission. In summary, this is a good city-builder which doesn't sacrifice much depth while providing a bunch of fun. Bursting with too many good ideas to list, plant your tongue firmly in cheek and sail on down. A good-looking, surprisingly deep, charming city-builder. Lots of good ideas that make intuitive sense. More than worth the price of admission. Only some minor issues keep it from a higher score.
