After getting your♥♥♥♥♥handed to you by Rocky Balboa, you find yourself stumbling into Chernobyl to raise money to feed your family who is now left to starve by the USSR. To your shock, you discover that there is more to the irradiated zone than meets the eye, and discover that your boxing days aren't quite over yet....

S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Shadow of Chernobyl is a first person shooter survival game. The description is accurate if not complete, because this game is a lot more, I would add sandbox and exploration to the mix at least. I will come back to this a bit later in the review.
You start the game in a rather nondescript way, you were left for dead in a field and wake up in the fringes of the "zone" with no memory. By investigating and exploring the "Zone" , a large exclusion perimeter of roughly 30 sq kilometers around Chernobyl which have been sealed off by the Ukrainian army, you hope to regain your memory and discover the place secrets. The "zone" is very dangerous, not only because of all the bandits , trigger happy military, mutants  and mercenaries roaming the place, but also the "natural" phenomenons called anomalies that will shreds you to pieces, burn you alive or electrify you depending of the type if you step on the wrong place. There is offcourse the radiations areas you must avoid in order to survive. The zone contains lot of treasures to find however , mysterious artifacts that can be very valuable and "caches" of gear left over by other lesser fortunate stalker which you have to find.
Those treasures and caches give an incentiv for you to explore the «zone» desolate landscape with it's abandonned factories and villages following the 1986 disaster. The people behind the game made a really good work depicting the zone and people who grew up in the 80's and 90s and have seen reports from the Chernobyl disaster in the medias will recognise several landmarks , like the famous  wheel of Pritpjat or the Chernobyl plant itself. The SGS Gameworld team did an excellent work at rendering the place in a very realistic way and at time I marveled of the landscapes of the ruined area in all their sadness. All in all the atmosphere in this game is topnotch and it makes even the most mundane generated quest an experience as you get to explore all those places , abandoned villages and ruined factories with the leftover of old trucks and cars there and here , a sad but beautiful reminder of the madness and destructiveness of human civilization.
The inhabitants of the zone are no less fascinating, and not all are enemies bend on killing you. many are stalkers like you or mercenaries hoping to find the mysterious but dangerous riches the zone has to offer. At night you might you might encounter small groups gathering around small fires telling stories , laughing (in russian) or playing the guitare. This gives an human dimension to the people of the place, stalkers like you trying to make it.
The story in the game is also very good if not always very clear, especially in those days when we're  tea spooned feed in other games plotwise, S.T.A.L.K.E.R let you do a lot of guesswork on what is really going on, and the answers you get from the plot usually set up more questions. Even the discoveries you make in the game are up to discussion about their meanings. Having finished the game which has no less than two distinct ending, and several versions of those ending depending of your gamestyle and decisions, I personally loved it but it's probably not everyones cup  of tea if you desire a more traditional tale with a “everybody lived happily ever after” end.  It must be said that the game has been partly inspired by the Sovietic art film directed by Stratovsky, Stalker taking on question as existentialism and human potential ,  you will find many elements from the movie in the game although it goes less into philosophy . Just like it's cinematic counterpart S.T.A.L.K.E.R isn't easy to gauge, let's just say it's a great experience gamewise.
The gameplay in S.T.A.L.K.E.R isn't very varied, but what it does, it does well. We've gone into the sandbox and exploration part of the game, but S.T.A.L.K.E.R is a competant first person shooter in it's own right, I found the enemies to be challenging and at time rather smart, hiding from me and trying to flank me or throwing grenades at me when possible. During the game you discover many different guns and rifles, both of Russian and Western fabrication. Although I'm not a gun specialist, I found the weapon system to be rather realistic and entertaining, with the weapons themselves true copies of the originals, mostly weapons dating from the 70 to the 90's, something you'd probably find if you were stuck in a postsovietic zone in the near future.
The quests , especially the generated ones,  can be rather bland but the great atmosphere of the game saved it from being a shore. While the main story was quite entertaining and really catched my interest through the game. It must be said the game could be rather creepy if not directly scary at time while you explore abandoned depots teaming with dangerous mutants and hidden enemies in the dark. I was a bit annoyed toward the end of the game when I was rather suddently forced to change my gamestyle from “crawling and shooting” which I had done in the majority of the game to “running and shooting” as I had helicopters shooting at me , leaving me no chance to challenge them. Other annoyances would be the bugs, although I played the “complete Mod” which eliminated many of them , I had a few crashes , but nothing gamebreaking.
All in all I can only recommend this game (which I would recommend to play with a Mod to eliminate the bugs), a competant shooter with a good if a bit convoluted plot  and a great atmosphere than very few games can measure themselves with. This game is quite old (from 2003) but has a vibrant community who deliver new mods and addons to improve the original product to this day.
I love this game really much but It's a shame it took over 6 years I mean, it was still a great game, but it could've been much more for how long it took....

Summarized:
If you played Vampire The Masquerade: Bloodlines, this is like an Action RPG (ARPG) version of that. It's RPG-like in that you develop your character, putting points in stats, skills, abilities, a talent tree, and level up. As far as "the world", it's pretty bare, most NPCs are there just as some part of the "story", vendors buy/sell items and maybe give quests related to the story. What the story is, I have no clue and I don't care. Seems you can pick which faction to join, seems there's some big-bad foozle to kill, but it's a real tedious affair. More on that later. The game world is basically levels and levels and levels of dark dungeons, with a tiny city area (about the size of "first city area" of Bloodlines" I'd say, but Bloodlust:Shadowhunter has a BETTER amount of detail, atmosphere).
If you haven't played Vampire: Bloodlines, this is basically a 3rd person ARPG in a dystopian vampire world of dungeons and more dungeons, and tiny city area. Everything is dark, and gloomy, and you run around inside dungeons, even ruins of dungeons, looking for loot, or something part of a quest, and killing whatever gets in your way. Some compare this to Diablo-style games.
PROS:
-As an indie game, it has a lot of polish and seems mostly well-thought out.
-The graphics are dark, shadowy, but colorful, and look better than I expected. It gets the job done.
I get occasional flickering with shadows or shadows cast on objects. Best to play around with settings to see what works best for each individual, but performance is really good even at high settings (at least for me).
-The sound design is pretty good, the music is atmospheric as one would expect for a "dark vampire" type game, and it helps compliment the look and feel of the game, and help set the mood.
-The game can be a bit scary at times in the sense you're deep in a dark (had to say it again) dungeon and keep delving further and further down. Your flashlight could end up going out down there, and creatures which are basically ghostly black shadows with glowing eyes can pop-up and mob you like a pack of ravenous gimps. Or some zombie or giant might come out from around the corner, or a giant snake pop-out from the wall and nibble your bum to death. The creepy music, and sometimes "lack of sound" can make the experience all that more "interesting".
-That the game gives you so much control over your character development is totally awesome. You create your character, pick Male/Female, then what class (basically: warrior, rogue, mage-ish, which are tied to the individual vampire clans) but like Elder Scrolls or Kingdoms of Amalur, you put points into anything you want, to be a sort of "hybrid" class.
-Like Diablo or Torchlight-type games, you can recycle/gamble loot with chance of getting better loot (or not). Loot can be item drops with varying stats, so you'll find yourself somewhat addicted to seeing "what better item/loot" can you get as you progress.
-A lot of nice small touches, no crashes for me, the tutorial is extremely helpful for new players.
-Dungeons are reportedly randomly generated, but so well done, that you wouldn't even notice.
CONS (these are pretty much all the CONS, everything else is really great):
-The game doesn't seem that well thought out in a small handful of areas. Foremost, is with progression. It seems to be a real grind to level up. There is a surprising lack of enemies to kill. That is good & bad. Good: because I hate ARPG where it's endless streams of monsters, so massacring a whole bunch takes away from the satisfaction of eliminating enemies. Bad: because you get XP for this and you need it to level up. *YOU SPEND MORE TIME LEVELING UP just so you can use a powerful item "you're too weak" to use. Other than that, the only other reason to level up is to get points to put into new powers just to see what they're like. EVENTUALLY, "sort of" ramps up, but the variety of monsters if LACKING.
-Progression is really uneven. High level items drop REAL EARLY in the game. At level 8, I got items dropping where you need like 80 Strength or 50 Charisma, or a combination of stats, like 43 STR *and* 38 CHR, just to use it. Given you only get 5 POINTS to put into stats, and start at around 10 or so, then it will take like 12-15 levels more just to use it. (you can get equipment though that give bonuses to your stats, enabling you to wield items you otherwise couldn't).
-Sometimes a item or weapon you got that requires a ton of points in a stat to wield it, isn't much better than what you have anyways.
-Dungeons can be very large and you might not encounter very many monsters at all. You'll get to a point where you're running around, spending more time running through dark corridors, just looking for something to kill that can give you a measily pinch of XP.
-Inventory space IS A BARRIER to fully enjoying this game. You can't go and just buy more bags like in some other game. You run out of space extremely fast. Vendoring the items yield a very tiny amount of money ($1-3 or so), and often involves running ALL THE WAY BACK through everything. You can't just "port to town" very easily in this game, like you could in others. **The only way to increase inventory space, is to "buy them with TALENT points", but you need "learn" all the prior talents, and they're spread all over the tree...which therefore requires a huge amount of level-grinding, which is really quite backwards. A real mess.
****you'll never escape the plague that your ONLY BAG is constantly being filled up with crap you can't use, that is only worth $1-$3 at a vendor****
-Quests involve getting something, but first you have to get something else, but to get that, you must....---yeah, that routine appears here and there, not all the time. You pretty much have to run into one of the randomly generated dungeons and search the whole bleeding place to find whatever it is. I have some quests where I couldn't find what was needed. Could be a bug. Not sure. Either way, most of the time, you'll be doing dungeons just to see what new, cool loot you can get a long the way. The story/quests are just there to "help it along", which is weaksauce, really.
-the voice-acting isn't great, but it didn't bother me.
-too many traps and puzzles for my taste. It's like it's there to balance out the lack of monsters to kill.
-rogue-like character supposedly good at "sneaking" but there is no sneaking-skill to activate or toggle. You can get close to some creatures, but as soon as you're in melee weapon range, it instantly wacks you, usually stunning. Melee combat can be frustrating because of fact enemies seems to ignore your attacks, hit/stun you which is annoying. I JUST USE RANGE ATTACKS.
-lack of direction on quest objectives; the story and level-design don't marry well, leading to time-wasting confusion.
NOTABLE MENTIONS:
-you can bite NPCs to sire them, and make them minions you can issues commands to. Have them follow and help you fight. Or, send them out to scavenge for loot, or sire their own people. Pretty cool. But NPCs are pretty scarce, which really stifles the fun of this feature.
-sometimes the mini-map works, sometimes, it decides "you aren't omniprescent" and refuses to show you anything of an area. Worse, explored maps reset!
Overall: 6.9/10
GOOD: Satisfying graphics, lots of cool abilities, great atmosphere, good loot-fest system, like a 3rd person Torchlight meets Vampire:Bloodlines-lite; light on world-RPG but strong on stat/skill-based RPG leveling, overall making it enough to stand out as MUCH MORE than just some hack & slash-game.
BAD: Redundant, repetitive music and randomly generated dungeons, clunky melee combat, uneven progression, topped with monotonous level-grinding for XP in dungeons lacking enough (varied) things to kill, can be real frustrating.
Conclusion: It comes SO CLOSE to being PERFECT, that you might actually end up HATING it for that.

So far, I'm very pleased with this game. I really wasn't expecting much, and I'm pleasantly suprised. Don't expect a AAA quality game. This is an indie game.
Pros:
- Character progression. The leveling system, the RPG elements, skills, spells, talents, etc. When it comes to progression, this game is deeper than most AAA RPGs.
- Randomly generated dungeons. I almost couldn't believe that they are randomly generated. They're that well done.
- Tricks and traps. Tons of traps and hidden areas. Lots of nooks and crannies to loot and explore.
- Random loot (like Diablo). This keeps you wanting to slay that next big baddie to see what he'll drop.
- Atmosphere. There are times that your flashlight is actually needed. Some dungeons make the hair on the back of your neck stand up. At times there is a real sense of danger.
- Avery well done tutorial that is skippable. A lot of indie games don't really offer a very good tutorial. This game never made me guess at how to play after I finished the tutorial.
Cons:
- A few graphical glitches here and there.
- Lackluster voice acting.
- Combat can feel a bit clunky at times.
The pros certainly outweigh the cons. This game suffers from the same cons as just about every indie RPG out there.
This game has it where it counts. It's FUN. This is one of the most comprehensive indie RPG's I've played. If you like third person action rpgs, you'll enjoy this game. You won't regret your purchase. I don't.

A gem among indie games, Papers Please is definitely worth the deal. It has such a great depth, the gameplay and the story itself constantly make you question yourself. As you play, you are constantly forced to make moral decisions. There are no right or wrong choices — only valid or invalid passports and documents. There are multiple consequences and endings to this game, so the replayability makes it even more worth the purchase.
All in all, it's a wonderful demonstration of the indie game genre moving to another level, beyond what conventional games would do. Definitely get this if you seek something new, or just curious about how it feels like to work at a border checkpoint.
It's literally a game about paperwork and pencil pushing, and yet I enjoyed it more then any of the big hit titles!

Okay so. . . In my opinion, this is more like what half-life 2 should have been. Those of you that played half life 1 back when it was the latest and greatest, remember what it was like. Brand new AI, an exceptional amount of weaponry and the need for all of it in every encounter. Well paced. Very scarey sometimes when the noises of aliens would go off and had you checking every corner. Make or Break puzzles and strange collection side objectives (get scientist to open this door), and a story line that was quite creepy.
Alien: Isolation is everything that the original half-life is today. It's not just boasting technology advances (like half-life 2) it boasts good story, dangerously random AI, situations that force the player to plan, strategize and think. These are all things that were in half-life one that made it a STUPENDOUS game that spawned a plethora of offshoots: CS, TF, Sven Coop, and that's not counting the follow ups built for half-life source/half-life 2. Alien Isolation is the best game I've played in a LONG LONG time.

I won't spoil the story in this review. Simply because it needs to be played. The only thing I can say bad about this game is persistent bugs. (Yes, you read that line correctly) for instance some mission triggers don't happen right away or not at all forcing players to reload an autosave or outright starting the mission all over again. But as everything else stands? This game is playable.
Also there is an active modding community bringing intersting mods to the game. The tutorial is really straight forward so you won't get lost at the controls.
Now the missions themselves, while some of them are straight forward. Other missions can be a pain in the butt. You will have to micro-manage your resources in order to survive some of these encounters as it can go from "All quiet" to "IT'S A TRAP" in a matter of minutes or seconds.
Overall if you like space battles on an almost epic grand scale. Then I recommend the Homeworld Remasted Collection.

If you're looking for a challenge you can up the difficulty by going for the harder modes or attempting some of the more difficult achivements. All of a sudden efficient placement of your tetrislike rooms becomes a lot more crucial!
In short, definitely recommended for anyone who is into this kind of strategy/management games. If you're looking for a game with a lot of different options or want control over your "troops", then Rymdkapsel might be too niche for you.

As a rating, I'd give it 7/10.
Bloodlust Shadowhunter is not a RPG like Vampire The Masquerade: Bloodlines. You should call it a Third Person Hack&Slash Dungeon Crawler with a little bit of RPG in it. The story, while nice, is nothing to write home about.
Character customization is nicely done... you really can customize your character according to your playstyle.
The game has got several random generated dungeons with 200+ levels. You can sink hours after hours into them, but for me they were just too similar after a while. And: you'll need to buy or find a special one-use-key to enter a random dungeon. While not bothering me greatly, I don't see a sense in that. Also: some doors inside the dungeon also need other one-use keys. Why? We've got a Lockpick skill and we've a Mist Form skill to float through gates.
The loot you'll find is working, but the item system has been done better in other games. When found on level 1 of a dungeon, the sword you'll find would have +2 Strength. On level 50, it'll have +45 strength. A lot better but still basicly the same sword. There are no items or item types which could only be found from a certain dungeon level up on, and there are no unique items. This takes away some excitement when finding a new item. The dev should have looked at Borderlands here: certain enemies drop certain items, bosses drop special items, it actually matters which weapon type you use, there a unique items etc etc.
To identify an item, you need to use a scroll. But you cannot buy great amount of them in shops. You are dependend on RNG as they drop from enemies and chests. This can work and you'll have enough scrolls. But this can also fail horribly (which it did for me) in the form of finding 20 unidentified items on a dungeon run but only 7 scrolls. So my pile of unidentified items only got bigger and bigger.
Graphics are good enough for me, the enemies could use better animations for my taste, though. Sound and especially the music is great!
So... would I recommend this game? Yes I would, it's well worth the money. The game has been made be a single person, and if you think about that is very impressive what he has done. It might have its flaws, but it's well above average. You'll not have the impression that the playing time was lost time.

This game is good and bad.
Good: a lot of areas to explore, secrets to find, enemies to kill, levels to gain, abilities to buy, spells to cast, etc. etc. etc.  That is to say, there's a good amount and variety of content.  The atmosphere (lighting, environments, voice acting, UI) is immersive.  Siring minions is a neat idea, although I wish you could interact with them more.  In my opinion, the price is reasonable.  The dev is responsive and a patch was pushed out at time of writing.
Bad: It is grindy.  Characters in the game were talking about going down to like level 67 of a dungeon.  I never needed to go lower than level 15, so who knows what I missed, but I just did not have the endurance.  Your wrist gets tired of double tapping 'w' to jump forward over and over again.  The color light and sound locks.  I never got the feeling that I found a particularly outstanding piece of loot.
I could go on nitpicking, but overall I actually liked the game.  Just set your expectations--this isn't a AAA title backed by a mega-publisher.  It's just an atmospheric game filled with a lot of good ideas.

You know, there are very few games out there that try to an extent to grab the player and at the same time create a world that can be immersive.  Of course there has to be a fun factor, and every review I have seen weighs that fun factor with time spent versus money paid.  Although that being said, free games get their bad reviews as well, which says a lot.  This game, I know, has that fun factor and creates a world that can be immersive.
So, Bloodlust Shadowhunter.  I played the demo, and now own the full game here on Steam.
The hand-created areas in the tutorial and beginning areas outside of the main city area are really well crafted.  Yeah, the combat is a bit different (some say its jittery or wonky), but it's that difference that gives this game its flavor.  I play a spell caster normally in my games, and to hang back and watch minions attack while I fire away at my spells is a blast in Shadowhunter.  Setup your key bindings the way an mmo is played, and you're right at home.  Changing talent tree is also new, and some have hated it, but I like it.  It makes it a different experience with each playthrough.  Loot drops are also interesting.  Not great, but they do provide enough incentive to push on through your campaign.  There is plenty to do in this title, and yes, even an endless type dungeon.
Yeah, there are some bugs.  Every game I have ever played has them.  This game doesn't make them stand out too badly.  There is some imrovements that need to be made to writing, and storyline and character creation, but overall from a one man band dev crew, I gotta' give this a great review.   If I were to put numbers to it, it would be a 7.5 out of 10.  A solid game, and a great take on the vampire world.
Now, if the dev reads this:  To add an expansion pack with maybe some new classes and character creation with some new areas would really make this standout.  Otherwise, great work.
So get out there and sire some minions.

Dark Souls 2 is exactly what you expect it to be, especially when you played the prequel.
Atmospheric, challenging, yet greatly rewarding.
The world feels void, empty, cold, and yet in a weird way incredibly alive and dynamic.
The sound design adds to the dark and unforgiving feeling. Almost no music, just the sounds you would expect from an old castle, damp catacombs or huge forests. In boss fights however the music lets you know just what you are up against.
Now of course the most important question:
Is the game just as difficult, or even more so, than Dark Souls 1?
In a word: no.
When you are like me and played DS1 multiple times, DS2 is hardly a challenge. There are though enemies, there are places hard to navigate, there are frustrating bosses, but those are just a very few. The rest is easily dealt with with the same tactics used in DS1.
And in coop the game gets almost too easy.
That does not mean the game is not fun, because it really is.
And the difficulty rises with New Game + and above.
If you played DS1, you should at least try this game ^^
If you did not, and look for a challenge, look no further.

I went into this with the right expectations. An Elder Scrolls game that would be very MMO like, less of everything I love about Elder Scrolls games. But what I got sort of shocked me.
Yes it's got a very MMO feel, but there was more, The mechanics of the game are carefully crafted to preserve as much of that Elderscrolls feel as possible... Hell I can steal axes and armor off of displays in shops and and then melt them down for parts or even sell them to or have them laundered by a fence.
Sneaking is a bit odd at time but works well and can be a lot of fun when you start lifting everything not nailed down from every market stall on main street... which i do far more often then my noble Nord warrior would like to admit.
Fighing is a interesting mix of do it yourself and auto targeting and hotkey skills. It works out well and does not break to much of the immersion at least in my opinion.
Graphics are suprisingly good for an MMO of this scale, and the artistic designs throught the game hold true to the feel of the Elder Scrolls lore and game series as a whole.
Many quests are simple fetch or kill but some of them turn out way deeping and far more interesting, Which as we know happens even in Skyrim and other games in the series. Overall the DLC content is the most well made of the story content. They seem to have taken more time in weaving a story and making it more then just fetch and kill. They even included player choice to some minor degree which actually made me think about putting points in the persuasion skill before.
All in all I have highly enjoyed my purchase so far. I got the gold edition for 30$ on cyber monday so im talking from the perspective of that price compaired to what I got.
I mean if you can often spend 60$ without blinking then ya this might be a good perchase for you, but if you struggle to spend 20$ on a game this might not be right for you if you think your getting a single player Elder Scrolls game cause you will be unhappy if that is what you seek.

Also there is an active modding community bringing intersting mods to the game. The tutorial is really straight forward so you won't get lost at the controls.

Overall if you like space battles on an almost epic grand scale. Then I recommend the Homeworld Remasted Collection.

I'm going to be continuously updating this review along the way. First of all some info about my PC. This will be more about performance then gameplay itsself, so you get an idea of how well it runs on my PC which handles BF4, GTA V and some more AAA games without too much problems.
i5 4CPUs 4210u @2.70 GHz
GTX 850M 4GB DDR5
8GB DDR3 RAM
normal HDD 440GB drive
First impression:
The game had to download about 3 hours because of the big download size (+35GB). When I first opened the game, it asked for some stupid advertisement of Square Enix or some newsletter of some sort. I skipped it, and started a new game. The cinematics looked amazing, and they ran smooth as butter. But when I played in-game at the default settings, it was at an average framerate of 34 fps, and it stuttered sometimes, but not enough to make it unplayable. I learned the basic stuff, and did the first 2 or 3 missions. Got the glider, then decided to call it quits. So I took a break.
2nd Time starting the game:
I read somewhere that lowering the resolution of the game could help with stuttering and framerate, and it was true. The game now runs at around 38-58 fps, and it stutters less frequently. I tested the game for stuttering by breaking the bridge with some vehicles on it, the game didn't stutter at all. So I decided to take over a pretty big, what seemed to be a power plant, base. It stuttered sometimes, when stuff exploded or when I got shot, but it was pretty playable. I took it over with succes, and decided to go see if the bridge I previously destroyed would have been rebuild. At this point, I played about 2 hours of the game, when it finally snapped. The game stopped working and crashed on me.
Day 3: Decided to delete the game since it's not worth the 53GB it's taking up on my HDD.
Liberate an island nation from a despot who is killing his own people and destroying their homes by.....killing everything and destroying everything.

Potential performance issues, but it works fine for me on my 3 year old computer, so 👌👌👌
Also, the solution for the bad driving is to never use cars, and the wingsuit is faster and more fun anyway, so it all works out.
If you're not sure about performance, just buy it and refund it if it doesn't work for you. Yay refunds.
EDIT: Good news, I actually UPGRADED my computer, and now the game constantly crashes! Fun. I tried a bunch of fixes and none of them work. Even though it is now impossible to play this game, I cannot refund it, since I already played too much before upgrading. Not recommended.

Pros:
-The gameplay is really fun.  Sneaking around as a silent assasin is challenging and rewarding.
-You can save whenever you want.  Especially if you're avoiding being caught, the constant F5 quicksave is really helpful.
-Many ways to play.  First off, you can pick from two different protagonists, but beyond that, there is a lot of choice that you have in the way that you want to play.  I just finished my first run through, trying to be sneaky and unseen, and as I was playing I kept thinking, "next time I'm going to be violent and kill people."  So there is a lot of replayability, depending on your play style.
-20-25 hour campaign, once you factor in the replayability, the number of hours you can spend here is based on how much you want to put into it.
-Definitely worth the asking price, if you buy it on sale.
-The seventh chapter uses a very unique method of puzzle solving and timetravel, which was incredibly enjoyable to play though.  (However, I wish that function came into play outside of that one chapter.  Also, the ending of that chapter was a cop out to the funcionality they created throughout the chapter and felt anticlimactic.)
Cons:
-Combat is really difficult.  Based on the animation of enemy attacks, it was hard to tell when to strike a block, so I found it much easier to be a sneaky assasin and take out guards without a fight.
-There are clipping issues with the Far Reach spell.  You try to jump to one platform, but you end up jumping right below the platform, falling toward alarmed enemies.
-The story is really bad.  Aside from the time-travel story element from chapter seven, the story is bland and falls into the same common tropes of video game stories.  The story doesn't fill me with a sense of urgency, or fear or make me feel connected to the world; it just feels like filler to cut between the action sequences.  Everytime the story goes to the Void is painful, storytelling wise.  I always saw it coming, it happened at the same time in the same place, it was ineffective.  The dialogue is overall poor. Okay so, you've probably clicked the game because it's on-sale.
Perhaps you're checking the sample pictures and sample video.
You might think that "Papers, Please" is not entirely pleasing, in fact, might get boring.
This game is actually brilliant, regardless of what genre you play.
Here's the catch:
If you have read George Orwell's '1984' and 'Animal Farm', this game will take you deep inside those "worlds", particularly '1984'. The precision of storytelling, and the "cruddy" graphics serve to emulate Orwell's '1984'.
If this is anything but to pay homage, it is a masterpiece as well.
If you have not read George Orwell's work and not a reader, tough luck, because chances are that you will find it harder to relate to the game.
______________________
Let's talk about certain parts of the game:
Music: The music is suited to show a Totalitarian sense of culture, because it resembles '1984' and North Korean parade chorale music.
Mechanics: Very simple, yet in its simplicity it shows the menialness in the job and culture. Struggling to fit the bill for your family, killing a person, refusing a refugee? These are tough choices the creator wants you to absorb, not to have fun with!
Writing: The English is quite straightforward that most non-native speakers can relate to, but also it is a literary homage for similarity in the style, which George Orwell wrote.
Story: Genius storytelling. It is paying respects to Orwell without copying the book itself.
Graphics: The kind of graphics actually has a purpose, it takes the focus away from the graphics rather than have the player struck in awesome graphics but not the gameplay and storyline. The graphics is also from the 80's which is a direct correlation between the inspiration (the book '1984') and the actual story line (it takes place in the 80's). The cruddy graphics is a complimentary technique used to express that the story is crass or horrible in itself (like what happens in the book, '1984')
Overall, I think this game not only deserves to be played but deserves to be respected as a piece of artwork.

I'm going to be frank about this. Grisaia no Kajitsu is painfully average in many regards. Let the fanboys pour their hate upon me, yet I shall still hold my position. The game suffers from some of the worst pacing I have ever experienced, only being topped by that of Hoshizora no Memoria. Ive tried to like this, as can be shown by my playtime. I was almost never idle when I was playing. Yet, I feel disappointed. About 70% of the entire game is filler. It is full of bland and boring dialogue,  with uninventive slice of life scenes. So far, i've only completed 2 routes, and i'm on my 3rd. Yet I have continuously found it difficult to keep forcing myself through the dull happenings that constantly plague the story just to get to the meat of the game.
Ive heard many people praise the game for exploring the backgrounds and psyches of the characters, and it does live up to that expectation. However, you have to get through 40 hours of sleep-inducing dialogue and repetitive events. Its simply not worth it unless you have a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of patience. Granted, even that probably wont be enough. Ive played around 20 visual novels, 7 of which take around 20-50 hours to complete. However, those visual novels contained something this one does not. An interesting plot. The plot is entirely non-existent, only focusing on character exploration of each heroine. The common route is merely 30 hours of filler. Its absolutely mind numbingly boring.
All in all, this game was a disappointment to me. I picked it up on its release date when it was being hyped up by a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of people. If theres anything I can thank this visual novel for, its getting me into the meat of the genre. However, I can not recommend this. Buy this if you are looking for a game ENTIRELY character-driven, as that is all you will get. If you are trying to find a thought-provoking or engaging story, I would recommend G Senjou no Maou.
Edit 1: The heroine routes are pretty good, I will admit. The flashback scenes hold quite a bit of tension during them, and keeps you hooked the entire time (unlike the rest of the game). Even so, I don't think it's worth it to have to go through the utterly mediocre and bland common route. Many people say that the reason that Grisaia is so great is because of its comedy and its characters. While its characters are where it shines, and they are quite complex, that is simply no excuse for the lack of plot focus in the game. It feels like the writer should have spent more time focusing on creating a compelling story rather than dragging the game out with filler.
Some of the scenes tugged at my heartstrings, but they left no lasting impression. In regards to the comedy, it might just not be for me. I honestly tried to enjoy the slice of life elements, but they just aren't that great. The comedy falls flat, and just doesn't compare to legitimately funny and gripping VNs like Majikoi Oh Samurai Girls. I will admit that I am judging this game harshly, but I truly did enjoy many parts of it. I do think this is one of the best VNs on steam, but I can't wholeheartedly recommend it with its flaws. Hence why I made a negative review instead of a positive review.
Edit 2: Alright, so I have currently finished Sakaki's route, and am now on Makina's. While I felt that Amane and Michiru's routes were quite dull, I found Sakaki's route to be much better. It started out very dull and boring, but ended up being quite good in the end. I don't wish to spoil it, but I honestly preferred it much more over Amane and Michiru's routes. Makina's route so far is quite cute in all honesty, and I think that she might be my favorite out of all of them. Also, it seems like the majority of Yuuji's (Protagonist) backstory is revealed in this route, making it much more interesting. I'm still not going to give this game a positive review as I feel that more people would see this if it was in the negative reviews rather than positive, and I have not seen any other reviews shed light on the game's issues.
I would recommend this game hesitantly ONLY to someone looking for slice of life with a bit of tragedy mixed in (definitely don't look for a compelling overall story, as that is not what you will get).

I went into this with the right expectations. An Elder Scrolls game that would be very MMO like, less of everything I love about Elder Scrolls games. But what I got sort of shocked me.
Yes it's got a very MMO feel, but there was more, The mechanics of the game are carefully crafted to preserve as much of that Elderscrolls feel as possible... Hell I can steal axes and armor off of displays in shops and and then melt them down for parts or even sell them to or have them laundered by a fence.
Sneaking is a bit odd at time but works well and can be a lot of fun when you start lifting everything not nailed down from every market stall on main street... which i do far more often then my noble Nord warrior would like to admit.
Fighing is a interesting mix of do it yourself and auto targeting and hotkey skills. It works out well and does not break to much of the immersion at least in my opinion.
Graphics are suprisingly good for an MMO of this scale, and the artistic designs throught the game hold true to the feel of the Elder Scrolls lore and game series as a whole.
Many quests are simple fetch or kill but some of them turn out way deeping and far more interesting, Which as we know happens even in Skyrim and other games in the series. Overall the DLC content is the most well made of the story content. They seem to have taken more time in weaving a story and making it more then just fetch and kill. They even included player choice to some minor degree which actually made me think about putting points in the persuasion skill before.
All in all I have highly enjoyed my purchase so far. I got the gold edition for 30$ on cyber monday so im talking from the perspective of that price compaired to what I got.
I mean if you can often spend 60$ without blinking then ya this might be a good perchase for you, but if you struggle to spend 20$ on a game this might not be right for you if you think your getting a single player Elder Scrolls game cause you will be unhappy if that is what you seek.

I bought this game while it was on sale and I don't regret the buy as I had and still have fun with it but I can't give it a positive rating because it's a giant cashcow that paywalls features that should be standard in an mmo, especially in a b2p one.
1. The crafting bag: Unless you have ESO plus at a monthly cost of around 12€ you won't be able to use this feature.
That means a full bank chest and lots of shuffling crafting materials around, I seriously just damned the damn small inventory spaces until I got ESO plus and now it feels mandatory if you want to do any provisioner, alchemy or enchantment crafting.
There are just so many materials that it's ridiclous that they didn't add a basic, toned down crafting bag for non subscribers but use it as an incentive, even for players who own all DLC's, to subscribe and hence making the buying of DLC's wasted money.
2. PvP: With the One Tamriel update they made players of any alliance able to play together, at least PVE.
BUT for PvP you and you friends still need to be in one alliance, that means either you all agree on one alliance and only choose between 3 races OR you pay to be able to play with any race in any alliance by buying the explorers pack.
The explorers pack uses a scarcity created by ZeniMax to justify paying for something that adds no additional content, they want one to pay extra money in a game that you bought and maybe even pay monthly for the ability to play together with you friends with any race.
In other words, they strip content out of the game (narrowing your selection of races) just so they can give you an option to buy yourself out of that situation. This is, in my opinion, one of the worst cases of "micropayment" use.
Even though it's a good game, the mix of microtransactions and artificial scarcity to justify them takes out a lot of fun for me, I myself would rather have a pure subscribing OR b2p model instead of this cashcow system.
That's why I will still give it a bad rating, even though it's not the game itself that earned it but the publisher behind it, I won't reward them with a good review.

Played this in closed beta last year and i must say it's an awesome MMO. I was expecting 2 MMOs this year that would live up to my expectations and both of them delivered. I will be playing this along with Black Desert Online.
This game is pretty grind-y but the amount of classes you can choose from is ridiculous. Also all the classes feel unique (You got 4 ranks when leveling so basically you choose to combine 4 classes together to create your unique character). There are a lot of enemies swarming you most of the time so for new players i would recommend a class that has a lot of AOE skills (you can always change your style of play at the next rank if you so desire).
And now for the most important thing to me in MMO games: The Combat :D The combat system is one of the most awesome systems that an MMO could have. It is action based and not only that, you actually have to aim at your target with the archer for instance to hit it. For some skills like lightning bolt you actually get a circle that you position where the lightning would hit.
So think of this combat style a mix between your favorite MOBA game and a game called Ys: The Oath in Felghana for PSP.
Also it plays very very well on a Gamepad (Which is what i was using for the first time ever in an MMO)
It really felt like true action combat with no targeting what so ever other than where you aim your skills to hit. The combat is also pretty fast, full of dodges, knockbacks, stuns, basically like playing an ARPG like Diablo 3 or Torchlight 2 on a gamepad.
I give this game 9/10 cause of the grind-y-ness. But if you enjoy awesome combat mechanics (i mean i could solo a party boss if i could dodge well enough, although it is very VERY hard when some of it skills kill you in 1 shot :P) And if you enjoy total creative freedom when it comes to classes, if you can look past it's a bit cartoony art-style then to you sir i have only one thing to say: GET THIS GAME! :D
It is in fact one of the best MMOs i've played n a long time. And i've played them all. From everquest, to lineage, to wow, to ultima, to EVE, to runescape, to SWTOR, to guild wars, to freakin darkfall, to all the others that exist.

I was a hugh fan of Ragnarok Online (RO), so I was very exited for this title. Unfortunatly this is not the game I was hoping for, which is very sad considering it delivers some aspects so good.
+ General  Gameplay, very fluid (also great with a controller)
+ Nice World (astetics)
+ The Class System (in theory)
~ The Leveling: preference thing. It is mostly quest driven, less free grinding than in RO.
- The World (structure): It is basically a giant tube where you run through. If there was ONE thing from RO that I loved, and that no other MMO does these days, it was the great delivery of the open world fantasy. Basically you where allowed to move in all directions and find mostly aproachable enemys. The stronger enemys where found in dungeons, that you found on the world map while exploring. Yes, a tube makes sure you always get the right difficulty of enemys, but it is boring and you feel seriously contained.
--- Skill and Stat System: This is where the game breaks and it is hard to take the game seriously. The Stat System consists of 4 Stats, And if you played Diablo 2 you are familiar at how one dimensional a Stat System can be. It is mostly the same here, won't go into detail. The problem is like in D2 that you don't know what stat is superior and which stats are useless. But even without a good Stat System, an RPG can be great, right? Yes, but the real dealbreaker is the Class / Skill System. Skill Damage works roughly like this: Skill dmg + Weapon dmg + Strength. So in other words, Strength becomes mostly obsolete with good weapons. And since low level dmg skills are just there to be replaced later by higher class dmg skills, there is no point in even investing in them! It hurts so much, that the whole Class system is so badly thought throu.

The game is mostly outstanding, though there are a few issues to consider before buying (especially for some laptop users or people with displays greater than 1080p - see the later part of my review). The atmosphere and aesthetics are great, and really capture the spirit of the first Alien movie. Sound design is phenomenal, and the game is long and tense. For whatever reason I don't find the alien scary (never have for the movies either), but the game does a really good job of creating tension, and creates some real heart pounding moments. I'm certainly very cautious of the Alien, and try to avoid encountering it at all costs. It's fairly varied in terms of environments and challenges, and the characters are strong. You have a range of weapons and objects you can use to complete objectives, and areas often have multiple paths you can take.
That said, I had a few issues with setting up the game to run on a laptop with a Nvidia GPU (there are no Nvidia drivers for the game) and a UHD screen (scaling issues, fixed by forcing it to run at full screen via Steam commands). I've only enountered one glitch, which I had to resolve by reloading, but for the most part the game is highly polished and runs well and looks great without requiring really high specs. The Alien AI is a little too intelligent in parts for my liking. Playing on Normal, it's alright most of the time but there are instances where it just is so unfair the game isn't enjoyable. For example, there's a part during Mission 6 which involves crawling though some floor vents. Crawling through vents makes noise, the alien is already scripted to be in the area, it hears the noise and kills you. Seems getting past it is just a matter of luck.
It's a great horror game, and pretty much a must buy if you're a fan of the first Alien movie, but be prepared for parts where you are going to be more frustrated than scared. These are rare however, and for the rest of the time the game is pretty much spot on.

A very stylish, spacy RTS-lite that has you commanding your little block men to mine resources, build, research and defend, with the ultimate goal of reaching and researching the four monoliths in each corner of the smallish map. The gameplay is as minimalistic as the graphics -- you have seven building structures to choose from, and have to balance your construction of them based on your available resources, while at the same time making sure you don't put your block men too far away from their battle stations at any time as they must fend off the occasional attack wave, which increase in frequency and strength as the game goes on.
Without balance and a fair (but not frustrating) level of difficulty, this game probably would have been too simple to be anything but a flavor of the minute, the type of game you play for a day or two to never return to. But it is well balanced and challenging, and the minimal graphics and excellent space synth soundtrack (my wife walked by and asked if I was listening to Pink Floyd) allow this game to succeed in both style and play.

Full review:
rymdkapsel is something else. It's a strategy game set in space. You control little rectangles and give them orders. They can build more rectangles (and squares too!). They get attacked by triangle-looking things that fly. Did I mention that the resources are also in the form of various shapes?
While playing, you're tasked with expanding your little "station" by way of ordering minionsto do various tasks. When you first start off, you're supplied with a limited amount of each of the three types of resources: blue cubes, purple squares, and yellow pyramids. Each resource is used in building new rooms and corridors for your station. Every room has to be attached to a corridor in some way. Corridors are relatively cheap to make, and you'll need them to get to the four monoliths in each corner of the map.
You start off with a few minions, who can each be given a single task. If a minion is placed into the "construction" group, then that minion will work on building new rooms and corridors whenever the player places a new one. You'll probably want to start off the game by building the basic resource-gathering rooms. The blue cubes are generated out of thin air and the purple squares are harvested from the various pools of them scattered throughout the map.
The yellow pyramids, however, require a bit more effort to earn. First, you must grow food in a "gardens" room, then, a minion (or two, or three) must be tasked with "food service". These minions will then bring the green trapezoids (well, I think they're trapezoids) into the "kitchen" room, which then turns the raw food into the yellow pyramids for use in other rooms, like the quarters (which gives you two more minions) or the weapons room.
The weapons room is essential for protecting the base from attack. Every round (yes, the game plays in rounds), a series of attackers will come in and attempt to destroy your minions. If all of the minions are destroyed, you're gone. The weapons room, when minions are assigned to it, allow the minions to wield weapons to defend against these attackers. I tried to clump together all of my weapons stations, but still failed in the later rounds, as there were simply too many hostiles for my minions to deal with.
I found that the rounds started progressing a little too fast. As I got farther into the game, the rounds got progressively shorter, and more aliens attacked the base. There's actually a monolith that can help out with this, as it slows down the rounds. I started going for this monolith first after my first play session.
Your ultimate goal is to survive as long as possible. The game does give you some minor "goals", but your major goal is to just survive. There are four monoliths in each corner, each containing a separate ability to help you out in the long run. One of them improves your extractor's efficiency, with another improving your minion's walk speed. Once you reach a monolith, you can assign up to three minions to research it. This takes quite some time, and I had to withdraw those minions several times due to incoming hostiles. I've yet to complete a game in which I've researched all of the monoliths, but I was close!
rymdkapsel is a fantastic game overall. It looks stupidly simple, but it's just so addicting. Highly recommended.

Minimalism is, counter-intuitively, a complex idea. What begins with the simple maxim, "Less is more," evolves into a study in negative space, contrast and juxtaposition, color, and the quintessential expression of an idea. It's an incredibly challenging discipline to adhere to and execute faithfully.
It's easy to see that rymdkapsel is a minimalist game. Stylistically this much is obvious. But this game embodies the whole spirit of minimalism. It does not merely conflate low-fidelity with minimalism, as some 8- and 16-bit styled indie titles do.
Rymdkapsel is a space sim. You control a tetrad-bound space station with little people in it. The presents you with one essential goal: survive. The fundamental strategy to do so is easily explained with the in-game tutorial and involves a handful of room types. How these rooms behave play into a neat and concise set of rules with no caveats and special cases.
There is a fine balance here between simple game play and flexibility of strategy. It might seem that there is a master strategy one could use, but the expression of that strategy allows a great deal of variance and keeps it interesting from game to game.
You could say that there are optional goals like "research all the monoliths", but those are just advanced constructs of the same root goal. Researching monoliths provides passive improvement to your space citizens, so the purity of the one goal is not diluted. You are never really required to pursue this. Artificial constructs like 'achievements' might goad you to, but in truth, you don't really "get" anything for doing so.
Games rarely last more than an hour. A natural escalation of aggression guarantees that, in the end, you will lose. Recall that the goal of the game is to survive - the metric, therefore, is how long you can. Consider: a strategy game that terminates like an endless line runner. The elegance of this solution is a little mind-blowing.

Simple interface, simple graphics, simple enough way to explain how this game works.  But it draws you in quick.  It's a paperwork simulator, sure, but it's engaging and interesting.  You are in charge of a border checkpoint and have to make sure only those meeting certain criteria are allowed in.  If that were it, it would be fairly boring.  But underneath it all, there's little things that affect how you play.  Do you take a kickback to help pay for rent?  How about saving up for your son's birthday?  Do you let the person with expired documentation in, or send her back to her country where she will be killed?
It draws you in with the little stories.  I don't think any other game has presented moral choices in a light such as this. Papers, Please is a huge surprise.  At face value it seems a bit dull, you play an immigration inspector denying or granting access to Arstotzka.  But then you play it and realize it's so much more.
Gameplay includes going over details on immigration papers and ensuring the immigrants papers are in order.  It can be as simple as making sure the papers are not expired, to being as detailed as checking a persons weight and height and the national seals on their documentation.
If that isn't hard enough for you, the game throws moral dilemas at you, people asking favors and for help.  Do you simply do your job, or do you knowingly flub an inspection to help those in need, knowing that your "good" deed could have ramifications for you and your family.
Papers, Please is an amazing and often times bleak / uplifting game that is well worth your time.

An indie game that is unlike any other I've played. Who would have thought looking at documents could actually be FUN? Papers, Please is a game that tests the skills of more basic gaming and cognitive ability, which is a great change in pace in this age of shooters and RPGs. Sometimes you'll want to quit the game, only to grit your teeth moments later and throw yourself at it again. It's a game where you, besides the occasional bug, can only blame yourself when you make a mistake.
And for a game with such a simple concept, it has the added bonus of giving you moral dilemmas. You have the power to reunite families and save lives, at the expense of your own family. Or do you do your job to a T, relentless following the rules of the Soviet-esque regime you live under?
While I'm hesitant on recommending this game at full price, it's definitely one I recommend on a more general scale. If you're looking for a change in pace from your typical gaming, Papers, Please is just right.

During game play you are given different options that can affect the path your character takes. With many different possible ending every move you make counts. This is not a game for someone who is looking for an easy and simple game. You will have to think and pay attention to details. This is by far one of the best indie games I have ever played! Papers Please was created from scratch by one man. Papers Please reflects on the checkpoints situated in Berlin during the Cold War. You might think that looking at dates, numerical values and pictures is boring, but the way PP does it is really great. It's a fun puzzle game that keeps you thinking.
Everything from the music to the pixelated graphics is topnotch quality. Everyone has different passports and there are different ways of dealing with situations. You have to watch out for workers, diplomats, terrorists, spies and people of the secretive Order group.
Of course, this game is not for everybody. If you enjoy playing generic COD shooters and that's all you play, this is not for you. You are working under time to deny and accept as many people into your country as possible without being fined. You have a family to look after and they all depend on you to pay for food, heat, medicine and rent in your class 8 dwelling.
However, I really wish for new content to be added, like a war breaks out between Arstotzka and another nation and new enemies are added, or you are relocated to a whole new checkpoint or something. I just wish something new would be added.
Apart from the noticable lack of updates and new content,  this game is worth it.

Dishonored 2 is a well made and polished stealth focused first person action game. For those interested in having a taste of the genre, Dishonored 2 is a decent starting point (the previous game is not essential lore-wise or for learning mechanics); for the people who have long enjoyed the genre, it should not fail to deliver a fulfilling experience.
What's good:
+ Good artwork and concepts.
+ Sufficient lore. If you like to read, there's plenty lying around for you to learn about the world.
+ Fluid movement with decent graphics (not very different from the first game).
+ Great level design and verticality, no minimap but meaningful map for navigation.
+ Interesting mechanics. Far Reach is a fun ability, and crafting bone charms is cool.
+ The gadget Timepiece is amazingly executed.
+ No ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t scripted sequences where you press certain keys as they pop up on screen, and player has full control even in critical encounters. Even in acclaimed titles like tomb raider and far cry 3, there exist these 'do as I ask' sequences that made me extra conscious of how pointless my choices are.
What's not so good:
- Aside from a few key abilities, most others seem pretty useless, especially in nonlethal playthrough. This is due to the fact that the bulk of the upgrades provide a quantitive increment in offensive power that is gratuitous for lethal runs and utterly useless for nonlethal runs.
- The UI dims the bottom of the screen when player is in stealth mode/crouch stance, which makes me feel like there is smudge in my eyes.
- Seldomly the movement can be awkward, such as being unable to move through open window or violently knocking down objects while stealthing pass them.
- The puzzles are largely superficial and a chore. Granted the game is not in the puzzle genre this is forgivable, and usually I just google it when I am stuck.
What depends on the person:
+- The dark vision ability has been nerfed, but is still an essential ability that needs to be spammed. To me this improves balance and adds meaningful difficulty, others may think differently. It also makes the screen a muddy brown, which is not particularly enjoyble to look at for extended periods.
+- While far reach is a signature ability, it can also feel quite overpowered, one solution to all situations that bars the need for other gadgets and abilities. It tends to break up my gameplay into a chain of far reaches and pauses for mana to regenerate. Of course, the player can artificially restrict their uses of it or use jump upgrade as an alternative.
+- It is very similar to the first game in terms of graphics and gameplay, like the batman games or the new tomb raiders, which can be good or bad depends on perspective.
All in all, Dishonored 2 is a competent game for fans of the genre and reasonably priced even for a single playthrough.

The Fruit of Grisaia requires a serious time commitment but if you enjoy Visual Novels, this is one of the best around. The game is not perfect, some of those 40 hours (50 at a relaxed pace) certainly feel a bit unnecessarily padded out. But before you know it, you'll be fully commited and won't be able to stop reading.
The main character Yuuji initially comes off as a bit rough unlikeable compared to a typical VN protaganist but as you come to understand his terrible struggles, you'll be rooting for him as well as grieving for his past. The cast of girls initially seems very one dimensional but as you explore their pasts and their stories, you come to realize how much depth and darkness everyone has buried deep inside them. Helping them heal, in turn helping Yuuji begin to heal, is a truly special experience.
Not all routes are created equal, the common route is lighthearted enough and a bit mundane, probably intentionally so to set up what comes after. The routes with each of the girls are each as long as or longer than many other visual novels, and deeper than most as well. Some are a little lighter than others and others are very disturbing. But I have no problem admitting that this story made me very emotional at times in complex ways. You aren't playing a cheap dating sim here.
While Higurashi #1  was my favorite horror novel, this is my favorite dramatic story. Please do give it a try.

This review will only cover Makina’s Route in general as I have not done any of the other routes. There will also be minor spoilers ahead, you’ve been warned!
This VN is a story about a person who has had a very deep past about himself and his family. He gets enrolled to a “special” school where he meets 5 girls (I know, typical VN right?) and gets to know them better as the story progress further. You also get to know the story behind the girls, why they are in this school, their past etc. This is quite a unique style as most VNs have a style of “get the guy, forget everything else” thing, this VN actually puts you in a realistic environment as the Main Character (MC). All the girls have a different personality (Again, very typical here), but they are all very loveable and picking a route to complete can require some thought as it feel like you need to do all of them.
Overall artwork, design and CGI elements are all on point. The visuals themselves are very appealing to the eye, as you would see in the anime (If you’ve seen the anime). There is nothing else much to say…the art is just too good.
As I mentioned above, this will heavily focus more on Makina’s Route. As for the common route, this is just the stepping stone for getting to know the characters, the setting and the general story. It is very long and some chapters take a long time (Sometimes an hour) to be completed. Some of the chapters focus on each of the characters which is nice for getting to know them.
Now, as for Makina’s Route. It starts off as “This might actually go well for us” feeling until you get around chapter 8 of the route and realise that the situation is harder to handle than usual. This route is filled with a lot of in depth character perception and by this point a lot of character development as arisen, nice touch. JB, Makina’s Mother and The Irisu Clan are also heavily involved with this route as well as the MC A.K.A “9029” by the company he works for. The story does get a little complicated between the relation of Makina and the Irisu Clan, which made the entire route seem a little off. It also splits in a few parts in which it shouldn’t have, making it harder to understand than it already is. There is also a reason why Makina needs to be alive, but the clan wants her dead, but this reason wasn’t mentioned right until the end which was frustrating as it was such as important note.
There is a good and bad ending to this route (As well as in the other routes). Your choice at the end of the route will affect the ending, so save before choosing. I did manage to do both the good and the bad ending. The good ending, well as from the name, is “good” in a way. The bad ending however didn’t feel like a “bad” ending per se, it felt more like a “neutral” ending to be honest. But overall, this route was really solid and well made.
Soundtracks including the OP theme, the menu soundtrack and the in-game scene soundtrack were very nice sounding, most were almost on point in the scene. It is not quite perfect as in some scenes (Tiny amount maybe only 4-5), they could’ve made better soundtracks in the situation. In this case it gets a solid score, very well done.
It is a solidly built with all the features a VN would ever need, some are even beyond the boundaries of the VN like a feature to optimise up to 3 monitors, which is completely unnecessary, but great otherwise. There is the usual speed text slider which works absolutely fine, I did find the faster speeds still a little too slow, but they’re good enough as they are. You also have full voiced support (Except for the MC), you can turn them off if you wanted to, change the volume and turn off some and keep the others on (Great if you want to role-play) as one or more of the characters.
Unfortunately, the SHIFT + TAB feature doesn’t work as great, sometimes it opens, sometimes it doesn’t and sometimes it would slow down the game as if it was going to lag or about to crash, not a pleasant experience. I would suggest just using ALT +TAB is you want to switch between the game itself and something like a group chat, this way the game doesn’t get affect at all. This is VN, but for some reason idle FPS is usually around 25-30 FPS, I don’t know why, but this value should be at 60 FPS, not 25-30 FPS. Not saying it doesn’t reach 60 FPS, it does, but only when you are constantly reading, but even if you leave it idling for 5 seconds, it would dip down to 25 FPS at the lowest.
Just look at my hours on this VN…It costs £30 and you can probably get it on sale for around £20 or less if you’re lucky. This is totally worth it, no doubts about that one. Took me 61 hours to finish ONE ROUTE, yes ONE ROUTE!! That should tell you a lot. So, if you are planning to finish all the routes, you’ll definitely get your money’s worth here. This is a must buy for the person out there willing to spend the time on reading all the chapters and finishing all the routes.

TL:DR I *recommend* this game but not the steam version due to content cut in the Japanese version this is based on.
First I'd like to say I have mixed feelings about the version here on steam. I got interested in this VN because of the anime. I  loved the humor that contrasted some pretty dark moments. That's not to say the VN here lacks that humor. It's just that the VN spends a lot more time with those dark elements. Overall its heavier than the anime. What does that have to do with the steam version? Some claim that in addition to the removal of the adult scenes that some of the more lewd humor was edited from the script. It's quite possible this happened even before it was translated. So I'm not pointing fingers. Just makes me wish I had bought the denpa version (which I will probably still buy since I do like this series).
I honestly thought I wouldn't mind the cut adult scenes since the denpa version is censored anyways. But in hindsight I've come to realize that, lewd or not, cut content is lame. Seriously. The fade to blacks are jarring and you inevitably end up wondering what happened when the characters make subtle references after the fact. So, yeah, mosaics suck but cuts are worse, imo.
That all said its still a solid game with a lengthy story. I'd give this version a 6/10 (8/10 if it was the full version)

I've been playign ESO since not long after it has released. The progress this game has made since it first debuted is just astonishing. It continues to approve and conquer issues MMOs have been stifled by since the genre existed.
One in particular is the ability to play with your friends as soon as they start. I have several high level characters, and a group of friends recently started playing - all starter characters. Even then, we can group up and quest and somehow the fights are the same difficulty for me as it is for my buddies. The only difference is I have more advanced skills to use and cooler looking armor. Aside from that, it's just as though I started my character with them. It's amazing and a ton of fun. We were runing dungeons together and taking on world bosses in the first few hours they joined.
And even though my characters have reached the "level cap", the champion points and New Game Plus style storylines makes prevents the game from getting old. Great writing makes the quests enjoyable to do and not a grind.
They also have Arenas for survival style fights with cool rewards. PVP is just insane...you can write an entire post about that.
All I can say is this is the best MMO ever. Period.

This is the closest to an Elder Scrolls MMO you will get. It plays actually kind of like an Elder Scrolls game, just with a bit more grinding. The world is absolutely beautiful - every part of it. I also appreciate the character customization, and like you'd expect from any elder scrolls game, the atmosphere is stop on. Unlike any elder scrolls game however, the music is just god awful - I HAVE to turn it off to play Morrowind or Oblivion OST in the background. I also don't like the fact that there is only an illusion of dialogue: you don't get to add any flavour or uniqueness to your character personality wise. It's always just "Yes", "No" or "Tell me more". Or of course, only lawfully good answers because white-knight.
This game isn't pay to win, it's pay to have fun, and that's a very risky model and probably why this game never has more than 10k players on at a time.
I ONLY recommend on sale. But I do highly recommend this game over Skyrim, ten fold.

It has been such a long time since I've written a review, so let's review the game that I've been playing a lot recently, Dishonored 2. Dishonored 2 is a first person stealth action game, developed by Arkane Studios and published by Bethesda Softworks.
-Story-
The game is set fifteen years after the events of the first Dishonored game. Emily Kaldwin, the daughter of the Empress and the Royal Protector is now the empress of the Isles. On the anniversary of Jessamine a mysterious figure, Delilah ( everyone who played the good old Dishonored DLCs should be familiar with that game ) appears on this anniversary and seizes the throne from Emily using the Duke's support.  One of the main characters ( either Emily or Corvo ) escapes Dunwall and meets up with a woman named Meagen to sail to Karnaca, The Royal Protector's homeland, to eliminate Delilah's support and take back the throne in Dunwall. That's the basic premise of the game. The Story is overall good, even better when you replay the game with the other character you didn't chose the first time around.
- Gameplay -
The gameplay is very similar to the first Dishonored game's gameplay, except that here it's even smoother. None-Lethal options are much more widely avaliable to you than in the first game. You still don't have a none-lethal sword unfortunately, but you can stun enemies in combat and choke them out instead of doing a critical strike which murders them. Emily has new powers that you can try out and good old Corvo plays out basically the same. IF you choose to have powers at all. Yes, this installment in the franchise actually gives you a choice of accepting the Outsider's Mark or not, which really shows how powers aren't a nessecity, rather just a way to make the game more fun. Oh, you can also craft bonecharms this time, If you buy a particular skill. Other than these, the gameplay is basically identical to the first game's gameplay.
- Graphics and Details -
The game looks absolutely stunning even on Medium settings. The city of Dunwall looks just like it did in the first game. Mostly colourless, feels like a dead city while Karnaca is full of these wonderful colours and is generally much more alive than what Dunwall feels like. Characters have their same Dishonored style-kinda look, and even a familiar painting style can be found as collectibles in the game. The ammount of detail that is in this game is super amazing. The level design is absolutely amazing in every single mission there is in this game. Not to mention The Clockwork Mansion or Crack in the Slab! Holy ♥♥♥♥ those missions! Probably the best pieces of quests I had in 2016 that's for sure. Every single decision you make in the game will change the game in some way. Either the posters on the streets, dialouge of some  civilians or major characters will change depending on what you did to certain people. Even the enemy placement and number of enemies change according to your decision. Even cooler thing is that if you go High Chaos, both of our main characters will be more sinister than they were before. This Equals awesome game design.
- Soundtrack and a few things to mention -
The Soundtrack is absolutely beautiful, I love it! The music during sneaking, during boss battles is really good! You can also find musician bands across Karnaca whom also sing really beautiful songs! Low Chaos and High Chaos also has different soundtracks. Reeeally cool. Now a few things that I wanted to mention. This time Corvo Attano is a fully voiced character instead of the original "silent" protagonist that he was in Dishonored. And I absolutely love it. His voice actor is super amazing. Actually, almost every single voice actor in this game is phenominal ( I personally HATE Meagen's voice actor, I can't stand her ) And I think that's about it. Sure this game had some optimization problems when it first came out, But now it should be totally fine. I can play this game on Medium settings without any problems even though my video card isn't really powerful. So if you loved the first Dishonored game, do check this one out since in my opinion this game is even better than the first one.
- Pros -
Amazing game design
Two playable characters. The Empress Emily Kaldwin or the Royal Protector Corvo Attano
Absolutely great level design
Crack in the Slab Mission
Clockwork Mansion Mission
Lot of replayability
Voice acting is top notch
Awesome gameplay
Really great attention even to small details
- Cons -
The game won't make much sense if you didn't play the two DLCs that the first game had. If you haven't played those, be ready to fire up Wikipedia or Youtube because the game will be confusing at first.
Ending Slides are kinda short and unfinished.
Sequel Baiting.
Kinda similar to the first game when it comes to the story, so if you didn't enjoy the first game, I don't think you should bother.
- Final Verdict -
Easy 9/10, I absolutely loved this game. It really deserved 2016's best action game award. I can easily recommend this awesome game for fans of the Dishonored franchise. Thanks for reading my review and I really hope I convinced people to buy the game or like the game more than they already do. Peace out lads!

I'm pretty sure it's one of, if not THE only, 3D RTS out there. In space.
HW1's campaign draws on Middle Eastern themes of a Promised Land and exile in a desert. The story telling is fairly minimalist and relies heavily on the player's imagination to fill the gaps.
HW2's campaign gives a constant sense of urgency; your homeworld is beseiged and every moment you spend dwadling means someone could have died. This is reflected in some of the mechanics: as soon as you've completed mission objectives, your fleet departs and all resources on the map are collected automatically, versus the first game where you'd spend half the time on a map just collecting stuff after finishing the mission and weren't in a rush. HW2's campaign also draws on Middle Eastern themes, this time of a Chosen One and the idea of vague prophecies.
Great set of games, and you can play the originals (included) if you dislike the remakes.

FINAL VERDICT: Conditionally Recommended
FINAL UPDATE after several hundred hours of playing:
I would only recommend this game to you if you are a tolerant gamer with the following conditions:
1. Being able to play the game WITHOUT any expectation in terms of game quality, server stability, bugs, restrictions, and resemblances to Ragnarok Online.
2. Being able to play the game alongside occasional bots that either passively steal your mob kills in dungeons, or spam silver-selling advertisements in towns.
3. Being able to accept the fact that certain classes are still more powerful than others (unbalanced)
4. Being able to understand that the game is still pretty much unfinished feature-wise
5. ... (there could be more)
With all that said however. I'm one of those tolerant players, and I do really enjoy the game so far due to the following reasons:
1. The ability to experiment with diferent character builds and see how each of them works out
2. The ability to get to higher ranks fast (~Lv.150) without much grinding, if you know how to do it. Note that you still have to grind in the late game anyway. But by that time you will already know if you want to continue forward with your character or not.
3. BGMs and overall graphic style.
4. Secrets and hidden mechanics to explore
5. A unique blend of everything that represents the community (Referencing SEA-Varena)
In conclusion, DO try this game out at least for the music and art style. And it's totally fine if you ended up not liking it due to all the problems. However, I can safely say that as long as you are as tolerant as me, you will enjoy this game a lot.
