Just got done with the VN, and honestly? Very much worth it at full price, although I'd still say try and snag it when it's on sale - as I think the 18+ version denpasoft might be better, as it keeps the full story intact from what I'm told. (( Even if they mostly just took out the sex scenes; still never a fan of a good read being messed with. ))
+ Pros +
- Very long read ( Clocked in nearly sixty hours total. Fifty or slightly less if you're a very fast reader or skim some of the basic parts of the VN. )
- Each girl has a great story to tell.
- Main Character is great as well, with a story you'll want to know more of as time goes on.
- Great soundtrack
- A GREAT deal of voice acting. (( Granted it's in Japanese ))
- You'll come to care for each girl over time, along with caring for the MC, Yuuji. (( Holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ his way of thinking cracks me up at times. ))
- Each route has two different endings, offering around ten endings or so.
- A emotional roller coaster, that will make you laugh, smile, sad, and even at times feel tense.
- Many of the cliches you'd come to expect in 'anime like' settings are not present. Such as how the MC reacts to the girls and how they at times react to him.
- After reading each route, get nifty stuff to download; voice clips, wallpaper, icons, and some nice pictures!
-- Cons --
-  Very little in terms of choice picking; you have about two or less per route. About a dozen or less choices if I recall correctly.
- One of the endings feels. . ."ill-fitting" compared to the rest, but still good. Take it with an open mind.
- Opening Video somewhat spoils key points, if you pay close attention or keep rewatching it.
- No english voice acting, it's only in Japanese. (( May not be a con for some, but do wish there was more, as I feel the voice acting would connect with me more, if it was in english. ))
- Due to this being the All-Age version, several scenes were taken out. Mostly the sex scenes, along with some parts of the game being 'toned down' just a bit, due to being consider 'too mature'. Shouldn't effect the reading, but I still greatly dislike something being messed with. (( Sometimes you might even miss the fact they had sex, which for one or two scenes can change your view on what's going on. ))
+- Other Notes -+
- The steam version, while not 18+, does offer a number of artwork not in the first version of the VN.
- Being in fullscreen and trying to Shift + Tab on steam wasn't a wise idea, as it seems the VN struggles to work with steam on that aspect. Nothing too bad, but somewhat buggy to deal with. May just be me.
- I'd highly suggest reading the story in a certain manner, via playing through the list below, as it feels the best reading wise, along with not effecting your view points of the others if read in another manner;
* Michiru > Yumiko > Sachi > Amane > Makina
NOTE: You can still do the routes in any order you wish, and it may not effect you much if you decide to choose. . .Amane first, or Michiru last. This is just my view and how I read through it, when suggested by another. The pacing felt right, and by doing this you also slowly learn more about a certain character; in a way that feels well paced and enjoyable.
In the end? Yes, I'd say get this VN ASAP if you're looking for a damn good read. Although I'd say get the steam version only if it's on sale, while getting the full version on denpasoft's website. Although the steam version keeps the story well intact, again mostly messes with the Sex scenes.

I played this game back before it was on steam and loved it then, so seeing it brought to steam made me squeal with joy. So let's get this review going. This game is a "Visual Novel," meaning that there's really nothing in the gameplay department apart from making a few choices at certain plot-relevant crossroads, but gameplay isn't what we're here for, this genre is all about the story, so what sets this apart from others in the genre? (list of differences to the non-steam version at the end)
The first thing that catches my eye is that instead of a bland, everyman, blank-slate protagonist like a large portion of visual novels, we get Kazami Yuuji, an unsociable, military-raised teenager not so different from Sagara Sousuke (for anyone who has watched Full Metal Panic). Yuuji is blunt and a bit bad with handling personal relationships, but I honestly have to say that he's a great guy; he is incredibly capable and very rarely does anything negative without a good reason. Our supporting characters are also very unique and each play off of Yuuji and each other in very entertaining ways (though I will freely admit that Makina can get on my nerves). Here's a quick overview of the other students while keeping spoilers to a minimum (skip a paragraph if you don't want to see):
Makina: Girl with stunted growth and childish tendancies. Ends up picking up a lot of bad habits and harsh language from Amane and Yuuji.
Amane: Well-developed body and lots of erotic teasing made towards Yuuji. Very maternal and watches over Makina carefully. Also seems to want to take care of the socially-hopeless Yuuji.
Michiru: Girl who is outright stated to be purposefully attempting to fall into the "Tsundere" archetype, but more often than not ends up looking like nothing more than a contrarian idiot who's the butt of most of the jokes around the dorm.
Sachi: Highly devoted girl who will listen to any order given to her. Often goes around wearing a maid uniform do to an offhand comment about it suiting her getting mistaken as an order (not an uncommon occurence). Has some obvious issues with common sense and flexible thinking.
Yumiko: Aloof and introverted, but has some violent tendancies when annoyed or threatened. Despite this, she is probably the most reliable of the group for tough conversations (if you exclude Yuuji since we're kind of playing as him)
The aforementioned choices in the game will lead you down the character arcs of different heroines depending on what you choose, though this game makes it pretty easy to get to your favorite heroine since there are very few choices in the game and the ones that actually matter are essentially "Go down this girl's route right now or continue the main route until we give you another choice." Ostensibly, each girl has one more choice leading you to the bad end or the good end, though I'll be honest and say that I can't agree that every girl's endings split into those two categories
. Every heroine (Yuuji as well) has some sort of emotional baggage holding them down which got them put into this school to begin with; needless to say, if you go into a route and get details about these incidents, you can get drawn into some seriously heart-wrenching moments of fear, depression, desparation, and rejection as you relive the most painful moments of someone's past.
Having just replayed the Matsushima Michiru route in celebration of getting my hands on the steam release, I will freely admit I was brought to tears multiple times despite knowing everything that was going to be said, and this girl's route probably wouldn't be considered heaviest of the tragedies presented here (though, paraphrasing some words from the game, "You can't really compare two tragedies to each other," so I feel a bit bad trying to order the routes by tragic-ness). I look forward to replaying my favorite two routes next. As a side note, knowing the characters issues in advance actually explains a few strange moments that I hadn't noticed the first time around, so the replay was quite worth it.
As promised, I will list out the differences I've noticed between this and the non-steam release. First off, this is absolutely the exact same translation that was provided in the original version (not that this will surprise anyone who knows what a pain translating a game can be). Though I noticed that there don't seem to be translation notes popping up in the corners anymore, so either those got removed or I missed the option to toggle them. Also, on the steam page, you might notice some CG that weren't in the original game; there's a fair number of those scattered throughout the game. Anyway, next up, Steam doesn't like erotic content, so the intercourse scenes have been removed. Judging by the routes I've replayed so far, usually this is just taking a hacksaw to the scene, cuting out the part of the game with erotic CG/descriptions, and skipping to the conversation afterward (leaving a very awkward transition), but sometimes they change the scene slightly and toss in a new CG to make the transition slightly less abrupt, turning it into a chaste, heartwarming moment as opposed to a lustful one. There are also some other changes to the non-heroine moments, like a certain flashback scene involving the captain of Amane's old club in middle school being changed to be less suggestive. Some of the other changes: There was some nudity in the original version besides the erotic scenes, such as when some "girl-talk" was happening in the bath, so the character sprites were changed slightly to cover the naughty bits with soap. Also, some scenes got cut in places, but were removed so subtly that I didn't even notice until I went back and looked at a CG set for the original game (Michiru and Sachi building sand...stuff on the beach got drastically shortened, but I didn't even notice until I realized I never saw the CG of Michiru being burid in the sand (This review has ended up mentioning her quite a lot, hasn't it)). This all being said, they kept a very large amount of content in the game. For example, stuff like Amane standing around in Yuuji's room in her underwear ended up making it passed the censor stick, and if that made it by unscathed, I highly doubt they made many big cuts besides the one beach scene that I happened to remember.
Conclusion: Hilarious characters, engaging story, and fun to replay despite (and/or because of) knowing the plot. Easily a massive thumbs up from me. I really want to play the two sequel games, but the complicated language used in this game is making my doubt my Japanese is fluent enough for the task, so I might have to wait until the others get translated...that or watch the anime versions for the condensed story.

After 115 hours of gameplay I decided that it is time to write a small review about a well made classic WOD game.
In Bloodlust Shadowhunter you are playing a newborn fledgling woken up in the middle of some ruins. Having no idea about what has /is happening he starts seeking the meaning of his existence. Fortunately he got help by a voice that is talking and guiding him in the beginning.
In the very first minutes you can select to be a male or female vampire or a dhampir (ok, dhampir sounds funny). A Dhampirs is half vampire, half human, that means he is a bit weaker as a regular vampire, but he also requires less blood and is more resistant to fire, light  and silver.
Once this is done you must now choose one of three classes that are warrior, witch, criminal (melee, casting or ranged class). Each of them provides you with different attributes: Strength, dexterity, charisma, vitality, intelligence and persuasion. Ok, now that the easy part is done you have to "Roll the dice" untill your most favorable stats are shown (I always loved this feature) stats like Health, Stamina and Reputation will be determined here and you can reroll till you get the most powerfull combination fitting to your playstyle.
Most of the stats are self-explanatory but some are more important to progress faster in-game.
-Persuation is one stat you should always spend some points because it enables you many dialog options that can help you saving a lot of work and time.
-Intelligence increases the chance of getting talent points when leveling up. These are used in your talent tree that is randomly generated everytime you create a new character. It becomes visible only after you have created your character!  Everytime you level up you receive 5 attribute points and 1 skill point +randomly 1 talent point (inteligence lvl /2).
The npc's in Bloodlust are mostly clanmembers of different clans. We got Vangres, Shadistin, Vurkas, Scades and Furlores. If you manage and make them to like you (using persuasion, do quests) your reputation with their clan will increase and enable clan related skills that can be purchased with your skill points. Some clans are more important to warrior classes (Vangres) some more important to caster (Vurkas) and some more to criminals (Scades).
One highlight of this game is the ability to sire humans by drinking their blood.
Once they become a member of your family you can send them to do various errands for you like collecting loot, collecting blood, assisting in combat and getting more family (victims). I managed to sire 4 and everyone got 10 victims. So I got a nice family of 44 members. In the latest versions you get extras for having more members (like another penthouse and more).
You can follow the mainstory with quest and many sidequests but you can also start exploring the city with all the hidden switches and walls or climb down into the sewers and dungeons. Every dungeon map is randomly generated and has a lot of puzzles and traps to survive.

This game quickly goes from "Ok, cool" to "I have not slept for 15 hours and I loved each and every one of them".
Some backstory: Factorio is a survival game with all of the bad parts cut out. You have no hunger bar, manual grinding is not encouraged, and automation actually makes things run faster. It's made to look (and, to an extent, play) like a mid-90s RTS, and even though I've never played one other than RCT2, I still think this aesthetic works in its favor. What does the game play like? Well, you know in Minecraft how once you get bored of digging 1:2 shafts in the ground you set up a crazy machine to do it for you? This is an ENTIRE GAME about that feeling. It's the type of game where you can make your own computer from chests and wires. It is the BEST feeling.
My only issue is the online. Creative/survival games often have online be a big focus: It's fun to collaborate to ease some of your own workload and help others with what they want to do. TL;DR: A game that starts off really good, but the later levels and characters drag down the tight gameplay.
This is one of those games that I really wish there was a third option between Yes and No. When I first booted it up and played it for an evening, I loved it. The second evening (that's all it took to finish it), it got me unbelievably frustrated. That is basically the juncture for the game. The first half plays out well, the game is fun, and the few drawbacks don't diminish it too much. By the end it is getting onto Kaizo Mario with RNG areas of frustrating.
Broforce is a side scrolling action game, reminiscent of Contra and Metal slug for the most part. You have one hit, and enemies will usually go down with one as well. Platforming is a little loose, but you can wall grab (depending on the character), and jump pretty well. The levels contain a wide variety of enemies to blow through, and each new one is introduced in sequence so you can adjust to the layers being added on. The levels themselves are almost fully destructible, barring some ladders and permanent platforms, so the fact that you can shoot through the ground and under/over traps and enemies adds some strategy to the levels. The levels are full of exploding objects, traps, things to drop on enemies and the like. Each level is broken up into different stages in sequence that you have to finish, usually with a boss fight at the end.
The key factor in the game are the characters. You start with one, and every so many rescues you unlock a new 'bro' to play as. The rescues also act as lives, but at the same time change your character every time you rescue someone. I will touch on why this becomes problematic later, but suffice to say you will probably play 3-4 different characters per level. The characters are all parodies of various movie characters, usually from the 80s and 90s, but there are some more recent characters in there. Each one has their own unique shooting attack, special items, and sometimes other features (McGuyver has sticky bombs, there are some melee oriented characters, etc). Each does feel rather fleshed out, and a lot of thought was put into making them unique. The cast gets pretty huge later on, and I'll talk about the issues there in a moment. Some of the characters do get unique levels just for them, built around how they play, but these are few and far between, maybe six of those stages for the whole game.
There is no story to speak of. You are a team of Bros, who go kill terrorists, then aliens, then demons. If you're angry about a spoiler....seriously?
As I said before, the game started out great. During the terrorist part of the game, the controls were tight, the bosses were unique and varied, and the bros I unlocked were interesting to play. Some were less useful than others in certain situations, but I felt I could make do with whoever, and at least make some progress before I died and switched to a different character. The first ten or so characters are clearly the best designed, and while there are some nice ones later on, I feel the game could have stuck with these and been fine.
After the terrorist stages come the alien stages. There are still terrorists in some parts of the stages, usually fighting with the aliens, but most of what you are fighting are aliens. In general, they mostly rush and either grab or bite you, with a few dive bombing flyers very rarely. This starts to cause issues. With the terrorists being slow to react and easy to sneak up on or climb above/below, you could always adopt your strategy to whoever you were playing. The aliens don't really have a strategy, and you can't really sneak up on them or rely on them to panic like the terrorists. Things like McGuyvers sticky bombs become useless, as you can't rely on the alien running to its friends...its just going to run to you and kill you, making every time you get him a waste. Other characters have some similar issues, as the game starts to add more and more, and less of them are actually useful to the stage. By this time you'll have unlocked a few melee characters, right around the time the enemies who explode on death you need to be -far- away from, and sometimes the aliens beat you in melee due to no fault of your own. Our bosses start getting less interesting as well, two of them are basically repeats (Giant worm that spits acid, and giant worm that spits acid and shoots rockets), and we start running into issues of bosses with very particular needs that will just screw you if you get the wrong character. In this part of the game, you will repeat a boss quite often, just hoping to get the right character with a special ability you can spam to chew through its health. Its cheap, but they fill the screen with so much scenery chewing garbage its the only winning strategy.
On to the hell levels...and this is where the game starts to become absolutely frustrating. Now you're unlocking characters like the girl from Grindhouse (Can only shoot down unless she's ducking and not moving, special only shoots down), 007 (weak gun, four entirely different specials), and Conaan (What the hell is with that wierd 'slight jump and swing' thing?) who basically serve to waste your lives. They do have very situational uses, but with so many characters unlocked, you likely will get them at exactly the wrong time. In addition, with so many very situational and unique characters, you are probably really missing the fact that more of them didn't get special levels to teach you how to play them, or the fact that you can't disable certain really bad ones. We are long past the point where Bruce Willis from Diehard is ever useful, as his gun is short ranged, his stun bombs are useless on bosses and most enemies. Most of the stages now are a mess of explosions, exploding enemies, random traps, pits, and basically a mad rush to get to the next helicopter save point so you don't have to start at the beggining again. Lets not forget the occasional short 'make it all the way to the end of this mess and don't die once' stage, where you will die many times because you didn't get the jumping just perfect...in a game with floaty controls. The bosses are ridiculous, and you are just waiting to get the right characters in order to beat them, not to actually learn their patterns...there is usually just too much stuff going on at once. Also, this part of the game has two more worm bosses, basically the same, one being by itself, another being a pair of them that are even more ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t.
So the review is basically my descent into the game. The start is great and enjoyable, the middle is ok, the end is frustrating and awful. For two evenings of playtime even with all the deaths, I'm not sure its worth full, half, or even humble bundle pricing. Writing the last paragraph reminded me why I got so angry at the game, and I'll have to give it a thumbs down...and remember people, I played on the easiest setting...there's an ironbro campaign where every death kills that character for good, and its game over if you lose all of them. I can't imagine anyone finishing that on normal or hard, especially with the last few stages being ridiculously hard.

Note: This is a review based on a connection from east coast Australia on already shaky connections to servers.
TL:DR
There are issues with lag for me, that were made worse by shaky servers. Class balance was off, especially with classes that where objectively better than another. Mana and mana regen were really scarce, which makes class balance worse. It's a pretty looking and it sounds quite nice as well. I recommend if you don't get lag issues (or you can stand it).
After playing in the CTB2 beta, my opinion of this game was not very high. The majority of this is due to the bad connection between me and the server. The latency was so bad, that I could have been out of a boss's tell for .5seconds and still get hit by it. This is also exemplified by the fact you are stuck in auto attack animations that you fired off. So it could be that you fired an attack off, .1 of a second later a tell appears but .1 second after that you are then stuck in a attack that you can't move from leaving you stuck in an attack that you couldn't dodge. There may be ways of attack canceling but I didn't play around to find out.
Besides that; The art style for this game is greatly pleasing. It really is just nice to look at, and the majority of it is smoothly animated. The pieces that aren't as smoothly animated do tend to be a bit jarring but often it isn't completely over the top. This game is a good looker and I sure as hell didn't mind staring at it the entire time.
Gameplay wise, this game is good. Not spectacular though. Once again, the game has problems with latency (further made an issue with servers). Only your movement didn't seem affected by latency while attacks and skills are. This leads to a lot of jumps with the character as it has to correct it's position to where the attack/skill actually went off at.
Fighting was really satisfying, however mana and mana regen is extremely low in this game. This makes it so every character needs to rely on their auto attack between chugging mana potions. At the time of CTB2, the only truly viable solo character, once again especially with lag, was the swordsman. This was mainly because the swordsman (barbarian class) had a skill that could 3 shot quite a lot of bosses making the experience much much easier than any other class.
That brings on the next issue, class balance at CTB2 was quite horrid in my opinion. I can't speak from mid-late game, but early game there are some really big balance issues, especially with the archer class not having any piercing benefits (even though they are piercing type). I'll leave it there before making a fool of myself though.
Leveling is alright, although with plans to drop exp bonuses it might become quite grindy to level even early game. If you like that great, but if it's too slow to me after launch, I might as well play other games rather than grind.
The best part is the classes in which it allows you to choose your own path and take skills that you want. You could say play a defensive archer and have that work etc etc. However as mention before class balance is off, and there were clearly better choices in classes you should pick at the time.
Storywise? Eh it was ok, nothing truly great, but enough to keep you going. Most quests however are not shown to the player. You actually needed to ask people, this is up to you whether or not you find it good. The bad part is, NPC's will not tell you if you are too low for a quest they have, meaning you could accidentally skip quests and end up behind the curve for levelling.
Soundwise, it was quite good. I've forgotten most of how it actually sounded, but if I remember correctly the music was a nice sub genre of electronic. One thing however. Sound was orientated depend on whatever direction your character was looking rather than the direction of the screen. A very awkward design choice there. (May not be the case for 2 channel audio)
Do I recommend this game? If it isn't laggy, go straight for it and see if you like the grind. If it is laggy, you may get frustrated like me and end up quitting because of the amount of BS that you couldn't control without going overly out of your way to correct.

Overall Dark Souls 2 is a great game. It has plenty of content. There are tons of bosses, an insane amount of areas to fight through, and a plethora of armor and weapons. Just like the previous souls games there is also a lot of replay value.
However, out of the games in the souls series, this was unfortunately my least favorite.
Don't get me wrong, it is a great game that i do recommend playing. But if you have played the previous souls game, this one might be a little bit of a dissapointment. I found the areas to be too easy to progress through. The challenge just wasn't there. Enemies movesets are slow and predictable. Even if you mess up and get hit, it doesn't matter that much; the enemies don't hit very hard. To add along to their low damage they also have low health. It felt like the developers toned down the difficulty a lot. Maybe to appeal to new players to the series.
The bosses are also incredibly easy. I beat the majority of the bosses in one try. They added A LOT more bosses in this game than usual. It seemed like they sacrificed difficulty for quantity. I would rather have few and difficult bosses than many and easy. In the other souls games I usually got that ♥♥♥♥ YEAH feeling when I beat a boss but this time around I rarely got that feeling; it didn't feel rewarding. I WANT to get destroyed by bosses. I WANT to have to focus and actually be skillfull to succeed. This is not the case though. Even the final boss failed to deliver a challenge. I, and many others, beat the final boss in one try and often refer to the final boss as a joke.
To add on to lackluster bosses and enemies. the level design just wasn't Dark Souls style. In the first Dark Souls you often found the areas of the map to intertwine in this magnificent fashion. This once again was a huge part of the first dark souls that I loved and wasn't delivered this time around. In Dark Souls 2 the levels just have areas that you go to, beat the bosses, reach a primal bonfire, light it and go back to Majula. They don't intertwine the areas to lead from one to another. There is actually a random small pointless area thats just a dead end. Like, what the hell were they thinking? WHY???
And my biggest complaint. The bonfires. They are everywhere this time around. I never felt relieved to reach a bonfire, or struggled to reach a bonfire, or even had to look for one that is hidden well. They just put the bonfires everywhere, and out in the open. It took a HUGE part out of the challenge of the game.
One of the BEST things about this game though is the DLC. The developers did a FANTASTIC job with the DLC areas and bosses. The DLCs are AMAZING. The level design was awesome and the bosses were actually difficult. Not only the bosses but the regular enemies themselves. It actually felt rewarding. Not only did the DLC pump of the difficulty and overall quality but they introduced some pretty sweet gear and spells to top it all off.
If you are looking for a challenge like I was you will be a little dissapointed. Despite all of these complaints about the game, it is still fun and well worth the money. The game has a lot of entertainment value. Even though it may not feel as rewarding as the other souls games, it offers more content to explore. I just prefer quality over quantity.
Overall 8/10

My honest review of Elder Scrolls Online:
- Character creation is pretty good. I can make my character look like Tom Cruise, so that's pretty cool.
- I usually skip the dialogue. That probably hints at something.
- Main story is weaaaak. I literally did not care about finishing the main plot. "The Prophet" who?
- Leveling up the character is fun. Gotta get all the skill points.
- I SWEAR IF I ACCIDENTLY HIT A CHICKEN INSTEAD OF A PERSON AGAIN, I'M GONNA LOSE IT.
- I'm pretty sure I saw a character named, "booty_licker69" so that's pretty 'ight.
- The world looks... plain. Not just because a lot of it is flat, but because it looks bland. No Man's Sky had more variety.
- I DID NOT KNOW YOU COULD QUICKSLOT UNTIL IT WAS TOO LATE.
- Your choices don't matter. The guards care more about how you treat a chicken more than you liberating a city.
- Tons of quests! Every time I walked into a city, I got a BUTT LOAD of new quests.
- Yeeeet, these quests don't feel completely developed. Many feel rushed and worthless.
- Tons of XP to earn. I did a thing and got a thing of XP. Thing.
If I had to rate Elder Scrolls Online. I would give the game a 6.5/10 dead chickens.
Mostly because of how rushed and under-developed it feels.
While it's definitely a fun "free-to-play" game, I don't see myself upgrading to ESO Plus anytime soon.
If you're getting this for free, I would recommend it.
But do not pay over $20 for it. It would not be worth it, especially with the lack of ESO Plus.

I went looking for a cheap RPG to play for a bit. What I found was a game that I put 20 hours into in two days. It already has plenty of content in for an early access game, is tons of fun (especially if you're like me, and loved Vampire: the Masquerade Bloodlines) and gets patched with bug fixes and new content extremely frequently. Like, sometimes patched multiple days in a row frequently. If you have limited bandwidth, you'll probably want to set this one to only update when you tell it to.  But this game is definitely worth a buy.
Still on the fence? Then check out the demo here:

: This is not Vampire the masquerade: XXXX, or anything like it (apart from the overall look and aesthetics of this title, although it is very reminiscing of the Vampire games) this is an action RPG where you delve into dungeons to find loot and complete quests, wich will help you with the main story line.
Every single bug i pointed as been fixed within 24h, the developer(it's only one, very impressive) actually listens and replies to your complaints. 10/10 for support.
The gameplay, apart from the main story line (wich will entertain you for 20h+), revolves around delving into deep (200+ floors!) dungeons(and now a creepy asylum) to dig up loot and pimp your character like many action RPGs. 10/10 for action RPG dungeon delving monster killing looting experience.
There are 3 classes to pick from(Warrior, Criminal(Rogue/thief like) and Witch), although there is the possibility to invest in whatever skills and stats you want, the class you choose will award you with an initial boost to your intended stat and skill set (and clan reputation) and give you a different look, you can also choose to be a Vampire,a Dhampir or a Shadowhunter wich will increase/decrease certain resistances and affect other things.

You can also pierce your nose to insert a baby-pin while wearing a top hat and a XVth century plague mask. 10/10 for weird customization purposes.
If you want to play Diablo in Bloodlines' world this is it.

This is the crowning jewel of pre-release games. I kid you not.
Day one, I found an exploit and two major bugs that could have wrecked the game. I pointed them out on the game forum. Day two, they were gone. The very next day I pointed out a couple interface anomolies, such as highlighting the slots where you place pieces of armor. Day three, they were gone. I pointed them out, and within the next six hours a patch arrived that addressed *minor* annoyances, and let me assure you they were minor--this is a pre-release game. I did not expect it to run well on my PC. I did not expect it without bugs.
No, I expected it to be a good game that required polish. Apparently, ONE designer did this whole game! If that's not polish, I'm not sure how teams of 17+ can complain. As far as gameplay, this is Vampire: the Masquerade: Bloodlines meets Diablo, as other reviewers have pointed out. What they have not pointed out is the nuances of dungeon crawling, such as secrets to be discovered, minor puzzles, and side areas nobody gets to discover. They even have lockpicking, keys, doors that require opening, and traps for the unwary adventurer. See? Diablo, this is not. It comes across as a homage to World of Darkness, in its raw form, but streamlined down to a very narrow interface which is easy-to-learn, hard-to-master. If you like vampires.
If you like dark fantasy.
If you like traditional fantasy.
If you like MMOs.
If you like RPGs.
If you like sci-fi.
If you like Chinese soap operas.
If you like dhampires.
If you like your mother.
Hell, if you like anything about PRE-release gaming, or even just gaming in general, BUY THIS IMMEDIATELY. If I could hold ten thumbs up I would! I can only hope the game progressively gets better from here. I feel I have gotten my full money's worth. A cinema ticket costs less! Seriously. Buy it! Games deserve this type of dev support. That's even without the synergy, and gameplay balance, here--that combine to make this video game more than the sum of its parts.
Even in its pre-release form, this is shaping up to be a visceral, and pulse-pounding (forgive the pun) experience. No kidding! Buy.
Just. Click. It.
EDIT: I have just gotten into the city areas. I will continue this review as I go. As it stands, the dev support alone has me sold on that movie theater ticket. ;)
UPDATE 9/27/2015 (Shortly after Release):
I cannot update my original opinions without altering the original review, so as of now, the visuals lack, but the gameplay is nicely polished. It adds up to a more action oriented experience than Bloodlines, but with more depth and sophistication than Diablo. I would ding it slightly for not being as polished as a commercial release, but that is where that ends. In spite of graphics, this is a monumental achievement for one man. For the price of a movie ticket, you get a first-person Diablo, in a World of Darkness-type setting, that nails gameplay and displays polish. Please note this is an independent release, and I think the price tag nicely suits it, though I would have paid $29.95 for the gameplay I got out of it, minus that other games are now haunting my time (Beware of Steam sales!) In conclusion, I would not buy it purely for boredom, but it is one of those "in-between" games where you can engage your RPG addiction before moving onto the dozen or so commercial releases stacked in your library. I would nicely rank it 8/10. Maybe an 8.5 if you like vampires or ARPGs.

I often read Visual Novels, and I must admit that this one was pretty good. If not my favorite for now.
I related a lot to the main character: being somewhat without any purpose in life, cynical, detached from everything. Even if he somewhat lack of social skills, and how to deal with these girls.
About the girls: they seemed to have a rich background and interesting personalities.
This visual novel is very humor oriented, and it's true that's sometimes it becomes annoying. But besides that, the story is very well written, with a touch of poesy and vivid descriptions of sensory experiences.
The art style is awesome, there's a lot of different interactions and illustrations for a visual novel. Some music are awesome, and some are somewhat mediocre. So I'm a bit reserved about it.
But the quality of the dialogues, and interactions between characters are absolutely awesome. I think that I will rarely found such quality elsewhere.
(I've only finished one path, but there wasn't any explicit erotic scene, and I must admit that it is better that way. I prefer when this type of content is implicit. I've not done all paths though.)
What can I add? The beginning can look long, but in the end it's worth it. The story is growing like a flower, slowly but it is beautiful. Full of intelligence and humor. The author have a lot of imagination, and shows us that even happiness can be reached with such anodyne things in life. And that we can understand each point of view, because if someone behave a certain way, there is a reason to such a behavior.
The price is certainly what makes me buy it, because I was really surprised that a VN could be so expensive. But know I understand this fact. And it is somewhat justified. If you want to read a VN, I really recommend this one.
Very strongly emotional game. Worth your time any way you look at it. Give the game some time and it will wedge it's way into your heart and tear it to shreds... in a good way.

If I was to sum up what I thought of this game, it would probably be this.
Smite is the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ son of League of Legends, raised with the loving care of innovation.
The reason I state it like this, is due to a few reasons which I'll list below as pros and cons.
Pros:
--First and most obvious, it's an over the shoulder MOBA, I don't know of a single MOBA out there that has done this before Smite
--Second. The gods are all quite unique in their own rights, sure you have different patheons with gods that would technically rule over the same domain (zeus and thor come to mind, thunder/lightning[correct me if i'm wrong]) but their skills and abilities are different.
--Third. There are numerous game modes you can play and usually a rotating special game mode every so often.
--Fourth. These game modes each have a different average play time. So if you're short on time, that you can't play a full game of conquest, maybe you go and play joust or arena.
--Finally even conquest is a fairly low time game mode. 30 minutes in league and dota are usually the avg time for a good game for one side or the other. Smite, games tend to go from 18-25 minutes for a LONG game. The reason being if one team starts getting wildly out of control the other can surrender and not suffer through being farmed in the base. Also when a god gets an item, it gives them a substantial boost towards their abilities which pushes the team with the most items to snowball and win faster.
-------------
With that all out of the way, you may be wondering why I still gave this game a negative review.
Cons:
--First and most importantly (and in my mind the biggest problem I have with the 'FTP' MOBA's) is the fact that 95% of the heroes are locked to start the game for a new player. Which pretty much means, it actually isn't FTP you have to chuck out the 30 bucks it takes to unlock all the gods or you pretty much abandon any other game to grind out the in game currency.
--Second. Is the god rotation. Most FTP MOBA's resort to this as a way to incentivise you to play the game even if you don't want to up and buy a god to start.You get this god rotation of 6 or so gods that may not fit the style of play that you actually enjoy. The rotations I went through were just not gods that I wanted to try at all and I kept wondering when I'd actually get a chance to try out the gods that I wanted to play like Loki, Athena, Aphro, Thanatos and a few more. And sometimes, the rotations are of extremely complicated gods that would take a while to learn to play properly. Then you sometimes get the gods that are currently out of the meta or just relatively underwhelming and get stomped no matter what god you get.
--Third. This is fairly frustrating to me but they don't explain very well what each type of god does, ie mage, assassin, adc, and Guardian. My point about this comes from one question, Who's the support? guardian sounds the most like but then you look at some of the mages and assassins and there are gods that look more like support characters than the guardians. I mean, aphrodite has a buff for allies that shares healing, invulnerability and movement speed, doesn't that sound more like a support god than a damage mage?
Now, you may ask, Stray, why when you put more pros than cons does this get a negative review? Well, the reason for that is that if you call it a FTP game it should be free to play, the base of a MOBA are the gods/heroes/champions and their interactions with each other. When you lock all of them behind a pay wall and tease players with a rotation that's mediocre at best, that's not free to play. Just get rid of the FTP and calling the ultimate god pack DLC and just say that smite is 30 dollars.

After a very long time of avoiding Broforce because of what kind of game I was
it to be, I was finally convinced to try it co-op with a cousin.
I was sold within five minutes.
First of all, it is not a pixelized vomit of jingoistic patriotism. It's satirical in the way of
. Your commander sends you into areas to "liberate" them (read: kill everything that moves) with lines like "They said I couldn't identify this country on the map. LIBERATE THEM." The villain that needs to die in most locations is the devil, a clear jab at the characterization of America's enemies as "evildoers". The bros pound "vitamins" (steroids) and flex to frighten enemies.
Any damage kills your bro, so a lot of the game is spent carefully avoiding a hailstorm of bullets, or an accidentally triggered series of uncontrolled explosions. If you die with lives remaining, or if you free a captive bro, you instantly change to another bro. This means that you have an opportunity (and requirement) to learn each one, which I find far more interesting than being able to choose from them.
+ A good variety of "bros". There are about 35 at time of writing, and they are each different enough to be interesting.
+ Every bro is from an action movie, and part of the fun sometimes is figuring out who they are, especially if you're (like me) old enough to remember most of them. Their abilities and melee attacks are all based on the films, which shows great attention to detail.
+ Bros are responsive and agile, and controls are snappy. This is good news considering the number of objects you'll need to dodge.
+ Great support for co-op play. My preferred way to play any campaign is co-op, and this game doesn't shortchange you for playing with friends.
+ Surprising attention to detail and level of nuance for such a simple game. For example, Predator's spears stick into walls and can be used as jumping surfaces.
= Levels are quite short (usually) and there are many checkpoints. Despite the constant risk of death from all sides, these things decrease the overall difficulty of the game (even on hard) and some may find that to be hand-holding.
= Gameplay gets very chaotic at times, with friendly actions resulting in a lot of character deaths. You
require a sense of humor about dying and restarting levels in order to enjoy this game.
= Bros vary widely in usefulness, playability, and overall power, so you have to accept that sometimes luck plays a role in how well you do.
= There could have been more non vanilla white males bros, but I'm not going to ding them on it because they pull all the bros from action movies, and it's the bias there that makes this difficult.
- The bros vary so much in power that some feel pointless. I've yet to find
use for a couple of them.
- The system for distributing lives in co-op is kind of stupid. Rather than going into a general pool, they go to the person picking them up, so it's easy to have one player with tons of lives and another who's dead. It's not difficult to do the accounting for yourselves, but it the game should do that.
- While the game has great co-op value for 2 players, it's chaotic beyond any reasonable tolerance at 3 or 4. The game doesn't have friendly fire, but chain reaction explosions from stray bullets are common, and it only takes one hit to die.

Dishonored 2 expands upon the tried-and-true gameplay and world of Dishonored and is one of the better FPS/stealth offerings in the last few years.  The skills feel familiar, but improved in certain ways, and still lend themselves to several different approaches to each objective.  The non-lethal playthrough, in particular, requires more creativity as most "boss" characters are immune to simply stealthing about and disabling them directly.  The chaos system may not be terribly noticable on a single playthrough, but it is very apparent if you do decide to use the New Game+ option.
There were optimization issues with the game upon release but those issues have certainly been resolved at the time of playing (December 2017).  I had zero issues with a GTX 1070 GPU.  I did not experience any glitches or crashes.
I very rarely play a game through a second time, but there's enough variety in playstyle that the game encourages a second look.  My first playthrough was on the order of 20 hours and the second was likely around half that time, as I knew the maps and key locations.  The bonecharm crafting was a little disappointing and some of the skills didn't feel intuitive.  But I would highly recommend this game for anyone who enjoyed the Dishonored.

First of all, you have to consider that THIS IS NOT A GAME BASED ON THE WORLD OF DARKNESS WORLD, so it isn't related at all with Vampire Masquerade Bloodlines, or Vampire Masquerade Redemption. Nevertheless, it reminds of these two games pretty much on several details, like it is set in an urban modern vampire's underworld, it's pretty atmospheric, it's pretty much a role game that allows you to make choices and it features a bunch of vampire clans with its own habilities.
But BloodLust: Shadowhunter is pretty much a game on its own: it displays an open world, dungeon-crawler-oriented universe with a number of NPCs, plenty of loot-searching and dungeon-crawling exploration (dungeons are large and may have up to 200 levels).
On the down side, when you play the game you soon realize some features are a bit rough round the edges and need more polish: the graphics aren't bad, but they are a bit out of date. So are some mechanics, models, aesthetics and animations, but still, they are ok and they show a certain amout of detail in their design. The voice-acting is good, considering it's an amateur work, but could be much better and more varied if the developers spent some money on hiring professional actors.
As an early access game, it is common to find glitches and bugs still, but as a whole, the game is quite solid and playable at this moment, and most of the bugs are being fixed by the developer.
In sum, the game needs polish and could reach a very high standard if more people would be involved in the development (most of the work has been done by just one person, which, given the final result, is really impressive).
On the up side, the game is pretty atmospheric and dark, and you play some sort of vampire "tomb raider", so you constantly depend on flashlights. Dumb idea, considering you control a vampire and they can see in the dark? Not really, the dependency on flashlights really adds atmosphere to the gameplay, more considering enemies tend to spawn from the air at every corner, and otherwise you're alone in the dark and won't see a thing except distant lights and glowing eyes gazing at you.
The combat mechanics are quite decent and as a vampire you have plenty of fancy powers and abilities to use against your enemies. You also have the ability to sire some NPCs, command them to carry out different tasks and make your own clan. There's also a vampire clan system, so you can allign with one or another clan and improve your renown among them (which translates into learning their habilities).
BloodLust: Shadowhunter is a more straight-forward game than VM. Bloodlines, it lacks a bit of its charisma or personality, but in some ways it takes the game experience further and expands it, in comparison with the Vampire Masquerade game.
All in all, BloodLust: Shadowhunter offers hours and hours of exploration, fighting, looting, dungeon-crawling and good fun, if you are ready to forgive the usual glitches and unfinished and out of date look of some models and mechanics. Still, consider it is an early-access game and is still beta, and the developer is working hard to polish things and fix bugs in an almost daily basis...
For me, it is definitely a game worth playing, and an ambitious and promising one. If you like proper vampire games, give it a try. In the end, this is the only serious attempt to a good vampire pc game we have had in years -and a successful one.

Let me start out by saying this is not a bad game by any means. There's a lot to be impressed with considering the game was put together almost entirely by one man. I respect that, and he did a lot of things right. For instance, some of the melee combat seems decent, there are some varied vampiric disciplines (spells/powers) you can cast/use. The game even has a Diablo-style loot system with items of different levels of quality, scrolls of identification, etc., 200-floor dungeons that randomly generate their arrangement with more XP and loot rewards the deeper you go, etc.
Although there are flaws with each of these, they're mostly done very well and I know this was a lot of hard work for the developer. The city map looks quite nice. It's a small, urban cityscape. Businesses are still open, though some have closed, and it looks good. A tree is growing out of a curb on one street I noticed, which looks cool, but the city looks too active for that to make sense. Weird, but I'm fine with it, even if it does make me scratch my head. One final note on the positives for this game: most of the music "works" and isn't very noticable, which is just fine, while a couple of the songs (tattoo parlor radio and main city hub in particular) were enjoyable and set the mood, respectively.
That said, I was at odds deciding whether or not to give it my recommendation. Simply knowing few people were involved in the game's creation, the fact it's (at the time of this review) still in early access, and it was decent enough that I could play it as long as I did...these things make me want to give it a recommendation, but those aren't particularly good things about the game.
At the time of releasing the early access of this game, the store page shows the developer estimated 2-3 months before it would leave early access. When I talk about the negatives about this game, I'll keep in mind that this is the state of the game now if someone purchases it, and that the negatives I will point out will not be ones I expect the developer to address within that estimated time frame due to the extremities of these negatives.
Like I said, it's not a bad game; just an okay one I couldn't get into despite having a big interest in the subject matter and genre. Here are some of the negatives:
The NPCs are very poor characters for the most part. The rare few who seem to have the slightest bit of personality are okay at best. The world also feels extremely empty. I don't mean bleak or hopeless; those are great for this kind of setting. No, I mean that there just aren't enough NPCs around for you to interact with or even those that just wander around making the world feel inhabited. I have encountered a total of three NPCs in the big city hub's streets. Imagine if Santa Monica in Bloodlines or Prague in Redemption had a total of 3 NPCs on the streets at night. Each building typically features 1-3 NPCs in it, with the exception of the night club, which I believe has 5 or 6. Many of these do not speak or give quests.
I just don't feel supernatural in this game, despite playing as a vampire. I wanted to play as a monster; not as an average person in the game's world. By not having a real human presence, my character is the average, normal person in the setting. I've only seen 3-4 NPCs which seemed to be human, and none of them are actual characters. One of them was just a random human to send to vampires to feed on, and the other three just lay or wander around until you turn them into vampires. Once you've done that, you're in a world without humans. That takes much of the fun out of being a vampire in the game. What's worse, it makes no sense that this many vampires can sustain themselves in a city without humans. There aren't any "vampires require invitations to enter homes" rules that the game has mentioned, so it's unlikely that the humans are just asleep at home, and as Bloodlines, Redemption, the real world, and many other games have shown, fair amounts of people are outside at night in urban areas. Even vampires aren't walking around the city aside from the player.
Humans seem to know all about vampires as well, because one of the three humans on the city streets says something to the effect of "Oh, your teeth. You're one of those monsters, aren't you?" Although Shadowhunters (vampire hunters) exist, regular humans seem to know about vampires' existence. It feels so awkward without in-game lore and explanation to make sense of vampires' place in this world. Despite there being five vampire clans, bunches of items, a number of powers and enemies, there just isn't much in the way of lore/explanations for things to understand the setting and get into it.
The story is almost non-existent so far, and I've gone through several main quests thus far. The game begins as you wake up in a sarcophagus, freshly turned, and get a message from your sire to come find her. You don't know who she is and you need to get out of some ruins and go to a tattoo parlor to find her. Everything that's been happening since then is a boring fetch quest of sorts. The plot developments haven't interested me or surprised me, and today, I loaded the game up to continue, opened my quest log, and just stared at it, blinking, thinking to myself "Why am I still playing?", and then quit. I'd been forcing myself to play as far as I'd gotten, and absolutely nothing sounded fun to do, even if it just meant going to kill things in the 200-floor dungeons. If a game doesn't have a setting or story interesting enough to interest me in continue, the gameplay must be absolutely fantastic for me to get past that, and the gameplay is just "decent." The controls and combat are comparable to blood lines, which isn't a good thing, though it is a little bit smoother when it comes to melee. You fight in third person and can use a variety of spells/disciplines. I haven't tried the ranged weapons, though I hear you will run out of ammunition pretty often at present. I will say that the combat is better than VtM Redemption's, but that combat was pretty awful (great story, though).
At the end of the day, I had no motivation to play the game and found myself uninterested in the setting and what I was doing in it the more I played, despite loving vampires and enjoying action RPG antics. Its actual gameplay wasn't enjoyable enough to drive me just by itself, and the story and characters are very forgettable with rare exception. This is not a bad game, but it just isn't all that good. That said, the developer really should be proud of what he's accomplished and I applaud him for his hard work, but I simply cannot recommend playing this game. I have many technical issues with the game which I haven't mentioned, but I won't hold them against the game in this review, because I believe the developer is still looking into them. The things I've covered here as negatives, though, seem highly unlikely to change or change sufficiently, given the amount of time and money involved in changing/adding to them.

The Fruit of Grisaia is the first of the Grisaia Trilogy. The Fruit of Grisaia is a visual novel where you take the role of transfer student, Kazami Yuuji as he enters Mihama Academy and hopes for an "ordinary" school life. As the story progresses, you will come upon the 5 heroines of the novel namely: Sakaki Yumiko, Suou Amane, Komine Sachi, Matsushima Michiru and Irisu Makina. Each heroine has their own unique story and personality.
As said by most players, this is a very long visual novel with a lineup of up to 32 scenes/chapters on the common route alone excluding the around 17+ scenes/chapters for the heroine's actual arc. The price of the game is well worth it because aside from its very long content, it also features the whole CG Gallery, Scene Replay and Music Collection unlike other Visual Novels in Steam where the CG Gallery and other features are removed from the actual VN. I finished this Visual Novel by around 50+ hours. After finishing one of the 5 arcs, you'll also unlock a Secret feature but I'll let you see it for yourself once you get your own copy of The Fruit of Grisaia.
I recommend this game to big fans of visual novels. This ain't for you if you can't stand to read a lot of content because this is really a very long novel. The content of the novel is very well written and packs quite a lot of humor. Each chapter/scene, whether its a common route or a heroine's arc, is very much worth every minute of your time. From the cuteness of Yumiko to Michiru's clumsiness, the novel will give you quite a feel of watching an actual anime episode. If you're looking for some humor with a mix of drama and feels, this is one of Steam's best Visual Novel available! If you don't believe me, then see and feel it for yourself!

Fruit of Grisaia is a visual NOVEL not a dating sim; you will be reading for hours before you make your first choice and another hour before you make your second choice. The story is a long and rambling account of a strange guy going to an obscure school of only five weird female students. Yes the setup is absurd, but Fruit of Grisaia knows it and goes with it.
As a novel I have to say how good the writing is since it is often thought provoking and emotionally touching. The problem is that those good moments are amongst a sea of silly-stupid encounters with those girls. That sillyness is fine if you like over-the-top Japanese cutesy schtick, but it's incredibly annoying if you don't. All the girls are to some degree frustrating-annoying with the Micharu girl being way off the scale. Michiru is so bad she is obnoxious. Makina is annoying but you later learn about her inner demons and why she is who she is. In fact, all of the main characters have their backstories developed wonderfully. Every character has their own genuine motives, wow. Micharu is still a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥
Other than the story: the art is lovely and each of the characters can be individually muted. Use the scroll wheel down to advance the story.
Overall I admit I like Fruit of Grisaia. I give it a 7 out of I-Don't-Do-Scores.

I nominated this for Best Singleplayer Story Narrative in the make your own category. For me, at the time this came out almost twenty years ago originally around the same time frame as the first Half Life game it had a story and background elements that unfolded and left a mark in your mind as you progressed through it.
I still have the retail box cd version of this tucked away in a box in the closet with a bunch of other games. The thing about this one to me was because it was a Real Time Strategy game and not a First Person Shooter that took storytelling in an original idea at the time and framed it beautifully for the kind of game it is.
The introduction sequences along with the first few levels is some of the best opening gameplay of any game I have ever played. It's why I nominated this because I still remember it to this day without having played it in so long until this remastered version came out.
The writing is top notch, what I liked best about it was playing and hearing all the little combat chatter from units the choices of words that were used. Similar to how I love the combat chatter from the units in the StarCraft games.
Can't say the same about a lot of games I have played. It also really helps if you are a big fan of the genre in both science fiction and real time strategy games. That old classic resource gathering base building model from the command and conquer games is used to a great effect in this game.
At the time this game took that formula and put into 3D space, you no longer were scrolling across a 2D map. You played this game and had 360 degree awareness all around your mothership.
The guys at Relic Entertainment came up with what's called the Sensors Manager for the game to handle that extra dimension and it was mind blowing when you saw it for the first time way back then.
Because it was in real-time, you didn't wait for it to load up. You tapped the space bar and toggled it on and off at will, it's a common feature now but back in the early 2000's when you first used that it was fantastic.
beautiful, enthralling, time-devouring.

Overall Dark Souls 2 is a great game. It has plenty of content. There are tons of bosses, an insane amount of areas to fight through, and a plethora of armor and weapons. Just like the previous souls games there is also a lot of replay value.
However, out of the games in the souls series, this was unfortunately my least favorite.
Don't get me wrong, it is a great game that i do recommend playing. But if you have played the previous souls game, this one might be a little bit of a dissapointment. I found the areas to be too easy to progress through. The challenge just wasn't there. Enemies movesets are slow and predictable. Even if you mess up and get hit, it doesn't matter that much; the enemies don't hit very hard. To add along to their low damage they also have low health. It felt like the developers toned down the difficulty a lot. Maybe to appeal to new players to the series.
The bosses are also incredibly easy. I beat the majority of the bosses in one try. They added A LOT more bosses in this game than usual. It seemed like they sacrificed difficulty for quantity. I would rather have few and difficult bosses than many and easy. In the other souls games I usually got that ♥♥♥♥ YEAH feeling when I beat a boss but this time around I rarely got that feeling; it didn't feel rewarding. I WANT to get destroyed by bosses. I WANT to have to focus and actually be skillfull to succeed. This is not the case though. Even the final boss failed to deliver a challenge. I, and many others, beat the final boss in one try and often refer to the final boss as a joke.
To add on to lackluster bosses and enemies. the level design just wasn't Dark Souls style. In the first Dark Souls you often found the areas of the map to intertwine in this magnificent fashion. This once again was a huge part of the first dark souls that I loved and wasn't delivered this time around. In Dark Souls 2 the levels just have areas that you go to, beat the bosses, reach a primal bonfire, light it and go back to Majula. They don't intertwine the areas to lead from one to another. There is actually a random small pointless area thats just a dead end. Like, what the hell were they thinking? WHY???
And my biggest complaint. The bonfires. They are everywhere this time around. I never felt relieved to reach a bonfire, or struggled to reach a bonfire, or even had to look for one that is hidden well. They just put the bonfires everywhere, and out in the open. It took a HUGE part out of the challenge of the game.
One of the BEST things about this game though is the DLC. The developers did a FANTASTIC job with the DLC areas and bosses. The DLCs are AMAZING. The level design was awesome and the bosses were actually difficult. Not only the bosses but the regular enemies themselves. It actually felt rewarding. Not only did the DLC pump of the difficulty and overall quality but they introduced some pretty sweet gear and spells to top it all off.
If you are looking for a challenge like I was you will be a little dissapointed. Despite all of these complaints about the game, it is still fun and well worth the money. The game has a lot of entertainment value. Even though it may not feel as rewarding as the other souls games, it offers more content to explore. I just prefer quality over quantity.
Overall 8/10

This game quickly goes from "Ok, cool" to "I have not slept for 15 hours and I loved each and every one of them".
Some backstory: Factorio is a survival game with all of the bad parts cut out. You have no hunger bar, manual grinding is not encouraged, and automation actually makes things run faster. It's made to look (and, to an extent, play) like a mid-90s RTS, and even though I've never played one other than RCT2, I still think this aesthetic works in its favor. What does the game play like? Well, you know in Minecraft how once you get bored of digging 1:2 shafts in the ground you set up a crazy machine to do it for you? This is an ENTIRE GAME about that feeling. It's the type of game where you can make your own computer from chests and wires. It is the BEST feeling.
My only issue is the online. Creative/survival games often have online be a big focus: It's fun to collaborate to ease some of your own workload and help others with what they want to do. I don't think the devs had this in mind. Connections are Peer To Peer, meaning that servers are designed for LAN connections or only a handful of nearby connections. This means you have to manually enter in someone else's IP. This is REALLY a pain. Every time someone joins, everyone on the server has to wait for them to download the map. And downloading is SLOOOOOW. For some reason, it downloads about 1/5-1/8 slower than my usual download speed (server load? i don't know). And when someone on the server lags. EVERYONE lags. Sometimes I can hardly play because of the lag. I know this game has a mid-90s aesthetic, but I didn't want it come with mid-90s modem-speed. This is excusable, at least: Multiplayer only came out a few updates back, and after all the game is still in early access. But the sooner multiplayer is better optimized, the better.
Well, if you like your games single-player, just disregard that. And who cares about netcode when you have a fudging MASTERPIECE on your hands?
Buy it now.
Buy now and meow

Among many thing that this game gets right, it's the ATMOSPHERE.
The art style blends in extremely well together. The character models, the background, the enemies, and even the UI. It just meshes together to really bring back a nostalgic feel that I feel a lot of old school MMO players would appreciate.
I also want to emphasize on another winning formula of this game; the music. Cerulean Wind, 3rd Wave, Due Solo. It's been a while since I played the beta, but I still remember the game themes clear as day.
If there's something they could have done more, is to provide a better information base within the game itself. While they've done an amazing job with this so far, there's still room for improvement.
- Show what upgrades do past not only the first level, in order to allow for better build planning. Sometimes, just increase in magic damage might not warrant the increased MP cost.
- Include what stats do in the tutorials list, again, for better understanding of which stat to build from. No need for the standard MMO formula, just show that it "increases max HP, increases HP regen" or whatever. Just basic text info. The formula should rightfully remain in the wiki for those who are curious even further.
- The miscellaneous stats, like magic amplification and block rate, should also be explained like in the first point.
- Include the name of the songs played while entering a new room at a corner somewhere on the screen. Will really help those who admire the music like me to get into the game more.

So I played this game on the CBT and I can say for certain that this game is pretty good.
It has a lot of classes that you can play, making it a pretty versatile mmorpg (even though the classes don't have that much of skills to upgrade), and each class has a specific clothing that you can change back to, even when you upgrade to a new class, if you like the older one more. It has this aspect of customization that is pretty nice.
The crafting, gems and etc system can be a bit confusing at the beginning, but it is also easy to use. It is not a very complex system, so those that really like crafting systems will probably feel a bit disappointed here (I didn't, but I still have to say that because I know that some people are really into this kind of thing).
The spells system is pretty straightforward, although the classes that use too much mana may feel a bit overloaded by the enemies, since their mana will go too fast and they won't manage to beat the monsters by pure sheer force. Classes like the Cleric are actually good to play alone, because it won't spend that much mana, be tanky and still have a bit of strength so they can continuously attack the enemy.
The game is pretty good for beginners, overall, it will help you a lot and also feel pretty easy at the beginning. Although it will be a bit hard later. When you reach certain levels it becomes a huge problem to level up and you will need to grind. I really don't like this aspect of the game and think it is a cheap way to make it bigger, specially since, in this game, you'll reach huge levels like 200 level and more than that. You shouldn't need to spend a whole life only leveling one character, it is more fun to have a lot characters and if you want to level each one to the "max", it will take a whole lot of time.
But, the game is fun. And also pretty. Since it is a F2P game, you can play it for a while and leave when you want to. So I can't not recommend it.

TL;DR: A game that starts off really good, but the later levels and characters drag down the tight gameplay.
This is one of those games that I really wish there was a third option between Yes and No. When I first booted it up and played it for an evening, I loved it. The second evening (that's all it took to finish it), it got me unbelievably frustrated. That is basically the juncture for the game. The first half plays out well, the game is fun, and the few drawbacks don't diminish it too much. By the end it is getting onto Kaizo Mario with RNG areas of frustrating.
Broforce is a side scrolling action game, reminiscent of Contra and Metal slug for the most part. You have one hit, and enemies will usually go down with one as well. Platforming is a little loose, but you can wall grab (depending on the character), and jump pretty well. The levels contain a wide variety of enemies to blow through, and each new one is introduced in sequence so you can adjust to the layers being added on. The levels themselves are almost fully destructible, barring some ladders and permanent platforms, so the fact that you can shoot through the ground and under/over traps and enemies adds some strategy to the levels. The levels are full of exploding objects, traps, things to drop on enemies and the like. Each level is broken up into different stages in sequence that you have to finish, usually with a boss fight at the end.
The key factor in the game are the characters. You start with one, and every so many rescues you unlock a new 'bro' to play as. The rescues also act as lives, but at the same time change your character every time you rescue someone. I will touch on why this becomes problematic later, but suffice to say you will probably play 3-4 different characters per level. The characters are all parodies of various movie characters, usually from the 80s and 90s, but there are some more recent characters in there. Each one has their own unique shooting attack, special items, and sometimes other features (McGuyver has sticky bombs, there are some melee oriented characters, etc). Each does feel rather fleshed out, and a lot of thought was put into making them unique. The cast gets pretty huge later on, and I'll talk about the issues there in a moment. Some of the characters do get unique levels just for them, built around how they play, but these are few and far between, maybe six of those stages for the whole game.
There is no story to speak of. You are a team of Bros, who go kill terrorists, then aliens, then demons. If you're angry about a spoiler....seriously?
As I said before, the game started out great. During the terrorist part of the game, the controls were tight, the bosses were unique and varied, and the bros I unlocked were interesting to play. Some were less useful than others in certain situations, but I felt I could make do with whoever, and at least make some progress before I died and switched to a different character. The first ten or so characters are clearly the best designed, and while there are some nice ones later on, I feel the game could have stuck with these and been fine.
After the terrorist stages come the alien stages. There are still terrorists in some parts of the stages, usually fighting with the aliens, but most of what you are fighting are aliens. In general, they mostly rush and either grab or bite you, with a few dive bombing flyers very rarely. This starts to cause issues. With the terrorists being slow to react and easy to sneak up on or climb above/below, you could always adopt your strategy to whoever you were playing. The aliens don't really have a strategy, and you can't really sneak up on them or rely on them to panic like the terrorists. Things like McGuyvers sticky bombs become useless, as you can't rely on the alien running to its friends...its just going to run to you and kill you, making every time you get him a waste. Other characters have some similar issues, as the game starts to add more and more, and less of them are actually useful to the stage. By this time you'll have unlocked a few melee characters, right around the time the enemies who explode on death you need to be -far- away from, and sometimes the aliens beat you in melee due to no fault of your own. Our bosses start getting less interesting as well, two of them are basically repeats (Giant worm that spits acid, and giant worm that spits acid and shoots rockets), and we start running into issues of bosses with very particular needs that will just screw you if you get the wrong character. In this part of the game, you will repeat a boss quite often, just hoping to get the right character with a special ability you can spam to chew through its health. Its cheap, but they fill the screen with so much scenery chewing garbage its the only winning strategy.
On to the hell levels...and this is where the game starts to become absolutely frustrating. Now you're unlocking characters like the girl from Grindhouse (Can only shoot down unless she's ducking and not moving, special only shoots down), 007 (weak gun, four entirely different specials), and Conaan (What the hell is with that wierd 'slight jump and swing' thing?) who basically serve to waste your lives. They do have very situational uses, but with so many characters unlocked, you likely will get them at exactly the wrong time. In addition, with so many very situational and unique characters, you are probably really missing the fact that more of them didn't get special levels to teach you how to play them, or the fact that you can't disable certain really bad ones. We are long past the point where Bruce Willis from Diehard is ever useful, as his gun is short ranged, his stun bombs are useless on bosses and most enemies. Most of the stages now are a mess of explosions, exploding enemies, random traps, pits, and basically a mad rush to get to the next helicopter save point so you don't have to start at the beggining again. Lets not forget the occasional short 'make it all the way to the end of this mess and don't die once' stage, where you will die many times because you didn't get the jumping just perfect...in a game with floaty controls. The bosses are ridiculous, and you are just waiting to get the right characters in order to beat them, not to actually learn their patterns...there is usually just too much stuff going on at once. Also, this part of the game has two more worm bosses, basically the same, one being by itself, another being a pair of them that are even more ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t.
So the review is basically my descent into the game. The start is great and enjoyable, the middle is ok, the end is frustrating and awful. For two evenings of playtime even with all the deaths, I'm not sure its worth full, half, or even humble bundle pricing. Writing the last paragraph reminded me why I got so angry at the game, and I'll have to give it a thumbs down...and remember people, I played on the easiest setting...there's an ironbro campaign where every death kills that character for good, and its game over if you lose all of them. I can't imagine anyone finishing that on normal or hard, especially with the last few stages being ridiculously hard.

Always good to play an Arkane game. I think this is improved over the first game, though I wasn't able to play the DLC for the first game. The level design seems like an improvement.
