I have never done a review before and I don't write too much so this will most likely seem like a very sloppy review however I feel the need to speak out for this great game. Rather than a review this will most likely be highlighting good points, there are obviously bad points to every product in existence so this will mostly be telling you why I think this game is amazing rather than comparing to other products and rating it accordingly.
I highly recommend this game to anyone who is familiar with and enjoys anime/manga. I relate this to these specific people because most people who will read light novels or play VN's will most likely touch this game if not play through it.
I think that this visual novel is an extremely good first visual novel as it offers a very rich and enjoyable storyline with characters that really make this game great. The choices are very simple and obvious. The only question you will have to ask yourself when you play this game is "Which girl shall I choose" and from that point you will be able to enter said route. However this can be a downside for those who choose according to the situation and like to see who they end up with. However the choices are not dull in determining good ends and bad ends. Sometimes the game will have you wanting to choose what will end up as the bad end and this can be very surprising and this brings life to the game. However the choices are ultimately very few and simple so I will state what is really good about this game.
The characters.
Ok first of all- Kazami ♥♥♥♥ing Yuuji. This is the character that you will play as and you will fell like batman or some♥♥♥♥♥♥when you are reading this VN. The fact that his background is mysterious when playing through this game adds a great amount of enjoyment throughout the entire duration of the game.
I will not go into detail for every single girl but just like a good VN should it caters to alot of different taste (even though some may be wrong) and has a very unique different story for each girl that does not make replaying every route worse than the first one you played through. I will mention one character Michiru I personally do not think that she is best girl per se. However this is honestly the first time I have seen the character of "Girl trying to pretend to be a tsundere" and I say trying to pretend because it is blatantly obvious and this causes for some great comedy scenes.
Playing the game-
I personally learned alot through this game, whether it be a way to approach or think about life. Or mearly just a quote from Kazami's 'Master" this game will introduce many new ways of thinking and approaching problems that you may have not thought of before. You will enter our main characters thought process and adapt to his methods of handling situations that you may be able to relate to in your own life. This is ultimately very situational but even if they do not relate to you specifically this can be extremely engaging and enjoyable.
The game has a very smooth progression that is paced extremely well in my opinion.
You may find that your life will be based around playing this game and spending all your free time on this throughout your first play through. This is very normal however this can be a bad point for some people.
The Soundtrack-
I love this soundtrack. From the moment you open the game for the very first time to the opening to the appropriate music for the right scene to the ending songs. I love everything about this soundtrack.
The Story-
Obviously as a story oriented game how can this be anything but amazing. The thing I like the most about the story however is the fact that every story is so unique to the point that playing through every story does not feel like you are repeating the game, rather playing say a set of 4 sequels to your first choice.
Dark aspects-
This game is not afraid to explore some dark aspects and sometimes can be slightly uncomfortable to read for some people (such as blatantly describing starvation). This is honestly one of the main reasons why I rate this game so highly. The story will get serious at an increasingly genius pace. They will relate every girl to a typical character you may have seen before and then show you that everything may not just be sunshine and [loli]pops!
Great CGI and Voices-
While playing this game you will really feel like you are interacting with the characters. This is extremely important for a VN and this game does it extremely well. The voice actresses/ors do a magnificent job in portraying every character/sidecharacter and the CGI will make it very easy to ascertain who you are talking to, when and how many people are in the scene. I cannot emphasize enough how important it is to do this properly and this game does it beautifully.
The Art-
When placed during the right scene the artwork in this game can bring a tear to your eye. The artwork is not merely but in many important scenes you can read many important traits of each character in how they are portrayed in the art and how they are feeling within the scene. This is so amazing in so many parts within this VN. However that is not only the case. The art does not only crop up in important scenes it remains amazingly consistent throughout the entire game allowing you to feel so much more in depth to the characters within almost every scene in the game.
In conclusion I think that this game is a great game to buy if you like anime/manga.This game is very well written and Sekai Project do not slack when it comes to translating properly, so you can expect some really great writing such as:
. Also added points for being able to choose the voice of your menu.
tl;dr
IF YOU HAVE NOT PLAYED A VN BEFORE BUT LIKE ANIME/MANGA PLAY THIS GAME

Total War: Rome 2 - Emperor Edition, is the Eighth game in the Total War series and was released in 2013. Plagued with Technical issues when it was first released, but seemingly much better now with the release of the Emperor Edition, Rome 2 takes place during the height of the Roman Empire, prior to it's fall and the start of the middle ages. Bringing back Naval Battles, absent from Seventh Total War, Shogun 2, Rome 2, is a worthy sequel in the Total War series. The cinematics give a much greater immersion in the overall game than previous titles in the series, and the new real-time combat engine looks really good. I like the immersiveness of it overall. The tutorial is pretty straight-forward and if you are familiar with previous Total War titles in the series, there is very little learning curve.
With Total War: Rome 2, Your armies are much more customizable. and in some instances such as costal cities, you can combine both Naval and Land-based forces to overwhelm and conquer your enemies. I found the battle portion of the gameplay to be very fast-paced and fun. The turn-based portion of gameplay is just as expansive as we've come to expect in the Total War series. Mercenaries, Diplomats, Spies, you name it, Rome 2 allows players to utiize them all. The game has 117 different factions, with more available through DLC's. Each faction has their own strengths and weaknesses, some focus on trade or combat, others are more diplomacy oriented. The Grand Campaign allows for you to chose between 9 different cultures, and one of 3 different factions houses. The Prologue campaign is essentially a tutorial, that introduces you to the workings of the game. I had fun with this.
Overall, I thought Total War: Rome 2 was pretty good. As with several of the newer Total War titles, there are multiplayer options available. Custom Battles, Historical Battles all make a familiar return. Rome 2 is put together in a nice, neat package. I am interested to see where the series goes from here.

UPDATED Hair Accessory Enchantment Odds and Prices
tl;dr: Cost to enchant a Hair Accessory with the exact 3 stats of your choice? $9,709.20 USD per Hair Accessory. Do you want specifically HP, SP, and Crit Damage all at perfect rolls? $5,126,457.60 USD per Hair Accessory. If you only care about getting AOE Ratio, regardless of any other stat on the item, it is only about $13.68. If you only care about a perfect PATK, and don't mind anything else, it would be $327.60 USD.
Edit: Post is for educational purposes only. I can't really take one side or the other anymore because the existence of the item may open pandora's box, or it may end here in its current form. I don't know. Hopefully this helps in your decision about how you feel about Magic Scrolls and the possibility of other RNG benefits IMC may introduce. All RNG formulated with an assumed (until proven otherwise) equal weighting. nizidr helped me realize there are multiple attribute types dealing with elemental damage, and possibly defense, that can stack on the same item. All odds updated from base 1:19 stats to 1:31 (1-17 stats remain the same, 18 Attribute Defense updated to 18-Holy 19-Dark 20-Fire 21-Lightning 22-Earth 23-Ice 24-Poison, 25 Attribute attack split into 25-Holy 26-Dark 27-Fire 28-Lightning 29-Earth 30-Ice 31-Poison) due to previous stats allowing multiple rolls from the same pool of options for those stats only. Appending the 1:19 values at the end for reference.
Firstly, as per IMC, 100TP = approx $9.00. From that we can discern that 1 TP = approx 9 cents and 8 TP (cost of Magic Scroll) = approx 72 cents.
So.. want to see the odds of getting the perfect 3 stats on your hair accessory using the Magic Scroll that IMC talked about?
In KToS there are 19 possible stats. Yes, this could change, but since they have confirmed the scroll coming to IToS we'll just have to use these numbers from KToS for now.
19 total stats to choose from and each scroll use has a chance to enchant either 1 stat, 2 stats, or 3 stats. However stat 18 and 19 have 7 sub-rolls each to account for Elemental Attack and Elemental Defense to a specific element. It also appears that while multiple elements can be rolled on to the same piece that no piece displayed thus far has two of the same elemental properties (i.e. a hat may have +Fire Attack, +Ice Attack, +Holy Attack, but not +Fire Attack, +Fire Attack, +Fire Attack) so this is incorporated into the equations at 1:31.
To get our wanted 3 stat types we'd take 31*30*29=26970, but, that is for sequential odds, and our stat order doesn't matter (HP,SP,CRIT is the same as CRIT, HP, SP for instance). If we give each of the three stats a number we'll see there are 6 combinations:
123
132
213
231
312
321
So we're taking 26970/6 to give us 1:4495, but since we can either roll a single stat, 2 stats, or 3 stats we multiply 4495 by 3 to get the final odds of achieving our ideal 3 stat types on our item at 1:13485.
For our costs we will simulate a faux 100% chance by saying if you rolled it that many times you will have been guaranteed the roll you want (even if we know this is not the case and you could re-roll hundreds of millions of times and still not get lucky).
So for a 1:13485 chance, just to get your 3 stat types, not including if the stat values are even high, you're looking at approximately $9,709.20 USD For one piece. $29,127.60 USD for all three pieces.
Going forward...
Most stats have a variance in what their values can be. For instance, PATK has a range between 21 and 45. 45-21=24, so there are a total of 24 different possibilities for the PATK stat to be. In this example, we'll say you don't even care what value the other two stats are and all that matters to you is having those stats plus a perfect PATK roll.
1:13485 for the 3 stats you want, but we're going to multiply that by 24 since 1:13485 is just the odds of getting all three stats at any random value. So to get a perf PATK and any value for the 2 other stats you want it is 1:323640.
Or, in translation, that roll is worth $233,020.80 USD in the cost of Magic Scrolls.
Now, a step further. What if you didn't care about the other stats at all and only want a perfect PATK value? This accounts for any random stats that accompany your wanted perfect stat of PATK, but also accepts the possibility you may not have any other stats on the item at all. To get this we first accept that the odds of getting PATK on a single stat roll are 1:31, but the odds for getting it on a double stat item are twice as good at 1:31/2 because there are now two possible stats on the item either of which that could be our PATK, and 1:31/3 for a triple stat item. PATK has a variance of 24 so we are looking at (1:31*24 + 1:31*24/2 + 1:31*24/3)/3 or (1:744 + 1:372 + 1:248)/3 which gives us 1:455, or $327.60 USD. Sounds more reasonable, possibly scarily so.
And if you only want, say, AOE Ratio? Well, that stat has no variance, and is locked at 1, so you are very likely to get it on your item with (1:31*1 + 1:31*1/2 + 1:31*1/3)/3 giving us roughly 1:19 or approximately $13.68 USD. The chances of getting a really good stat like AOE Ratio, that is always by default locked at its perfect value, is very high.
However, as per the example I listed in the other thread, let's say I want HP, SP, and Crit Damage, since these three stats have the highest possible variances. What are the odds of rolling perfect stats on all 3 of those on a single piece?
HP: 383 to 803, 420 possible values
SP: 76 to 150, 74 possible values
Crit Damage: 32 to 66, 34 possible values
Getting all 3 of those stat types is 1:13485, getting all 3 stat types with perfect HP is 1:5663700, with SP would be 1:997890, with Crit Damage 1:458490.. add those 3 since each is already its own perfect roll, so...
1:7,120,080...
That's roughly half chance of winning the lottery.
You're more than 7 times as likely to be struck by lightning this year at 1:960,000.

This review is an edit of my closed beta one. Now that I've had time with the game in early access, I've had to relook at my original review and add all the recent changes, good and bad.
First of all, the game is beautiful, and for any Ragnarok Online players, you'll notice a great similarity, since this is supposed to be its "spiritual successor". It feels, for the most part, like a 2d game set in a 3d world. I actually enjoyed the game, and it was pretty fun. However, with all games, there are always some points of discussion that will either make a game really good, or really bad, so I'll try to break it down with as much detail as possible.
Pros:
- Very easy to pick up for beginners
- Very easy to level early on via quests
- Character progression is customizable (stats and skills)
- Fast paced battles
- Easy to add members to your party
- Bosses are decently difficult
- Excellent market system (one of the best I've seen in an MMO aside from Guild Wars 2)
- In-game video recorder
Cons:
- Storage is small, and you have to pay real money to expand it
- (New) Trading is behind a paywall, and even then you can only trade 30 times per month
- Quests are too repetitive
- Too many quests; in the early game, the only ways to level efficiently is to do all the quests
- The sheer amount of quests makes the game too linear instead of being "open world", since you have to go to where the new quests are if you want to level at a steady pace.
- Without quests, the game becomes a bit grindy, much like Ragnarok Online (though not to that extent)
- The majority of bosses are very easy
- While there is character progression, most classes are forced to stick to repeating their same class (wizard -> wizard instead of wizard -> pyromancer for example) in order to achieve their maximum potential (DPS). If you switch too often, you miss out on a lot of skills, or reduce your DPS substantially in one skill just to obtain another.
- The game is very unforgiving about making mistakes when choosing classes. At this time, the only way to fix a mistake is to make a new character.
- In some cases, if you want to be a certain class, you're forced to stick to one single possible combination of classes in the skill tree in order to get to it.
- You have to research a lot online before choosing what you want to be.
Pre-release cons:
- The game is very laggy. Sometimes when you talk to NPC's, it wont register for 5 mins to half an hour. Sometimes all you can do is relog, and try again.
- There are lots of bugs from closed beta that still remain.
- Some quests are impossible to complete.
- Spam bots are rampant, mainly gold sellers.
- You are very limited in what you can sell on the market without a token. The cost of selling something on the market is 30% of its value vs 10% with a token. Essentially you're losing 1/3 of an items total value AND non-token users can only sell one item at a time. Token users can sell 5 at a time.
- Optimization is horrible.
In my honest opinion, the game handles more like a grid based RTS RPG, at least when skills are involved. As an example, cleric heals are squares that stay on the ground till an ally steps on it. Most of the cleric spells are squared.
Although there seem to be more cons than pros in my list, the game is still one of the best MMO's I've played in a very long time, and really fun to me, so I highly recommend at least trying it. However, the lag has pretty much killed the entire experience for me. The majority of the time in the afternoons (high traffic hours), I can't even play, and I just log off, despite wanting to get in some leveling. Its just impossible.
The game is not optimized at all, and your FPS can drop to as low as 5-10 if theres lots of people on screen (even on a high end PC). My advice is to add -dx11 in the steam launch options, to force the game to use all your available cores. Apparently, this game only uses a single core otherwise. Its also a good idea to disable all visual effects in-game.
I really do like this game, but I'll have to leave this as a negative review until the lag issues are resolved, and the horrible market and trading restrictions are changed. I'll change it if anything changes for the better.
Life is too short for not playing this game, for those who loved Ragnarok Online in his days, this is its successor!

STALKER: Shadow of Chernobyl is a game based entirely on the gameplay provided, as well as it's difficulty that stems from it's mechanics, and the hazards laid throughout the zone. The design, be it in the environment seemingly crafted from real-life examples to great detail, or the monsters themselves, as well as the great balance of guns and their somewhat realistic portraits conveyed through the game, is simply undeniably good, throughout balance with fights and environmental situations that can't fail but to make me a bit paranoid and scared.
The game, itself, falls short with it's story, however. The backstory behind the main character is explained well as time goes on, but the story itself is nothing but fetch quests and favors where you are rebounded across the entire country just to find out whom Strelok is, whenever the most people have given you is nothing short of, "Oh, I know this other guy who might know him." There is not much motivation to do it after that, and overall, it starts to become tedious within the first few hours of the game as you start to realize that the quests seem silly, as they're nothing but jumbled messes of situations haphazardly thrown together because you're trying to find a man, and even then, that logic goes straight out the window sometimes, so you're left with, "Just do it, because hey, you want to do it!" It is a good mechanic for a free-roaming STALKER game, but not for a man with such an objective in mind, which doesn't even matter until it is pulled up again later on in the game.
Anomalies in this game aren't exactly clever, save for a few. The majority of them are simply you getting harmed and then having to use a med kit, which is not much variety between the two, save for that one just stands there, and one pulls you in. The anomalies that go well beyond this, like making you go straight to bleeding badly as soon as you step in them, are good, for they experiment with what they can do, but overall, they just seem a lot like random environmental hazards, which don't really change positions at all.
The gunplay is favorable, and, in the right setting, STALKER has monsters and situations that just plain get to you, that really make you shiver in fear. There are flaws in the game, such as stashes being completely devoid of anything until you get the information of the stash itself, but overall, the experience that it makes you go through, as well as the balanced difficulty and unsettling environments, as long as they last before they get bombarded by human enemies out of nowhere, truly make the game what it is.
Do I hate this game? Not at all. Despite what I have stated, I could play STALKER: Shadow of Chernobyl lots and lots, and still find out new things, which recreates that magical spark that made me love the game whenever I first started playing it.
The gameplay is done to such a degree that it actually goes with the very theme of STALKER itself, which completely makes it all the more meaningful once you do discover what it is.
What is it, you ask?
Well, that's an answer that you'll have to find for yourself. The Zone is full of mysteries, but let it be known that you are like everyone else, improving and trying to live just a little better. Maybe, through the situations you find yourself in, you'll find out what it all teaches us sooner or later.

Let me start this out with how much I love the Dishonored series, excluding the Death of the Outsider simply due to the fact that I haven't played it (and also think its kind of a lame idea). But let me follow that up by saying Dishonored 2 is certainly no Dishonored 1. Dishonored 1 had a better slew of characters, and the DLC added even more depth to characters you hated for the main game and also introduces the main villian of dishonored 2. Now lets get into this review.
Dishonored 2 has a lot of goods and bads to it, but I feel the good out weighs the bad, and a lot the bad only exists in contrast to Dishonored 1. So I'll start with what makes the game great. It has tight controls, fluid combat, and a whole lot of ways to play the game. While your first playthrough limits what powers you can chose from, starting a new game + allows you to access all the powers in the game, through upgrades obviously. This allows for a lot of ways to play the game, from hoping into another person and walking past the guards, to spawning clones of yourself that can take out enemies at a distance. It's all in the way you decide to play. You can slaughter everyone, knock everyone out, or even just slip by entirely unnoticed. Not into hiding corpses of the dudes you killed? Summon a rat swarm to eat up those bodies. You can even reject getting any special powers and go through the whole game with just your weapons.
But there are some stains on the game. The story is the same for both characters, the only change being the voice connected to your character, and the thoughts they have. Personally, I like Corvo's character better. I feel like Emily developed weird and she doesn't really feel like the same person you were protecting in the first game. I get that she got older, and is empress, and whatever. But I feel like they didn't really do her justice when it comes to developing her character. I also feel as though they simply recycled the villian from the first game's DLC. Like they couldn't make a good new villian so they just popped in an old one. Although I have the feeling that there are not too many space RTS games, and I feel like there are even less massively popular RTS games, Homeworld is to me that one space RTS game that stood the test of time.
Whereas many other attempts at space games usually result in big empty 2d grids on which you play in a fancy 3d arena Homeworld did one thing that many still do not do today: It played in true 3d. Now you could argue that it doesn't matter that much for actual gameplay, and perhaps you are right. But the sheer sense of 'space' and 'freedom' you have when you can tell ships to fly to any part of the map, no matter how high or low, gives it way more immersion than any '2d' grid-locked space RTS game ever could. The base game itself may have aged a bit, but some of the mods (PDS, Complex and many others) managed to spice it up in such a way that it was back up to par compared to many other space games. And now with this remastered edition it's still a treat to the eyes as well.
Unit variety is done through variations of ships in different classes, which beforementioned mods greatly expand upon.
Building these units is done through an intuitive 'module' system where you equip your mothership or any special builderships with the right gear to be able to build specific units.
Research is done through a research tree, no nonsense with managing 20 buildings or prerequisites for a specific unit.
Everything is surprisingly simple, yet the combat is quite deep.
The factions are slightly different, creating this familiar yet distinct slightly asymmetrical gameplay that allows players to easily try the other faction while still experiencing the capabilities of a different playstyle.
If you are just as bothered by 2d-gridlocked space RTS games as I am and like the clear approach this game has over others when it comes to gameplay, this is the game for you.

this game never gets old. the story's fun and interesting, and there's NEVER nothing to do, even when you complete everything. the weapons are fun just to use, click on something and watch it explode! the vehicles are unique, and have different abilities. for example the ptakojester is a massive cargoplane capable of fitting TEN full sized vehicles. you can go in the interior midflight and it will maintain altitude and speed, and you can open the door from the interior and while in the cockpit (plus it can land on water!) and a hroch (i think) is a boat capable of holding 2 cars. there are also seaplanes and sea helicopters. there is also a jet with heatseaking missiles, one with bombs, and more. there's a fleshed out upgrade system for vehicles, the wingsuit, (oh, by the way there's a wingsuit) the grappling hook, and tethers. the weapons are unique and perfect for different for different situations, so you have to pick what you're going to bring for each task. there's also a mechanic that allows you to spawn in vehicles for (almost) free. you unlock most vehicles by liberating bases, and you can then get them airdropped to your location. there are 2 catches though. 1: there is a cooldown time for each indivisual vehicle, but with upgrades, these wait times can be made smaller and eventually be completely removed. 2: you need beacons to call in airdrops, but that's not as bad as it sounds. beacons are common, spawning at gas stations, garages, and some enemy bases, so you'll pretty much always have a beacon on you. there are some issues, the first one being the frame rate. even with low settings, you might get low FPS, but it's managable. the second one being there are a couple of bugs. they won't break the game, and they won't kill you, but they can be annoying sometimes. other than that, the game never gets old, i highly recommend this if you have a powerful computer,  there are mods, but they seem to have been broken by a recent update, hopefully they will be back soon. if you're questioning whether or not you want to buy this, then watch youtube clips of it, there are lots of them.

WHAT IF YOU WERE "EL PRESIDENTE"?
I bought Tropico during 2013 Summer Sale and I only got around to playing it after playing several games ranging from action and racing to casual and stealth and I felt it was a good idea to play a city-builder game. So...
GAMEPLAY
TROPICO 3... is a fabulous and addicting game. It's all about being "El Presidente", managing an island banana republic and making it prosperous while embezzling some of the money for your Swiss bank account (which is non-crucial, it only serves for high score). You start every game by choosing your avatar, either pre-configured real ones like Che Guevara, Evita Peron and Voodoo Pizzaman or you can create your own. Then you start (always) with a banana republic which is in shambles and then you can do whatever with it by issuing edicts, constructing, pleasing different factions (like socially aware communists, hypocritical religious and more) and you rise through the difficulties and build a prosperous nation based on ore/coffee/rum/whatever exports... Or you pass a martial law and conscription edict and build a giant army... or♥♥♥♥♥♥off USA and make it invade you; the choices are many.
CHARM
Next, you have at first charming and humorous, but then repetitive Juanito who keeps Tropicans up to date on current issues, passed edicts and humorous event reports. The soundtrack is short but so sweet, you won't help but shimmy to the infectious salsa rhythm and graphics hold up pretty well (but it's a 2009 game, so it's kind of expected). The humor in this game is terrific and well though-out so you will definitely giggle at some of the event reports (like a llama assassinating El Presidente's favorite hat) and you will grow to curse at least one faction in this game. All of the mentioned elements make for a really freaking addicting game.
MODES
I first recommend playing the campaign mode, it is great to keep you occupied as you try to get through different goals and finish each island. The campaign mode definitely has some variety however even then, it will feel repetitive doing the same thing over and over again, just with a different end. The sandbox mode is great and there you can develop your island however you please and where you have your own ways of building a rich Carribean country.
ITERATION
Now, it seems that this game is simply a remake of Tropico 1 and while I feel that's a good thing for newcomers, it brings nothing new to the table if you played the earlier games. Also, after a while it feels repetitive doing the same thing over and over again, you will eventually grow sick of it as every scenario you play starts the same.
CONCLUSION
+ Highly addictive and gratifying
+ Salsa soundtrack
+ Great humour
+/- Remake of Tropico 1
- Brings nothing new
- Repetition

STALKER: Shadow of Chernobyl is a game based entirely on the gameplay provided, as well as it's difficulty that stems from it's mechanics, and the hazards laid throughout the zone. The design, be it in the environment seemingly crafted from real-life examples to great detail, or the monsters themselves, as well as the great balance of guns and their somewhat realistic portraits conveyed through the game, is simply undeniably good, throughout balance with fights and environmental situations that can't fail but to make me a bit paranoid and scared.
The game, itself, falls short with it's story, however. The backstory behind the main character is explained well as time goes on, but the story itself is nothing but fetch quests and favors where you are rebounded across the entire country just to find out whom Strelok is, whenever the most people have given you is nothing short of, "Oh, I know this other guy who might know him." There is not much motivation to do it after that, and overall, it starts to become tedious within the first few hours of the game as you start to realize that the quests seem silly, as they're nothing but jumbled messes of situations haphazardly thrown together because you're trying to find a man, and even then, that logic goes straight out the window sometimes, so you're left with, "Just do it, because hey, you want to do it!" It is a good mechanic for a free-roaming STALKER game, but not for a man with such an objective in mind, which doesn't even matter until it is pulled up again later on in the game.
Anomalies in this game aren't exactly clever, save for a few. The majority of them are simply you getting harmed and then having to use a med kit, which is not much variety between the two, save for that one just stands there, and one pulls you in. The anomalies that go well beyond this, like making you go straight to bleeding badly as soon as you step in them, are good, for they experiment with what they can do, but overall, they just seem a lot like random environmental hazards, which don't really change positions at all.
The gunplay is favorable, and, in the right setting, STALKER has monsters and situations that just plain get to you, that really make you shiver in fear. There are flaws in the game, such as stashes being completely devoid of anything until you get the information of the stash itself, but overall, the experience that it makes you go through, as well as the balanced difficulty and unsettling environments, as long as they last before they get bombarded by human enemies out of nowhere, truly make the game what it is.
Do I hate this game? Not at all. Despite what I have stated, I could play STALKER: Shadow of Chernobyl lots and lots, and still find out new things, which recreates that magical spark that made me love the game whenever I first started playing it.
The gameplay is done to such a degree that it actually goes with the very theme of STALKER itself, which completely makes it all the more meaningful once you do discover what it is.
What is it, you ask?
Well, that's an answer that you'll have to find for yourself. The Zone is full of mysteries, but let it be known that you are like everyone else, improving and trying to live just a little better. Maybe, through the situations you find yourself in, you'll find out what it all teaches us sooner or later.

Want to be an industry titan, producing oil, cigars and rum in mass quantity to make your city prosper? Or will you make the island a "paradise" and profit off tourists in hotels? The choice is yours.
Well, ish. The industry option MASSIVELY overpowers tourism in revenue, and also is better of when you focus on just one type of product. However, the game is still quite fun and the possibilites endless.
The events and occur in the campaign are interesting and add a twist to your gameplay, which by the way, is still themed as you being a dictator on an island. The said island has different interest groups, and some are more powerful than others. You may  wish to build a church over a factory if elections are close and the religious group is upset. Or maybe even an army base, lest you wish your own generals and soldiers turn on you.
The way you control these groups is up to you. Do you praise democracy and have free elections? Or do you declare martial law and shoot any protesters on sight? The choice is yours, Presidente.

Nostalgia prevents me from delcaring this my top game over HL2, but S.T.A.L.K.E.R. is brilliant. It's certainly highly flawed in some aspects (nothing that a few of the many avaliable mods can't fix), it manages to capture the eerie beauty and tantalizing allure of the mysterious and dangerous. Fusing horror, immersion, realism, gunplay, and atmosphere without any subtracting from another and without, sacrificing any of the 'fun' factor, as many overly-ambitious games do. It creates an expansive, ominous world, (rivaling that of Fallout) riddled with sprawling underground bunkers and tunnels and military and commercial complexes full of loot and danger. The gunplay is intense and real-feeling, as you have as much HP as most humans and take equal damage from weapons, leaving you only with the advantage of wits and strategy when going up against a well-equipped opponent, and the mutants are terrifying and strangely numerous. Creeping nervously through a dark subterranean laboratory and peeking around a corner to glimpse some strange, grotesque creature you've never seen before is never loses it's thrill, and is a perplexingly common occcurence, even after playing the game for some time. The game's faults (dismal ambient sounds, bugs, etc.) are more than tolerable given the game's many and unique strengths. All in all, fantastic game. 9.1/10

Papers, Please is a thought-provoking, emotionally impactful look at the gritty intersection of government and humanity. This game is a one of a kind experience I won't soon forget.

Papers Please is the perfect example of gameplay and idea, over graphics.  In this day and age, we are forcefed fantastic graphics over what normally turns out to be marginal gameplay.  This game may not win any awards in the graphic and sound department (Indie game title), but the gameplay is surprisingly eclectic.  Without spoling anything, you are solely responsible for the admission of people in to your glorious nation with communistic undertones.  What seems like a very simple idea, quickly becomes nerve-wracking as you balance the wishes of your government with the need to maintain your family.
The interface is functional, it does what it sets out to do.
This game claws at your personal ethics and viewpoints, and challenges you to do it efficiently.  The only reason I have not played more, is due to being snowed under and having limited game time.  I suggest you prove me wrong.
For an indie, this game is massive. Choices matter, your attention matters, details matter. Twenty different endings and morality. Simply amazing.
If you can get into games, then this is an experience you need to have. If you can't take games seriously, then this game sucks, but in my opinion, It's one of the best games I've ever played.

If you ask me what this game is about, I can't tell you. To describe it would not only give you the wrong impression, but it would be insulting to the game.
"Papers, Please" is an addictive masterpiece, encompassing hummor and morality, as well as mortality. As simplistic tasks become more and more complicated, taking longer to perform, and holding a more intense weight over the livelihood of you and your loved ones, our ideas of morality change. Between bribes, corruption, sabotage, and simple cold-heartedness, the game knows exactly how to get at you, as you race to the end, trying only to survive.
When I tried to explain the game's mechanics to my friends, they were put off by the concepts. In our minds, a paperpusher does not make a great game. Yet everyone whom I've demonstrated to, or let play have expressed their own interest, many of whom bought the game for themselves. So yes, I suggest this game to anyone who wishes to explore humanity at it's finest.

One of the best visual novel games to date, Grisaia no Kajitsu aka The Fruit of Grisaia was a very enjoyable playthrough, with many heartfelt moments and fantastically well written characters.
The story follows our main protagonist Yuuji Kazami, who has been admitted into a private school for students who can't function well in modern society due to the tragic events that happen to them when they were younger. Kazami quickly learns that he is the sixth student to have started to attend a school and that his other classmates are all of the opposite gender.
Yuuji's classmates consist of a cute little ball of energy named Makina Irisu, who has a noticable lisp in her voice when she speaks do to having a very small tongue. Makina is usually intimidated by people she just meant and usually hids behind her bestfriend/older sister figure Amane Suou.
Upon opening up to someone, Makina shows her more troublemaking side and loves to use the fact that she is small and adorable to get her way with just about anyone who she is comfortable with.
Makina's tramatic past has to deal with her rich family background that is just as amazingly well-written as it is sad. A mother who has abandoned her and screws around with other men.
Yuuji's next classmate is a fake-tsundere by the name of Michiru Matsushima. Michiru has conciously decided to act as the token tsundere archtype, although it is pretty easily to tell that it is forced. Michiru tries to empress others with her tsundere act, although most of the time she fails horribly due to the fact that she is a massive klutz, but at the same time she is very sweat and cares about her friends dearly.
Michiru trama is rooted in an accident that she was a victim of and she suffers from an identity crisis that has nothing to do with her fake-tsundere persona, but is so bad that she is almost suicidal.
The best girl is Sachi Komine, a girl with a passion for the maid lifestyle and an unhealthy obsession with helping others. Sachi is the first girl you will speak to upon entering the school as she is very suspicious of you being an intruder.
Sachi takes on the role from a class rep, who will take on any request no matter how ridiculous it may be. Sachi also has shown many times throughout your run to be someone who takes every way too seriously and has a serious weird catchphrase when someone has to explain something to her when she either has the wrong idea or just being weird.
Sachi loves being praised by others, mostly the main character and adores it when you pet her on the head. She also has a weird obsession with expecting you to do perverted things to her or the other girls and has a slight masochistic nature to her personality.
Sachi's trama deals with the fact that she is convinced that she was the cast for the people in her life disappearing and so she will do anything anyone tells her to in the hopes that she has to never again experience the pain that she went through as a child.
The next girl is Sakaki Yumiko, the daughter of the person who is currently funding the school that they all attend. Yumiko is at first very hostile towards the main male character and likes to keep her distance from other, preferring to spend most of the day in her room when not attending class.
Yumiko is a menace, always caring around a box cutter blade to threaten anyone who approaches her, due to her paranoia.
Much like Makina, Yumiko's issues have to deal with her family, being the daughter of a Wealthy businessman, who treats her like a pawn for him to use when he feels the need to and how her fathers cold personality affected her and her now dead mother.
Last but not least, we have Amane Suou, the big sister character who absolutely adores the main character, play the role of the horny big sister character with large breasts.

She quickly latches on to the main male lead, using her feminine charms and large assets to gain Yuuji's affection. she is very aggressive in the aspect of romance and is not afraid to fault her body to the point where even being naked in front of Yuuji does not embarrass her all that much.

she is an exceptional cook having been raised in the kitchen at her families restaurant and has a passion for driving since she got her license.

An excellent visual novel, this tells the story of a young man, Yuuji, with a military background who tries to reinvent himself at a "normal" school... and ends up at a small academy with five very broken girls.
The game starts out light-hearted and mysterious; clearly everyone has secrets--including the main character--but the group is insistent on them remaining secrets.  But as the player, you are given the choice to involve yourself with any one of the other students--at which points their secrets unfold in front of Yuuji's eyes, some of Yuuji's own past is revealed, and the game steadily takes a turn for the dramatic (and at times, tragic).  By playing through all of the endings, the player reveals a good portion of Yuuji's own tragic past as well.
It's a clever story, with fascinating characters, a wicked sense of humor... and ultimately, a satisfying conclusion (if the player makes the appropriate choices, that is).  I highly recommend this to anyone who likes visual novels.

Although I have the feeling that there are not too many space RTS games, and I feel like there are even less massively popular RTS games, Homeworld is to me that one space RTS game that stood the test of time.
Whereas many other attempts at space games usually result in big empty 2d grids on which you play in a fancy 3d arena Homeworld did one thing that many still do not do today: It played in true 3d. Now you could argue that it doesn't matter that much for actual gameplay, and perhaps you are right. But the sheer sense of 'space' and 'freedom' you have when you can tell ships to fly to any part of the map, no matter how high or low, gives it way more immersion than any '2d' grid-locked space RTS game ever could. The base game itself may have aged a bit, but some of the mods (PDS, Complex and many others) managed to spice it up in such a way that it was back up to par compared to many other space games. And now with this remastered edition it's still a treat to the eyes as well.
Unit variety is done through variations of ships in different classes, which beforementioned mods greatly expand upon.
Building these units is done through an intuitive 'module' system where you equip your mothership or any special builderships with the right gear to be able to build specific units.
Research is done through a research tree, no nonsense with managing 20 buildings or prerequisites for a specific unit.
Everything is surprisingly simple, yet the combat is quite deep.
The factions are slightly different, creating this familiar yet distinct slightly asymmetrical gameplay that allows players to easily try the other faction while still experiencing the capabilities of a different playstyle.
If you are just as bothered by 2d-gridlocked space RTS games as I am and like the clear approach this game has over others when it comes to gameplay, this is the game for you.

Just as the The Force Awakens is an attempt to rekindle the magic of the original Star Wars Trilogy, Alien: Isolation attempts to ressurect the best elements of the first Alien film... into video game form.
The good news is that Isolation is one of the scariest games I've ever played, recreating the same kind of insane tension that I had watching the original film for the first time. I can't even imagine how much worse (better?) it would be if I was playing with a VR headset.
The attention to detail in environmental design is amazing - the artists really went all out to make the items and locations look like late-70's futurism, and even the hacking mini-games have a spot-on retro aesthetic. Sometimes I found the sheer amount of little details to be a little distracting, but for the most part clever lighting, sound effects and level design balance out the distractions.
The audio work is probably the best I've ever experienced in a game, period. In particular, the alien's walking, crawling, and vocalization sounds give it a terrifying sense of
and threat. The various environmental sounds are subtle, suggestive and varied; again, just like in the original movie. The musical score is fantastic: it grounds itself in Jerry Goldsmith's movie score while still developing its own, intense style. While lip sync is sometimes an issue, the voice acting is pretty solid all around. The inclusion of original Alien cast members in some of the audio logs is a nice touch.
The plot is... well, pretty average. While there is an interesting backstory about the space station, the game sometimes feels like it's also a sort of "greatest hits" tour of the best moments of Alien reworked into a less compelling story.
There are an awful lot of moments where (mild spoilers)
Some of the missions felt arbitrary, almost like they were just created to extend the length of the game.
I had a hard time developing a real emotional connection to any of the new characters. They're not badly written, per se, just not particularly unique within the franchise. Still, they do the job, and are at least as decent as the characters in Dead Space.
I didn't really try the Survivor Mode challenges, but if you've gotten really good at the mechanics of the game, you might enjoy them.
The other downsides are occasional bugs, sections where it's not really obvious where to go next (often while being put under constrant threat), and a few useless items. For example: why would you ever need to use a flare once you get the headlamp? The item crafting system creates some items that are immediately useful and others that I didn't feel a need to use more than once in the whole game.
However, none of the downsides I've mentioned change the fact that I felt real terror playing this game, and real relief in escaping from the various in-game dangers. Also, despite my nit-picking, I have a huge amount of respect for the people who clearly spent an enormous amount of time making this game into a polished, atmospheric experience.

My favorite VN to date.
The story is very rich, well written and manages to make you care about the heroine, which is necessary in these kind of games. Memorable soundtrack that fits the atmosphere. The steam version lacks the H-scenes but they were few and far between and the VN never relied on them to be awesome which makes the steam version alright.
Content-wise, you can easilly get around 40-50 hours of gameplay by going through each of the 5 routes. The story is divided into the common route which will then either split into one girl's route or continue, then repeat until you are forced into the last girl's route. When Elder Scrolls Online was preparing to lauch, and during it's launch, I was skeptical. I never got it, but my friends got it day 1, and played the beta. They were dissapointed into oblivion, it wasn't what they were expecting. 2 years later, it was on sale, and I had money to blow.
So I picked this up for 10.00$ initally (No DLC, and I did play quite a bit of the free weekend before purchasing it). It changed monumentally from inital release, I immediatly bought it for my friends, and I got the first 4 DLC's (Gold edition) half off. It was more than worth it, and I'm going to play it for a long time to come.  Just to cover some of my more favorite changes:
Level scaling: used to do it like World of Warcraft, where areas decided levels; howver, they put a scaling system that affects everything.
Subscrition fees: Completely removed. No longer do you have to pay for a sub to play the game. You buy it, and it's yours to play.

Beyond just the changes, they do a good job with lore as well. Just like in Skyrim, there are books everywhere, with tons of story to them. You have all your races, along with the fact that you can basically go anywhere in the game, that's in the lore (excepting some of the places, but I'am almost certain they are going to add everything, and some of the most noted places are there anyway).
There's really only one important thing to note: Don't go into this game, when you get it, as it being Skyrim. It is not online skyrim. This is the elder scrolls online, and MMORPG. That means things like combat, and stats have change a fair bit. Other than that, I recommend the hell outta' this game. It's one of few games that can keep me up till 7:00 AM on a school night.

So it took me a really long time to get into this game.  I started out as an Alpha tester, then again as a Beta Tester.  And because of my experiences in Alpha and Beta, I just couldn't bring myself to buy it.  It was fun, but only sort of.  It was Elder Scrolls, but it wasn't.  I didn't like the way they locked you to specific power classes and sets instead of being able to build your own thing. But given that it has PvP I understood it because they have to balance the classes for PvP.
Fast forward to a few months ago.  Had a friend who got hooked on it again and talked me into picking it up.  Add to the fact that I managed to work the discounts and coupons to get the game for $6.00 I really decided what the heck, why not?
I logged in, created a toon and got to it.  The initial starting level in the jail was my first sight...I thought "Ah, the same as in Beta...can't say much will be different."  Then I started playing.  The core storyline was pretty much the same, but many of the mechanics had a more Elder Scrolls feel to it.  More items to loot and satisfy my kleptomania, as well as my hoarding that is rampant in Elder Scrolls games for me.  I didn't remember being able to loot like this....
Made it to the starter island....Even more changes.  Some of the missions I remembered, some I didn't.  And more stuff that is Elder Scrolls oriented instead of just another MMO rubber-stamp.
What cinched it for me is the Thieves Guild missions.  I always play a Breton battle-mage type.  Double swords, fire attacks, and a bow for range.  Then my first guild I work for is the Thieves guild.  I like the bonuses and weapons/armor sets that come with doing those missions first before I tackle any others.  ESO lets me play exactly like that.
Are there grindy parts?  Yes.  It is an MMO so there are plenty of go here and kill something quests, but I have yet to come across one that makes me hate it.  Even the simpler go kill quests are still fun.
Are there public dungeons that will make you hate your fellow player?  Sorta...It's really not as bad as other MMO's and the community is a lot nicer than some places I've been.
The economy is very player driven to the point that there are zero npc markets.  You want a market, you have to join a trade guild.  They allow you to join up to 5 guilds at once which is really nice.  Join a couple of trade guilds and you will find a pretty wide varity of marketplace stuff within the guild, and even may find a guild that will help you out with your skills and crafting.
I like the fact that some of the best armor and weapons in the game are player made.  Honestly having the very best equipment be mob dropped and player made gear is never as good just kills crafting in any MMO for me.  What's the point of busting my butt to make an awesome elite sword that no one will ever buy from me because mob boss so-and-so drops something better after only a 1 hour grind?
The other advantage to this system of trade is I really don't see a lot of gold-spammers in chat.  That is really nice.
Pros:
Graphics are really pretty, and very Elder Scrolls.
Crafting system is fun.
Theft system is REALLY fun.
Missions are all voice acted and not to grindy.
Stealth system can be worked around sometimes by waiting till someone else screws up and distracts the guards. :-D
Supports hoarding.
Cons:
Open dungeons still suffer the same loot-♥♥♥♥♥ and enemy camping that is in any MMO open dungeon.
The level grind is pretty slow.  It takes a while to level up.
Item store can be a bit pricy.
Access to the craft bag requires paid membership. (Honestly worth it though)
Overall I would give this game a solid 8/10.

this game never gets old. the story's fun and interesting, and there's NEVER nothing to do, even when you complete everything. the weapons are fun just to use, click on something and watch it explode! the vehicles are unique, and have different abilities. for example the ptakojester is a massive cargoplane capable of fitting TEN full sized vehicles. you can go in the interior midflight and it will maintain altitude and speed, and you can open the door from the interior and while in the cockpit (plus it can land on water!) and a hroch (i think) is a boat capable of holding 2 cars. there are also seaplanes and sea helicopters. there is also a jet with heatseaking missiles, one with bombs, and more. there's a fleshed out upgrade system for vehicles, the wingsuit, (oh, by the way there's a wingsuit) the grappling hook, and tethers. the weapons are unique and perfect for different for different situations, so you have to pick what you're going to bring for each task. there's also a mechanic that allows you to spawn in vehicles for (almost) free. you unlock most vehicles by liberating bases, and you can then get them airdropped to your location. there are 2 catches though. 1: there is a cooldown time for each indivisual vehicle, but with upgrades, these wait times can be made smaller and eventually be completely removed. 2: you need beacons to call in airdrops, but that's not as bad as it sounds. beacons are common, spawning at gas stations, garages, and some enemy bases, so you'll pretty much always have a beacon on you. there are some issues, the first one being the frame rate. even with low settings, you might get low FPS, but it's managable. the second one being there are a couple of bugs. they won't break the game, and they won't kill you, but they can be annoying sometimes. other than that, the game never gets old, i highly recommend this if you have a powerful computer,  there are mods, but they seem to have been broken by a recent update, hopefully they will be back soon. if you're questioning whether or not you want to buy this, then watch youtube clips of it, there are lots of them.

Definitely recommended for first-person lovers.
Movement of the players are very good - when I compare it with Assassin's Creed games, this game is definitely much smoother when it comes to player-movement. You climb the walls you want, and you use parkour to get over obstacles.
Graphics are awesome - the lightning and the details... All of them were good. However, you can't really notice it if you use the power "Dark Vision" often - since it turns the whole world yellow - covering all the aesthetics of the game.

The(My) Cons - The bugs. Throughout the game, I encountered some bugs. I got stuck inside water, a guard went through a wall and got stuck inside, unconscious bodies died by themselves while they were placed in a safe place(This almost ruined my gaming experience since I was going through a pacifist playthrough), and allies such as Megan dying with no particular reason(During the game, she just died. In conclusion:
Visuals: Great
Optimization: Good
Story: Good - but disappointing when compared to the original game.
Sound: Awesome
Free-Roam Elements: Great
Story Choices: Good - They do matter - somewhat.
Combat Choices: Spectacular! Its always upto you how to engage a mission.
Combat: Fantastic
A.I. : Good
The Verdict: 9/10

Genie was the 2nd in the Drizzlepath series and it should be noted it was a huge step up. The first Drizzlepath used the CryEngine and it was marred by optimisation errors. Graphics options were almost completely missing and it wasn't always clear where we needed to go.
For its sequel, Genie, the developer picked the Unreal Engine. In terms of graphics the world created by this engine is just as beautiful, however, unlike its predecessor Genie is now greatly optimised and has a smooth performance throughout. A lot of options are available to tweak its graphics and some reviews state that a 4K resolution is also possible - this is good for screenshot aficionados like myself.
Since this is a walking sim we do not encounter any enemies and the objective here is to reach our goal while the game's beautiful scenery and relaxing music all help with the immersion. Our protagonist, Lula, does the narration as she tries to reach the Mountain of Fire in search of the Genie. Normally, walking sims are relatively short so I was happy to see that early on we have the option to pick from two paths - they will change the locales, the atmosphere and, eventually, how Lula's journey ends.
- longer than usual: with the availability of two paths we have two different experience and two endings
- graphics & soundtrack: the music in the main menu is already captivating; the landscapes give us the opportunity to take screenshots
- sprinting: while walking can be toggled the option for a constant sprint would have been nice. Occasionally, sprinting is turned on but at key areas it is deliberately taken away.
- not much interaction: this is not really a weakness since walking sims usually do not require you to interact with objects of the world. However, in Genie we can do this a couple of times so it would have been nice to see more such events.
Genie is definitely an improvement following its predecessor. In fact, of all the currently available 3 episodes I have found this the best. This is a highly recommended walking sim; I recommend that you check Mr Bodur's library of games as they are of similar nature.

Drizzlepath, like it's predecessor, is a walking simulator where you walk along a path. The story and some poetry are drizzled along the path as well as some art. The story as well as some of the poetry is narrated by a fresh and young but soothing voice, this time around however it is fully subtitled. The music is very nice and quite divers, it facilitates a sense of relaxation. The difference with the previous game is that there are two paths to chose from and differ quite reasonably in tolerability.
The problem with this game is that the content is spread very thin as you are supposed to enjoy the environment along the way. Except the scenery, props and textures become repetitive very soon, this isn't at all helped by the fact that the walking speed is very, very slow...
I will reccomend this game with caution as the art, poetry and music can be appreciated, but the game does overstay it's welcome due to them being stretched far and few between. So I will conclude with a warning:
WARNING: This game can only be appreciated by true walking simulator fans who have enough patience.

Know what you are getting.
>Players do not need to follow the fixed routes
This is largley false at this point. A few years ago they described this game as a very open ended game, this has diminished more and more as the development went on. Id still reccomend this game.
There are more linear games out there, but you are going to follow through a questline (one of two at the time of this writing, they merge togeather around level 80-100ish, you can go back and do the other though), and end up doing daily dungeon and mission runs. You are not going to be grouping up and grinding in a comfy spot like you did in RO or any older mmo. It may be possible at the higher levels, but thats up in the air at this point, the disparity between daily exp and actual mob kill exp is massive.
Its still cute, has a nice soundtrack, and is not a bad game, its just not really the spiritual successor to anything. Its good for a modern mmo.
>f2p
As far as cash shop, a lot is cosmetic, but there is what some might call slight pay2win, its far far less (at this point) than any of the cash grab games out there and i am not myself anticipating needing to pay for any of that, but you are going to want a token.
"Token" is the vip/subscription service. It gives you more dungeon runs, a slight exp boost to all kills, and allows you to use the auction house better (its very restrictive with out token), as well as a few slight buffs that are not all that big a deal. Its mainly for the extra dungeon runs and better auction house use. This works with an EVE PLEX type system (or RO2s VIP for that matter) where you can sell token to other players for in game money. I have no reason to expect that higher level players shouldnt be able to afford buying token in this way, and i think its ideal for a game like this to be primarilly driven by this sort of 'soft subscription' instead of gimmicky scams like gatcha boxes.
I would reccomend buying either the $50 or $30 early access pack if you intend to ever spend money on this game. Its not for the exclusive stuff which you may or may not want, but straight up the TP+token alone is worth more than the price, assuming we follow general korean pricing conventions.
>PVP
Not really balanced at this point, not really worth making a dedicated character for following the unbalanced meta either.
>GVG
Not a write off yet, not really fleshed out yet. Again im going to stress, this is not really a successor to RO in any way but visual style. Dont be expecting WOE.
To summarize: Its not a bad game, its cute, dont get your hopes up and they cant be dashed.

Poor.  Drizzlepath: Genie is a walking simulator.  It's sticks to this description fiercely.  As you will walk, and walk, and walk.  The problem is, the gameplay, without anything interesting going on, is fairly awful.  It was just not fun.  There is next to zero interaction which is hardly surprising for a walking simulator, so you need the story to support the game entirely.  This is where it fails.  The poor, monotonous voiceover is hard to listen to, and there's a couple of botched lines where the intonation and flow of the speech is completely out of synch with what the actual dialogue is trying to say.  I did have subtitles on which mercifully allowed me to speed read on and tune the narrator out, but being able to read just highlighted how bad the text is.  It is not a good story, and the ending twist is beyond ridiculous.  Half of the time the narration is overly flowery, non-sensible ravings about mystical beings and the rest is straight forward, to the point railings against religion and faith.
Thankfully, and this was key to me actually finishing the game, there is an autowalk feature which I turned on about two thirds of the way through which allowed me to tune out and do other things and just occasionally steer my character up and down the never ending hills.  If you must play I recommend you do not skip over the tutorial messages at the start which tell you about this feature.
Graphically, some of the vistas you encounter are fairly decent.  But the graphics as a whole are seriously underwhelming.  Coupled with the fact that nothing ever really happens.  The trailer has pretty much all the interesting parts.  The rest of the time it's just you, trees, hill, the rain, and that godawful narration.  Occasionally you dip into a cave.  The nature based walking simulator equivalent of the FPS sewer levels.
Also, supposedly there is a second path you can take which the game informs you of at the end.  I will not be trying it.  For those interested, I took the blue path.  Hopefully for you the red path is better.  Or at the very least shorter.

In my ongoing effort to play through some of the games I have owned for quite a while, I thought it high time I got back to Drizzlepath: Genie, which I had started just after release but never quite made it back to. Today, I sat down and played through both of the branching paths along with the nice bonus section provided by Tonguç Bodur as a thank you of sorts to those who actually finished the entire game. So, how was Drizzlepath: Genie?
Ultimately, in my opinion, Drizzlepath: Genie is about accepting your mortality and embracing life as opposed to living for your eventual death. I completely agree with the philosophical ideas presented in this game. Most people forget to live their lives, so consumed are they by religion, acquisition of wealth, and so on. Generally, it takes a traumatic event for people to really appreciate life.
For me, the prose was a little much, but the ideology was spot on, and I think it takes a brave soul to confront those ideas head on. Overall I quite enjoyed the story as it was presented in Drizzlepath: Genie, along with the twist at the end of each story path.
8 out of 10
This is a true walking simulator in every sense of the genre. In Drizzlepath: Genie, the choices you make are basically just which path you choose and whether you care to explore off path or not. There are a couple minor platforming sections and a couple simple puzzles, but overall, this game doesn't stray very far from the path, so to speak, and seeks to provide an honest exploration of the world while conveying the story. At the very beginning, the game explains why there is no running, but despite that, there is both a one click jogging feature as well as auto walk, which was a surprisingly awesome addition. You can choose to basically just kick back and steer Lula as she wanders about.
There are a couple features related to screenshots which are a recognition of the fact that people like to wander about in walking simulators trying to find that perfect capture. As such, a filter is available as is the ability to pan out pretty much as far as you might like. These two features led to my abusing the F12 button lol. I believe I took something like 510 screenshots.
8 out of 10
Drizzlepath: Genie is a stunning looking game. Use of the Unreal Engine has really been elevated over the years and Tonguç is a practiced hand. There is a reason why I took more than 500 screenshots. The game is simply that amazing. There is also a variety of geographical areas, from forest to almost swamp areas to mountains to underground cavern systems, and plenty in between. It's really everything you could hope for and more.
9.5 out of 10
The audio tracks are mostly comprised of mood setting but gentle background orchestrations. There are some ambient noises, most notably when the dragon is near the path (that's right, there is a dragon). It all sounds very nice. I will note however that in the bonus unlockable section, the music switches to metal riffs which I found quite enjoyable and a little surprising.
In the first Drizzlepath, I thought the voice actor sounded amazing, but I found it difficult to understand what she was saying due to a very heavy accent. In Drizzlepath: Genie, I found the voice acting to be completely clear and in fact, it seemed the voice actor took pains to enunciate at times. However, her delivery for all of the blue path and a fair amount of the red path felt forced and very much as if she was reading the script rather than feeling it. I wish the acting had conveyed more emotion than it did.
6 out of 10
All told, Drizzlepath: Genie was an excellent game and an excellent follow up to the original Drizzlepath. There were some things I enjoyed more with the original, but this installment was excellent nonetheless. One further note: My total playtime was right at 5 hours completing both story paths and enjoying the bonus section as well.

Perhaps you're reading this review because you played the first Drizzlepath and would like to evaluate the sequel.
If you expect them to be remotely similar, then you will be disappointed; the only similarity the two share is horribly forced voiceover and disjointed, pseudomystical narration. But I hope you're not trying to play this game for its narrative quality. If you played its predecessor, you know not to expect. You're expecting a gorgeous walking simulator with refined graphics and intuitive controls and logical design.
Again, you will be disappointed.
The graphics, even on maximum settings, appear so overcooked that you would be better off buying Morrowind (the original). Really you would, because not only does it have equivocable graphics; it has actual gameplay, intuitive controls, voice ACTING, an appreciable narrative, and Player Models (which were very impressively present in the first Drizzlepath, but in Genie, you are an immaterial set of eyes).

A real treat for any "Alien" fan. And I mean "Alien." With no "s" at the end.
The game takes place between original Alien and its sequel. You play as Amanda Ripley, a daughter of Ellen Ripley who seeks answers regarding her mother's fate.
A:I biggest strength is its faithfulness to the source material. The Alien is done wonderfully, both visually and gameplay wise. It is a deadly and unpredictable beast, which will kill anyone in sight. You have no way of killing it but later in the game you do flamethrower which you can use to repel it for a moment. Strangely, it makes the game more stressful, as you need to manage your fuel carefully. The AI of Alien is great, making him fairly intelligent. He doesn't follow strict patrol patterns which makes evading him quite thrilling. That is quite impressing as it is Creative Assembly game who has established reputation of writing horrible AI.
The environments look fantastic. The original soundtrack by Jerry Goldsmith is back and it is tastefully expanded for the needs of the game. The new stuff added to the lore (mostly the addition of Wayland-Yutani's poor competitor Seegston Corp.) is really good and fitting. Overall, finally the game Alien deserved to get.
If I have any complaints it is the writing and the characters. It is not bad, but it is quite forgettable. People you meet are Alien Fodder and are not developed enough for you to care. Also while the 1st half of the game is brilliant it gets less interesting later on. Final two missions try to recreate the frantic finale of the film and to some extend it succeeds but as you need to switch from the heavily established by that point stealth focused gameplay to running&flamethrowing it becomes frustrating rather than tense.

The crafting system is BEAUTIFUL, requiring only raw materials; even the most complicated buildings only need a few copper and iron plates in your inventory at once. (It creates everything you need out of raw material, and those materials make up the thing you want.)
The art style is akin to Dungeon Keeper and other mid-90s management games, which I was a fan of.
The aliens on the planet provide a constant threat launching surprise attacks at you every so often encouraging you to do something when everything else is covered by automation.
And the best part about all this is, it's only in Early Access.
TL;DR I have not gotten very far into the game, but I can easily say this is one of my all-time favorite games.

Overall, I'd say this game is pretty decent. There are many pros and cons, of which I will mention further along in my review.
What I find the game does right would have to be level design and combat. When it comes down to level design, the game presents many intricately designed places to explore, be they gang hangouts or houses infested with flies.
Combat is satisfying for a certain period of time, but it only goes so far before it becomes repetitive and easy. There are many instances where all I would have to do when I was surrounded by guards was continuously block and strike. What makes combat enjoyable are instead the kill animations, which are satisfying to watch, and the number of ways in which an individual can eliminate their foes (i.e. using mines). Point being, combat isn't challenging, though it's interesting to watch.
Stealth is only difficult in this game if one chooses to avoid killing/knocking anyone out unless absolutely necessary, which can make the game long and boring.
The world is definitely unique, though quite the same as that of the first installment (putting aside the obvious change of setting). Whatever aura of mystery the previous game emitted has practically vanished in Dishonored 2. There have, however, been new additions to the lore of the game, for better or for worse.
The plot is underwhelming, although plot has never been the strongsuit of the Dishonored series.
Characters are mostly bland and one-dimensional. Meagan Foster is one of the only characters I actually developped a liking to. Sokolov wasn't quite the same character he was in the first game, time difference aside. He had nostalgia going for him, but not much else asides from that. Everyone else is pretty flat and predictable except maybe for Jindosh, though his character wasn't explored well enough.
Chaos is noticeable, albeit lack the same effect it did in the first installment of the series.
Overall, I'd give the game a solid 7/10. If it ever goes on sale, buy it.

Solid graphics,
solid sound (albeit some random guard phrases come up very frequently),
solid, if predictable, storyline,
solid, albeit easy, gameplay.
Overall,  a quite fine game worth it's price, especially because you get enough motivation, both story and mechanically, to play the game through twice.
(I recommend doing the first playthrough on reckless straight-forward murder, and the second as a stealthy nonlethal run. Latter is more challenging and provides more lore and story, and I feel like doing it the otherway round would bore you with being a step down on the difficulty (even if you increase said difficulty), and as well unsatisfying on the story side.)
One could potentially squeeze in a third replay on the highest difficulty with the power disabled option (and do NOT select that on your first playthrough. Powers area core of the gameplay and without them you'll play hard++ mode) for the maximum challenge, or go spend time clearing every single loot drop of the maps for the 100%, but that's not my personal taste.
One thing that needs to be noted, and negatively so, is that this game is not a true Stealth Action RPG, or even a 'challenging' Action RPG, but more or less a Superpowered Protagonist go mess up the world style game. Keep in mind every level is designed in such a way that you can clear it with no detection, no kill, WITHOUT any powers. This means, most of the time, I was entirely fine just sneaking/stabbing my way through the levels whilst only using a sight (for collectibles and spotting enemies through walls) and a movement power. At rare occasions I used a different, more active power to save time / watch the hilarious effect, but never did I run into a real 'this is difficult, I can only get past by using powers' situation.
This is a weakness Dishonored 2 shares with it's prequel, but in the end it still makes for fun and casual gameplay.
Summa summarum, it's not the masterpiece of games, certainly not the best Stealth Action RPG, but still worth it's money (double so if you get in on sale, as I did) and, most importantly, fun to play.
